# On the Exact Anatomy of Bread or Wheat.

->B 4<-

so also we shall find bread to be divided into its two-fold species, namely the spiritual and the earthly. Earthly bread was produced in the first creation, and has been continued through multiplication in this vegetable grain even unto this day; but that celestial bread proceeds from God, in whose power it always remains to dispose of it as it pleases Him, as we shall declare in the following chapter. And indeed, it appears by many manifest arguments that God has infused no small virtue of His own splendor into the nature of this lower bread. Whence it is so highly esteemed, and held in such great value among all nations of the world, that even gold itself is not held in such high price by man; for although it is sold in greater quantity and weight than gold, gems, and precious stones, it is nevertheless observed to far excel them in both price and utility: first, because it abundantly nourishes and refreshes the tabernacle of the human soul <note>The author uses "tabernacle" to refer to the physical body as a temporary dwelling for the soul.</note>, whereas the precious office of gold and gems is only to adorn it and make it splendid on the outside; and also because it is capable of multiplying itself unto infinity, which gold or gems cannot provide, unless it be the gold of God and the mystical gems of the Magi <note>A reference to alchemical or esoteric traditions regarding "living" gold.</note>. And therefore it is much more precious in the eyes of God and men than either gold or the most precious and rarest stones of princes. For this reason, therefore, it was not said in *Numbers 15:19*: "Of the riches of that land you shall partake," but "of the bread of that land you shall eat," proving by this very fact that bread is the highest good and the price required for the life and sustenance of man. This the Psalmist also manifests to us in *Psalm 104:15* <note>Original cites Psalm 103:15 following a different numbering system.</note> in these words: *Bread strengthens and supports the heart of man, as that wine makes it glad.* Furthermore, we find there to be so close an affinity between earthly or material bread and the spiritual bread that descended from heaven, that if we look rightly and deeply into this lower bread, it would indeed be a matter of no great difficulty to behold and contemplate the images and shadows of the mysteries contained in that more sublime bread. And for the sake of this matter, we can observe in the Holy Scripture itself how effective a comparison has been established between these two, as if one were joined with the other by a certain secret and essential connection; whence the royal Psalmist, in *Psalm 104*, ingenuously confesses that Bread is brought forth from the earth by the benefit of God. So also in *St. Matthew* we find in *26:26*: *He blessed the bread and broke it, and gave it to his disciples, and said, take and eat, this is my body:* from which it appears how great an excellence there is in this earthly bread, since Christ Himself compares His own body with it—a discourse surely of such consequence that it has effectively set the entire Christian world on fire concerning this doubt, namely: whether the consecrated and sanctified bread is the real body of Christ or not? So also we find in *Luke 24:30*: *And it happened while he sat at table with them, he took bread, and blessed and broke it, and handed it to them, and their eyes were opened, and they knew him.*

This miracle our Savior Christ manifested in bread after His resurrection, from which we may evidently recognize that there is an admirable correspondence situated between this earthly creature and the celestial Creator. We read also how many miracles Christ performed concerning this subject on the mountain, where He satisfied four thousand men with seven loaves, a great abundance of remains and fragments being left over, *Matthew 15*. And in another place, five thousand hungry men worn out by lack of food were sustained by only five loaves, not counting the baskets of fragments that remained, *Matthew 16*. Furthermore, the world cannot deny the blessings which God imparts to the grain of wheat every year, which supplies the people abundantly in its season, as it is their life and the sustenance by which they live. For which reason King David in *Psalm 53:5* shows how detestable and barbarous it is to eat bread without a humble invocation of the most high Name, and due thanksgiving for such great beneficence, deeming that man impious who devours bread without grace preceding it. And it was held as a vice and transgression by the Pharisees and Scribes to eat bread with unwashed hands, for they exhibited such reverence to this principal nourishment, *Matthew 15:2*. Does not Jehovah, when He is about to punish the wicked, threaten them with a lack of bread? *He broke the staff of bread, and brought famine into the land,* says the Psalmist, *105:16*. How many commands and statutes were divinely ordained for the Israelite people concerning this kind of nourishment—namely, leavened and unleavened bread—let him who has read Exodus and Leviticus judge and determine? For in one place it is said of it: *You shall eat nothing leavened on that day on which you went out of Egypt.* *Exodus 13:3, 7.* By these things, therefore, we can perceive how precious this earthly bread is in the eyes of the Creator, and how mystically it is connected to His secret will. Nor can we deny that it draws its life, multiplication, and consequently its preservative virtue from the secret workshops <note>original: "ergasteriis"</note> and treasuries of Jehovah Himself, since the dew and the rains, which are the true causes of the fertility of this royal grain, are established in the hand of our God Jehovah; who preserves them in His secret treasures, as if in a storehouse, either to impart them to the earth or to deny them according to His pleasure—doubtless so that by such retention and denial, wheat may be denied to the wicked living on earth, whereas conversely, by the sending forth and pouring out in due time, God grants it and supplies it abundantly to the pious and to men pleasing to God, as the sacred histories teach us in many places. Furthermore, we find not only that the offering of wheat was pleasing to God (as we hinted above), but we also read that bread was consecrated to Him in place of the principal offering: for thus we gather from *Leviticus 23:17* that two loaves are to be offered to Jehovah. And *Job 28:5* seems to assert that a certain bread comes forth from the earth, and that which is under it is turned into something like fire: what this bread and the earth from which it emerges may mean in mystical theology, I leave to be explained by those far deeper and more learned than myself. To me, indeed, it is very easy to bring forth to you testimonies of even greater importance attesting to the mysteries of this most noble vegetable; both to explain its sanctity, which is verified by that offense and sacrilege committed by the Prophet David in the taking and eating of the consecrated bread, as well as many other examples of a higher nature: but I must fear lest...

## CHAPTER VIII.
### Concerning the heavenly or spiritual bread, with its infinite mysteries and effects.

Just as earthly grain is reckoned to exist among us, so also is heavenly grain given; and consequently, it follows that in a similar respect, earthly bread holds a relationship to that heavenly bread. What this heavenly grain or spiritual bread truly is, the prophet David describes most excellently for us in Psalm 78:24: *He rained down Manna upon them to eat, and gave them the grain of heaven, so that every man ate the bread of the mighty* <note>original: "panem robustissimum," often translated as "angels' food" or "bread of the strong."</note>. And this same thing is confirmed by Moses in these words, Exodus 16:5, 9, 14: *Manna, the bread from heaven, etc.* What this manna was, whence it came, and by what discrepancy it differs from wheat or earthly bread, the same supreme Prophet sufficiently teaches us in these very words: *He afflicted you, and made you to hunger, but fed you with Manna, which you did not know, nor did your fathers know, that he might make known to you that man lives not by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of Jehovah.* Deuteronomy 8:3. Now it is established that nothing proceeds from the mouth of Jehovah except His word alone, and therefore at the first glance we can discern how excellent a thing this heavenly bread is, since it proceeds from the very spirit of God, and is as if it were His very word, which nourishes both corporally and spiritually. And hence it is that the wise man says in Wisdom 16:26: *The natures of fruits do not nourish man, but the word of God preserves them;* from which it clearly appears that this bread proceeds from the very word of God, which is also confirmed in the following passage, Exodus 16:5, 14, 16, 17: *Bread is rained from heaven called Manna; This is that bread which Jehovah gives you to eat. This is the word which Jehovah commanded: gather of it.* This same was that bread of angels of which Solomon speaks in Wisdom 16:20, saying: *You nourished your people with the food of angels, and you provided for them bread prepared from heaven without labor, having in itself every delight, and the sweetness of every taste;* whence it appears first, that this heavenly bread was ordained by God to be the food of angels, and then also that it was a most delicate nourishment, and most pleasing to the taste and palate. To finish in a few words, this bread hidden under the type of Manna sent from heaven contains within itself a greater mystery (as I believe) than can be explained in words by the greater part of men. And although I freely confess that I have not yet fully progressed in the knowledge of such arduous and mystical food, nevertheless I dare to affirm that the sole vow and desire of my soul is to know as much of it as anyone who knows the most; for my internal spirit, as well as that sharpest stimulus of the mind implanted in man by God and his own nature, urges and impels me toward such blessed contemplations—a mind which continually strives to elevate itself to the highest contemplation of that happiness and blessedness where unity dwells. My mind has taught me, teaches me, and will teach me (God favoring) the way to the palace of blessedness, to the center of creatures, to the light of the world. *What? Does not the Wisdom of Solomon teach us the same, namely that it is a pleasure for wisdom to be among and dwell with the sons of men,* Proverbs 8. Was she not sent from the bright heaven itself upon the earth, so that she might remain and cooperate with man for this end: that he might learn and know what is acceptable to God? Wisdom 10. And for this cause God himself said to Job 38:36: *Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? or who has given understanding to the heart?* From this, therefore, it clearly appears that God infused wisdom into man from above, and that wisdom is a bright emanation proceeding immediately from the Majesty of the eternal God, Wisdom 8. Therefore, let no one think it a matter of presumption or ambition to strive, as much as possible, to climb to the true knowledge of divine mysteries, since by divine grace we have tasted from the bright fountains of eternal wisdom, which by their benefit lead and accompany us even to the very throne of Jehovah himself, so that with a joyful and eager soul we may contemplate and behold glory through the spirit. But what shall I say? This gross and obscure body (a blind spring of darkness) veils and covers our captive spirits so that we can only with difficulty discern those things which are set before our bodily eyes, and much less the things enclosed in the spiritual heaven. Did not the wise man testify that he felt the same in express words when he said in Wisdom 9:15: *The body subject to corruption weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling depresses the mind full of many cares? And we hardly guess the things that are on earth, and we find with labor the things that are at hand, but who shall search out the things that are in the heavens? and who has known the counsel of God? unless God has given wisdom, and sent his holy spirit from the highest places, thus the paths of those who dwell on earth were corrected, and men were taught the things that please God.* It is therefore the flesh which draws the spirit away from the high contemplations of heavenly things, and not the will of God, who liberally rains down his wisdom upon us to lead and direct us to himself. But to return to our subject, which is the spiritual manna or heavenly bread, it is very easily gathered how sublime and mystical that nourishment is from various citations of the holy Bible. And to begin from the speech of our Savior himself in John 6:32: *It was not Moses, he says, who gave the true bread from heaven, for the true bread is he who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world. They said therefore to him, Lord, always give us this bread; but Jesus said, I am the bread of life; he who comes to me shall not hunger...*

I know not what to say of that miraculous bread which the Angel offered to Elijah during the second visitation, of which it is written in 1 Kings 19:6: *That the cake baked on the coals and the vessel of water strengthened Elijah, by means of which food—that is, in the strength thereof—he walked forty days and forty nights.* That nourishment, beyond all doubt, was of the same nature as that heavenly manna by which Moses was nourished when he stayed for forty days and as many nights on Mount Sinai: just as our Savior Christ, when tempted by the tempter, seemed in some way to imply by these very words (having also been sustained in the same manner in the desert for forty days and nights): *Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word proceeding from the mouth of God* (Matthew 4). What then was this precious nourishment? Did it not bear the true type of Christ, or Christ the type of it? Was this not that spiritual rock which followed the Israelites in the desert, by whose protection they were fed? And was not Christ himself that spiritual rock? Let us hear the doctrine of Saint Paul on this matter in 1 Corinthians 10:1: *Brothers, I would not have you ignorant that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized by Moses in this cloud and in this sea, and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from that spiritual rock which followed them, and the rock was Christ, etc.* Wherefore it is evident that Christ (who was before every beginning) was that spiritual rock, and this rock was the spiritual food and drink which feeds both body and soul, by which both the internal and external man is regenerated and called back into life. What then? Is this not that heavenly and hidden Manna which shall be given to him who overcomes? (John 2:17). This, I say—this same bread is without any doubt the fruit of that tree of life planted in the midst of the paradise of God, promised to him who shall overcome (John 2:7), which brings with it that white stone in which a new name is engraved, known to no one, saving him who receives it (John 2:17). Does not our Savior acknowledge this same thing when he says, *I am the true bread of life, the true rock,* and the cornerstone, which St. Paul calls the *spiritual rock which fed the Israelites* (as was just said). Indeed, this is that unique rock, that true hollowed stone, I say, fallen from heaven, which Jacob recognized to be the gate of heaven and the house of God (Genesis 28). Since, therefore, Christ is perfect wisdom in whom, according to the wise man in Wisdom 7:22, *the spirit of understanding resides, which (I say) is holy and only-begotten, manifold, subtle, mobile, clear, undefiled, open, free from deceit and harm, loving the good, sharp, which cannot be hindered, doing good, lovable, constant, faithful, without care, having all power, circumspect in all things, permeating all intellectual, pure, and subtle spirits; since it is more agile than all things, and for this reason penetrates all things because of its purity (for it is the true spirit of the power of God, and a true influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty, and therefore can be contaminated by nothing, inasmuch as it is the splendor of eternal light, the unpolluted mirror of divine majesty, and the image of his goodness; which, though it be one, can yet effect all things, and remaining steadfast in itself, yet renews all things, and having regard for the distinction of ages, enters into all holy souls and makes them friends of God and of the prophets).* This is, I say, that true gem of the world, the spiritual rock, the true manna falling from heaven, which sustains the entire world both spiritually and corporally, which is one with Christ. This is the light and life of men according to St. John, chapter 1. And this, finally, is that universal spirit which gives continuous being and essence to earthly wheat, without which no one can live, since life is virtue, and all virtue proceeds from the spirit of Jehovah; for so we are taught by the psalmist David in Psalm 33:6: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the spirit from his mouth, all their virtue.* Nor has this holy spirit deserted the world, as some profanely imagine, who relegate it to the heaven of the greater world <note>The "macrocosm" or outer universe</note>, since the effects of the world, the multiplication of things, and the constant renewal of creatures after corruption seem to testify that it is even now as powerful in its operation as it ever was. But what need is there for words, when Solomon himself is a witness of this thing, saying in Wisdom 1: *The spirit of the Lord fills the orb of the earth; and conversely it is said, the heavens and the earth are full of the glory of God.* And Isaiah chapter 6 teaches us that God fills heaven and earth; so also we read in Jeremiah chapter 23: *That heaven is the seat of God, but the earth is his footstool,* all of which persuade us that God is even now as much in all things as he is above all things—namely in you, in me, and in any thing whatever, at any time and place, as much in this instant of time as in the beginning, according to that saying of the wise man: *God is the center of every thing, whose circumference is nowhere; as if he were to say, the Spirit of God is uniquely within and without all things, and consequently incomprehensible.* Whence it is clear, according to Solomon's saying, that this same true wisdom takes pleasure in dwelling among men as much in this present time as from the beginning of the world; for the power of the divine arm cannot be diminished in the least. For it is not to be believed that God has turned away or withdrawn the rays of his wisdom even from the impious, since she [Wisdom] even these...

# Section I. Portion III. Part I. Book I.

she even attempts to entice [souls] to herself, if by chance they might be seriously induced to seek her: For we find in Proverbs 1:20 <note>original: "Prou. 1. 20."</note> that Wisdom cries aloud and lifts her voice in the streets, calling out in the high places, in the throng of men, at the entrance of the gates, and uttering her words in the city, saying: *"How long, O simple ones, will you embrace simplicity? How long will mockers and scoundrels delight in their mockery? How long will fools hate prudence? Receive my reproofs; behold, I will pour out my mind to you and make you understand my words. For I called, but you refused; I stretched out my hands, but no one took it to heart."* From this it is clear that it is not by God's fault that such power and familiarity between us and Him—and the sacred wisdom flowing from Him—does not intervene, but rather it must be imputed to our innate darkness. It is not the severity of Jehovah, nor that kind and gentle Spirit of all power, but the envious perversity of the Devil that keeps us back and restricts us from performing miracles and seeing miraculous visions, which our fathers—namely the Patriarchs and holy Prophets—happened to see, according to that passage in Wisdom 1 <note>The Wisdom of Solomon, an apocryphal book</note>: *God did not make death, nor does He delight in the destruction of men; for He created all things that they might exist, and that the generations in the world might be preserved, and the poison of destruction is not in them, nor is the kingdom of hell upon the earth: but man brings destruction upon himself by the works of his own hands,* and likewise in Wisdom 2:23: *God created man incorruptible, and formed him in the image of His own likeness, but through the envy of the Devil, death entered into the world, etc.* What then shall we say of Wisdom, except that she was sent by Jehovah to counter the tricks and machinations of the Devil and death, by instructing man in what is right before God, and preserving us—like a true tree of life and spiritual bread—from the stings of hunger and death, both spiritual and corporeal.

Wherefore, by the wise King <note>Solomon</note>, Wisdom is said to hold prosperity and longevity in her right hand, and honor and riches in her left, for which reason she is preferred above gold and precious stones: for Job 28 denies that man knows the price of Wisdom: *Gold shall not be given for it, nor shall its price be weighed in silver; no one can value it with gold, or the shining gem, or the Diamond,* and for this reason Solomon judges that man most blessed who attains her in Proverbs 3. And let no one of our age flatter himself, saying that he possesses wisdom: for this imagination of theirs is a type or index of "double ignorance." For in the first place, these men are not wise except in their own judgment, and then afterwards they are entirely ignorant of that discrepancy which exists between human wisdom and divine wisdom. If they knew this, they would frankly confess that human wisdom is mere foolishness and a "fantastic science" <note>knowledge based on appearances or delusions</note> propagated by the vain inventions of men; whereas, on the contrary, Divine Wisdom was with God Himself when He prepared the heavens, and established the high clouds above, when He stabilized the earth and the springs below, and served Him as a "helping right hand" in that all-encompassing composition, and who continually plays before God, as we find in Proverbs 8:22. This Wisdom has built her house with seven columns skillfully polished, to which she invites all to drink of her wine and eat of her food, saying in Proverbs 9:5: *Come, eat of my food, and drink of the wine which I have mixed.* This is she who says to her friends in the Song of Songs 4:17 <note>original: "Cant. 4. 17."</note>: *Enter into my garden, gather my myrrh with my spices; I will give my wine with milk: eat, O friends; drink, and be inebriated, O beloved.* This is she (Wisdom 5:24) who never fades or withers, who is easily perceived or found by those who praise her, and is quickly found by those who seriously investigate her; she goes to meet those who wait for her, and offers herself freely to those who desire her; she dwells among those who require her, and manifests herself to them in the "Royal Way." This is that true Wisdom which can teach man all things; for she herself is "certain knowledge," etc. (Wisdom 7:17). Inquiry provides the science of all things; it shows the knowledge of the creation of the world, and reveals the powers of the elements, the beginning, end, and middle of times, and their vicissitudes and changes of the parts of years, the course of the year, and the situation of the stars, the natures of living things, and the rages of beasts, the powers of the winds, and the imaginations of men, the diversities of plants, and the virtues of roots. Finally, she lays open all things, both the abstruse and the known. What then is human wisdom in respect to this, but mere fatuity and willful ignorance, which produces nothing but delusory imaginations?

O blessed man, therefore (let me repeat the very words of the wise man in Proverbs 3), and thrice blessed is he who possesses and rightly governs this splendid heavenly manna! How well he may be counted among the chosen sons of God, who is adorned with the presence and power of Christ! For he acquires whatever treasures there are of health, wealth, and prosperity, both spiritual and corporeal, which were mentioned above. Nor do I doubt that such men are found in the world, for Holy Scripture teaches us that Wisdom delights most of all to be among the sons of men; she even blesses with all these gifts of hers those who perhaps incline themselves toward her, and hold her in honor and esteem, and in the place of a most splendid queen. So that I may conclude this chapter as well as this part of my discourse, I say that this heavenly bread, this heavenly manna, this spiritual rock, this divine wisdom, this "all in all" of life—this, I say, is Jesus Christ, according to that kind of bread which differs from common bread as heaven differs from earth, or light from darkness. He is a companion so excellent that whoever has attained Him can say with the best right, along with the Philosopher: *"I carry all my things with me,"* <note>A saying attributed to Bias of Priene</note> or with Morienus, 그 pious hermit: *"He who has all things with him has no need of foreign help."* <note>Morienus was a legendary alchemist and hermit</note> But because I may perhaps seem to you a stranger in this arduous science, and to have wandered very far from the investigation of this real Divine Wisdom, I will nevertheless show myself a supporter of its investigation, and I will give my greatest effort (God assisting and being propitious) toward this "palace of happiness" for my journey. Finally, as for the internal secret which I have contemplated along with this external and earthly bread, it confirms me constantly that there is such an eternal and life-giving essence among men, which is the true heavenly bread, the spiritual rock, the heavenly manna, and the most divine wisdom, through which every single thing participates more or less in the nature of its Creator; but principally her delight is to converse with man, the most excellent image or icon in the composition of the Divine Creator, as one to whom this very Wisdom—the immediate offspring of the Deity—is most nearly present and within.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical and theological defense of Divine Wisdom as the source of all true knowledge and miraculous power, contrasting it with the "double ignorance" of worldly wisdom.</meta>

# Section I. Portion III. Part I. Book I.

She even attempts to entice people to herself, if by chance they might be seriously induced to seek her: For we find in Proverbs 1:20 <note>The author quotes a Latin version of the Bible, likely the Vulgate or a similar Renaissance translation.</note> *Wisdom cries out and raises her voice in the streets, calling out in high places, in the crowd of men, at the entrance of the gates, and uttering her words in the city, saying: "How long, O simple ones, will you embrace folly? How long will mockers and scoundrels delight in their scoundrelry? How long will fools hate prudence? Receive my reproofs; behold, I will open my mind to you and make you understand my words. For I called, but you turned away; I stretched out my hands, but no one took it to heart."* From this it is clear that it is not by God's fault that such great power and familiarity with Him—and the sacred wisdom flowing from Him—does not intervene for us, but it must be imputed to our innate darkness. It is not the severity of Jehovah, nor that courteous and gentle spirit of His omnipotence, but the perversity of the envious Devil that keeps us back and restricts us from performing miracles and seeing miraculous visions, which happened to be seen by our fathers, namely the Patriarchs and holy Prophets, according to that passage in Wisdom 1: *God did not make death, nor does He delight in the destruction of men; for He created all things that they might exist, and that the generations in the world might be preserved; the poison of destruction is not in them, and the kingdom of hell is not upon the earth; but man brings destruction upon himself by the works of his own hands.* And likewise in Wisdom 2:23: *God created man incorruptible, and formed him in the image of His own likeness, but by the envy of the Devil death entered into the world, etc.* What then shall we say of wisdom, except that she was sent by Jehovah to counter the tricks and machinations of the Devil and death, by instructing man in what is right before God, and preserving us like a true tree of life and spiritual bread from the stings of hunger and death, both spiritual and bodily. Wherefore, by the wise King <note>King Solomon</note>, wisdom is said to hold prosperity and longevity in her right hand, and honor and riches in her left, for which reason she is preferred above gold and precious stones: for Job 28 denies that man knows the price of wisdom: *Gold shall not be given for it, nor shall its price be weighed in silver; no one can value it with gold, or the shining gem, or the Diamond,* and for this reason Solomon judges that man most blessed who attains her (Proverbs 3). And let no one of our age flatter himself, saying that he possesses wisdom: for this imagination of theirs is a type or index of double ignorance. For in the first place, these men are not wise except in their own judgment, and then afterwards they are entirely ignorant of that discrepancy which exists between human wisdom and divine wisdom; if they knew this, they would candidly confess that human wisdom is mere folly and a "fantastic" knowledge <note>meaning imaginary or illusory</note> propagated by the vain inventions of men. On the contrary, divine wisdom was with God Himself when He fitted the heavens and established the high clouds above, when He stabilized the earth and the fountains below; she served Him as a helping right hand in that all-encompassing composition, and she continually plays before God, as we find in Proverbs 8:22. *This wisdom built her house with seven columns skillfully polished, to which she invites all to drink of her wine and eat of her food, saying in Proverbs 9:5: "Come, eat of my food, and drink of the wine which I have mixed."* This is she of whom it is said to her friends in Canticles 4:17 <note>Song of Solomon</note>: *Enter into my garden, gather my myrrh with my spices; I will give my wine with milk: eat, friends; drink, and be intoxicated, beloved.* This is she (Wisdom 5:24) *who never fades or withers, who is easily perceived or found by those who praise her, and is quickly found by those who seriously investigate her; she goes to meet those who desire her, and offers herself freely to those who long for her; she moves among those who require her, and manifests herself to them in the royal way.* This is that true wisdom which can teach man all things; for she is certain knowledge, etc. Wisdom 7:17: *Inquiry provides the science of all things; it shows the knowledge of the creation of the world, and reveals the powers of the elements, the beginning, end, and middle of times, and their vicissitudes and the changes of the parts of the years, the course of the year, and the placement of the stars, the natures of living things, and the impulses of beasts, the powers of the winds, and the imaginations of men, the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots.* Finally, she discloses all things, both hidden and known. What then is human wisdom in respect to this, but mere fatuity and spontaneous ignorance, which produces nothing but delusory imaginations? O blessed man, therefore (let me find the very words of wisdom in Proverbs 3), and thrice blessed is he who possesses and rightly governs this splendid heavenly manna! How well he can be counted here among the chosen sons of God, who is adorned with the presence and power of Christ! For he acquires whatever treasures there are of health, wealth, and prosperity, both spiritual and bodily, which were mentioned above. Nor do I doubt that such men are found in the world, for Holy Scripture teaches us that wisdom delights most of all among the sons of men; she also blesses with all these gifts of hers those who perhaps incline themselves toward her, and hold her in honor and esteem, and in the place of a most splendid queen. So that I may conclude this chapter as well as this part of my discourse, I say that this heavenly bread, this heavenly manna, this spiritual rock, this divine wisdom, this "all in all" of life—this, I say, is Jesus Christ, that fruitful kind of bread which differs from common bread as heaven differs from earth, or light from darkness. He is a companion so excellent that whoever has attained Him can say by the best right with the Philosopher <note>Likely Bias of Priene</note>: *I carry all my things with me*, or with Morienus, that pious hermit <note>A legendary alchemist</note>: *He who has all things with him has no need of outside help.* But because I may perhaps seem to you a stranger in this arduous science, and to wander very far from the investigation of this real divine wisdom, I will nonetheless show myself a supporter of its investigation, and with my greatest effort (God assisting and being propitious) I will give myself to the journey toward this palace of happiness. Finally, as for the internal secret which I have contemplated along with this external and earthly bread, it confirms me constantly that there is such an eternal and life-giving essence among men, which is the true heavenly bread, the spiritual rock, the heavenly manna, and the most divine wisdom, through which every single thing participates more or less in the nature of its Creator; but principally her delight is to converse with man, the most excellent image or icon in the composition of the divine Creator, as one to whom this very wisdom, the immediate offspring of the Deity, is most nearly present and inherent.

<summary>The author argues that true Divine Wisdom (identified with Christ and the "heavenly manna") is available to those who seek it, offering mastery over both spiritual truths and the natural world, including the "virtues of roots" and the "placement of stars." He contrasts this with the "mere folly" of human invention and asserts that man's inability to perform miracles is due to his own spiritual darkness rather than God's withholding of power.</summary>

# Section I. Portion III. Part I. Book II.

...or subtle, and that all water is nothing else but a spirit, either dense or thin; and therefore all things, in respect to their matter, are nothing but one thing, namely water. This was that sole and unique substance in creation, upon which that unique <term>Elohim</term><note>The Hebrew name for God used in Genesis</note>, that God alone, moved over the waters to work toward the perfection of the world and all things contained within it. Furthermore, lest anyone here should quibble and object: "What then is the reason for the thickening and thinning through so many degrees in the whole element of water, so that it is divided and appears as different heavens, spheres, and elements?" I answer that, just as we gather from ice, snow, and similar effects of winter, cold is the primary agent in the mutual binding and condensation of different discordant substances; so, on the contrary, heat is found to be the attacker of the frozen actions of cold, by means of which those actions are weakened, melted, and finally dissolved entirely into the liquid nature of flowing water. 

Hence it happens that where cold (which is the origin of dark <term>Chaos</term><note>The formless state before creation</note>, and therefore the enemy and opposite of heat, which is light and the offspring of <term>Demogorgon</term><note>A primordial deity often associated with the underworld or the deep origin of nature</note>) claims dominion for itself, there thickness and density reign in the general mass of water. But where heat—the most noble officer of the universal Emperor, namely Light—is present and powerful, there conversely an effect opposite to cold is produced. Where they meet together and rule with equal dominion, there also is the sphere of equality, or the orb or circle of the <term>Soul of the World</term><note>Latin: *Anima Mundi*; the vital force connecting all living things</note> about which the Platonists treated in such a perplexed and intricate manner. By means of this (as we hinted in our *Physical History of the Macrocosm*) the most splendid Sun of the greater world moves, or in it (as we explained in our *History of the Microcosm*) that vivifying heart in the <term>microcosm</term><note>The human being as a "little world" reflecting the universe</note> flourishes and leaps. 

Wherefore it appears clearly to the wise man that where light most abounds and dominates, there the watery spirit is rendered most subtle and thin by the operative virtue of heat, proceeding and flashing forth from the act and motion of the luminous rays. For the succeeding heat, by its presence, so repels and drives away its adversary, cold, that it denies it the matter, time, and place to bring the natural effects of condensation into action. On the contrary, where light, and consequently heat, is weak, there its opposite is necessarily rendered stronger. And although the degrees of heat and cold in this semi-diameter—the measure of which is taken from the circumference of the world of light to the dark center—are infinite in number, nevertheless, disagreeing very little from other philosophers in this matter, we have distinguished them into only six natures evidently differing from one another, which, like <term>Jacob's Ladder</term><note>A biblical reference to a ladder reaching to heaven</note>, stretch upward from the center of the greater world to its circumference. And the order of the ascending steps or intervals of this ladder is as follows: **Earth, Water, Air, Fire, Ether, and the Empyrean Spirit.** Furthermore, just above this highest sixth step, a seventh or supreme step stands out, where the general <term>Sabbath</term><note>Original: *Saboth*; the divine rest</note> of all rest resides, as it is the place where the presence of God is permanent. From which it is right to gather that the further we recede from this source of light, the thicker and denser the substance of water becomes.

<column-break/>

For just as light, by the ministry of its heat, works from the highest heaven or the circumference of the waters downward toward the center through thinning and purification; so also darkness, by its instrumental cold, striving in the opposite way—that is, by opposition from its center tending upward—endeavors by its natural inclination to meet and receive the actions of the descending messengers of light. This is the reason for the comparison established by me in both my Microcosmic and Macrocosmic history: namely, of the formal heat and motion in the region of light, and the dark matter, to two pyramidal figures of equal dimensions. The ascending material cone of one touches the base of the formal pyramid which is above; and on the contrary, the formal cone of the pyramid descends downward and reaches all the way to the center in the base of the material pyramid, which is in the earth. I have proposed to discourse more widely on this below. We have set forth the figure and position of the said pyramids in this place so that our intention may be more clearly explained to you.

After, therefore, the vigorous act of my earthly fire or heat had penetrated the dark vegetable mass so prepared by a certain secret reverberation, and because in this rejected, putrefied, and almost deformed substance it had imitated by its remarkable agility the virtue of that first and most excellent light leaping out of the dark <term>Hyle</term><note>Greek: *Hyle*; primordial matter</note>: it immediately sublimated a mist or dense cloud from the putrid mass about ten cubits high, not unlike that huge smoke or most foul shadow in the universal creation of all things from nothing (which Moses and Hermes mention in the places cited above). In this action of the art, it was worthy to consider the oblique motions and revolutions made in its ascent: namely, the way the mass was disturbed by the contact of that earthly fire. In exactly the same way it is written that the water of the abyss in the first generation or creation was disturbed and terrified because of the luminous presence of that illuminating fire which lives for all eternity (Psalm 77:17). And the same prophet recites (Psalm 18:12) that the clouds and dark waters fled from the splendor of His presence. So also this cloud leaped out from its dark and putrefied abyss away from the sight and contact of this lower light or fire, and flew into the heights, and again tended downward. Withdrawing itself for a long time to the upper part of its vessel, it hovered like a thick mist, until by the virtue of condensing cold it is coagulated (just as in the middle region of the air we see vapors frozen by cold into dense clouds) into a denser water. Because of its weight and by a natural impulse, it was forced to fall back toward the earth from which it had ascended by violent motion. Thus, by this progress, namely by coagulation...

# On the Exact Anatomy of Bread or Wheat.

Although the thicker and thinner waters of the sublunary region <note>The region below the moon, which in ancient science was subject to change and decay</note> were produced within the universal structure of the macrocosm <note>The great world or universe</note>—namely, from an infinite moist vapor or smoking and misty cloud reduced into an aqueous substance—this substance was more tightly constricted and condensed in this sphere of the "greater world" than in the other. This occurred by the power of the cold quality hidden in the dark matter of every thing; therefore, it is heavier and more exposed to sight in one place than in another. By such a distinction, the waters are said by Moses to be separated from the waters, and the earth from both. And so, I have set forth to you the full substance of this, my first mystical vision, which first presented itself to my eyes, now revealed through this common dissection or "anatomy" of ours.

<image-desc>A detailed copperplate engraving illustrating an alchemical distillation or sublimation process. At the bottom, a round glass vessel sits atop a brick furnace. A long neck rises from the vessel, leading into a large, dense, billowing cloud. Inside this cloud, vertical lines represent moisture or rain falling back down. To the right, a secondary part of the apparatus is visible, suggesting a continuous process or a separate stage of the experiment.</image-desc>

### CHAPTER III.

#### Concerning the second appearance in the form of Water exhibited by itself.

Just as we observe a thick mist gather on the peaks and ridges of the Alpine mountains—while the solar rays nevertheless shine all around in their most excellent glory—which suddenly, by thickening into a dense cloud, finally vanishes and drips drop by drop, dissolved into rain that fills the surrounding wells and pools: so also it happened in this work of ours. For in the second appearance, the dark mist or misty vapor, by gradually vanishing from the sight of the eyes, was converted into downward-dripping drops. These represented that "golden rain" which the Poets fabulously tell of raining into Danaë’s tower <note>A reference to the Greek myth where Zeus visited Danaë as a shower of gold</note>, so that I observed a sea, as if a certain small abyss of water, succeed that dark mist. This water was everywhere splendid, animated and decorated by the tincture of spiritual light. 

And from that moment, I immediately recalled to mind how the Spirit of the *Elohim* <note>original: "spiritus Elohim"; the Hebrew name for God used in Genesis</note> is reported by Moses to have been carried over the waters in the first creation of the world, liberally imparting to them from his fiery act or virtue. Regarding this passage, St. Augustine, in his commentaries on Genesis, writes: *The Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters, giving them a fiery vigor* <note>original: "Spiritus domini mouebatur super aquis, vigorem illis igneum edens"</note>. And Hermes Trismegistus <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure associated with alchemy and hermetic philosophy</note> says: *The Holy splendor flourished, which led the elements forth under the sand and moist nature.* 

In plainly the same way, I perceived that the universal water of this experiment of mine contained within itself the image or vestiges of that same light, which was infused into it by the vivifying spirit in the threefold creation, inasmuch as it received its essence from it. Thus, with due contemplation leading the way, I clearly observed that this "lesser world" of water comprehended within itself all those things which the Water of the universal "greater world" contained at that very time in which the Spirit of the Lord was carried over them—namely, the universal spirit of light or splendor, which was the soul of the world <note>original: "anima mundi"</note>, or a certain universal spiritual and volatile Air containing within itself the five particular elements: namely, Ether, Fire, Air, Water, and Earth, concerning which...

<summary>The author describes an alchemical experiment where a misty vapor condenses into "golden rain," comparing this laboratory process to the biblical creation of the world and the separation of the waters. He invokes authorities like Moses, St. Augustine, and Hermes Trismegistus to argue that the water in his flask contains the same divine "soul of the world" as the primordial elements.</summary>

# Section I. Portion III. Part I. Book II.

...of which we shall speak later in its proper place. I say, therefore, that in this mass of the aqueous element I observed a thing worthy of note: namely, that after I had separated its airy tincture and spirit from it by the common way of Alchemy <note>original: *via Alchimiæ communi*; likely referring to standard distillation</note>, the water nevertheless strove daily to attract a new tincture to itself more and more. This occurred by the power of that remaining vegetable and multiplying spirit which could not be separated. Furthermore, the abundance of the aqueous element springing forth from so small a subject <note>The "subject" here is the grain of wheat being analyzed</note> showed me the reason why bread or wheat in its own nature—if the due preparation and correction through both fermentation and cooking (by which this superfluous moisture is consumed and fed upon) are not first applied—is so adverse and harmful to the human body, producing many infirmities in it through putrefaction. On the contrary, I am certain that this is that very excrement or moist superfluity in bread, ingested along with the nourishment, which nature purges from the blood mass through the kidneys into the bladder; and that false spirit, which can hardly be separated due to its volatile disposition, is the reason why human urine is salty and infected with such acrimony. Here, then, is that very salt which is extracted by Alchemists from the multitude of urine, which they call salt ammoniac <note>original: *sal armoniacum*; ammonium chloride, historically derived from organic waste</note>. And so, I shall lightly pass over this second appearance of this subject, which concerned the universal water, so that on swifter wings of dispatch we may approach the anatomy of its more central parts—namely, their formal qualities, figures, and occult virtues, by means of which it was preserved from corruption.

### CHAPTER IV.

->*The third vision was the spirit which was covered by and intermixed with the waters. The method of separating the airy part from the dreggy aqueous part: How this airy liquor differs from common water. Its use and properties in both the vegetable and animal nature. Furthermore, many experimental conclusions are revealed in this place, by which the faculties of this spirit are disclosed.*<-

But since I discovered a twofold nature in this aqueous abyss, one of which seemed to act, while the other sustained it as a passive participant in just proportion, a vehement desire immediately seized me to seek out that airy disposition. Thus, I attempted by a subtle operation to distinguish it from its thick matter which receives its actions, so that I might subject its naked and open nature (if it were possible) to my eyes. To accomplish this, I changed my agent—that is, the heat serving the aforesaid operation—from the burning heat of a parched summer to the temperate disposition of a misty spring. I was forced to divide this degree of heat, or "rule of fire" <note>original: *ignis regimen*; a technical term for controlling the intensity of the furnace</note>, into three natures. The first was warm in the first degree and less moist, and because of this, the coldest of the three; I adapted and appropriated this to the first entry of springtime, which refers to the month of March, specifically after the Sun has entered Aries. The second degree of this spring fire was warmer and most moist, proportioned to the entry of the Sun into Taurus, which produces those April showers by whose power plants yearn to put forth their shoots and leaves, and the crops are accustomed to germinate. The last was the most warm and more moist, which can be not inconveniently referred to the entry of the Sun into Gemini; by their most pleasant temperament, the most beautiful and regular state or circuit of the year is established—namely, that lovely time of May, when the meadows, distinguished by sweet-smelling and variegated flowers, laugh on every side. Thus I adapted the degrees of my fire to perform this act of separation: so that by the first heat I might separate the thinner water from the thicker mass, in which the lurking spirit (though previously indicated only by its effects) now appeared in its visible substance. By the second, I segregated the pure vegetative spirit from the thicker residues of the water. And finally, by the third of my spring degrees, I exhibited the spirit in various forms and at last in its own proper disposition.

# On the Exact Anatomy of Bread or Wheat.

<image-desc>An engraving of three alchemical distillation vessels. The central apparatus is a large alembic consisting of a rounded boiling flask on a stand, topped with a tall still-head or cap. A delivery tube (beak) extends from the cap into a smaller receiving vessel on the right. To the left stands another separate, smaller flask or vessel. The engraving uses fine cross-hatching to create a sense of three-dimensional form.</image-desc>

When, therefore, in my first action I had separated the thinner water from the spirit (which was still held back by the viscous muscles of the fundamental or drossy mass), I perceived that the entire residue had taken on the form of a honey-sweet and thick liquor. It was drawn through with rays on all sides, and distinguished and suffused with a bright tincture like gold. After I had considered this sufficiently, I extracted the purer spirit from the drossy substance by the power of my second heat or agent. However, it appeared defiled on all sides by spots of earthy parts, which strove to ascend with it into the head of the <term>alembic</term> <note>A distillation apparatus consisting of a boiling flask and a cap with a beak.</note>. For this reason, I adapted this still-impure spirit to the lowest degree of my heat. By the power of this (a thing wonderful to relate to the ignorant), a spirit—entirely pure, white, and crystalline—composed (as far as I could recognize) of pure volatile salt, ascended into the head of a certain crystalline vessel and fell back into its receiver. 

And this liquor—although because of its clarity and liquidity it seems to be the purest water—is nevertheless, by its bulk, fluidity, and the quality of its substance, seen to be of a nature far more excellent than common water. It was to the sight liquidly flowing, penetrating, and agile in action. By well-known experience, it clearly appears to be that other <term>Psyche</term> <note>The soul or animating principle.</note> of that celestial Cupid, seeking the act of all things, and as ardently desiring the beautiful heat and golden tincture of the Sun as a woman desires union with a man. And I know for certain that this is that hidden *patient* <note>The passive principle that receives action.</note> in the world which receives the secret influences of the celestial act, and not that common water, which is rather the helper and cause of putrefaction, or the patient of the choleric fire of the element, by which all lower things are reduced to corruption. 

This is that hidden vegetable balsam in every vegetable creature, whether it be plant or animal; for it causes vegetation in plants by extracting its like from the air or the water which falls from heaven to moisten the plant. Yet it is not the whole substance of that rainwater that contributes to vegetation, but a certain insensible part of it, which is elicited from that rainwater by its true and natural <term>Alchemy</term>, leaving what remains in the grain as a superfluity, of which I spoke a little before. By this means, I say, the plant multiplies itself in its material substance, which, then eliciting and deriving its form from the golden palace of heaven, abundantly distributes the power of multiplication to all things. 

But when this matter has attracted a form worthy of itself, a <term>Hermaphrodite</term> <note>In alchemy, a union of opposites, often male/female or fixed/volatile.</note> is produced—that is, one most fertile in both sexes, namely male and female ruling under one vegetable form. And yet, it will nonetheless produce offspring of its own kind no less than a man will procreate progeny—unless it is included in the general matrix of the mother of all vegetables, namely the earth, just as a man must first immerse his seed in the womb of a woman. This is that hidden water which follows the animal with such love, which generates blood and increases seed in the animal, and consequently is the sole pillar or support of the natural faculty both in man and in beasts. But because all these things may seem impossible to the incredulous as well as to the ignorant, I shall proceed to cite faithfully in this place those experiments which came into my sight in this work, even unexpectedly, so that you may give credit by a more certain demonstration to those things reported by us.

### The first experiment by which it is proved that this spirit participates in the nature of the universal air.

After I had manifested the crude spirit to my eyes (prepared, as I said before, by a spring-like fire of the second degree), I set about purifying it by the moderation of the first heat. By means of this work, I observed the spirit ascending in the head of the Alembic coagulating into small bits of whitish substance, some of which were like snow, while others were turned again into tiny particles like hail. The residue, however, which felt the external cold the least, distilled downward into the Receiver in liquid form. From this, one can see that snow or hail is nothing other than air in the middle region of the air, coagulated by the virtue or force of freezing cold. Therefore, this operation by artificial heat—just as the air of the world by natural heat—demonstrates that this spirit draws its origin from the universal spirit of the air. In turn, I gathered from this frozen snow or hail that although the external and manifest appearance of the aerial spirit is translucent and white, its internal and hidden nature is fiery and shining like gold; for this white substance, touched or treated with even a little heat, immediately [turns] into moisture...

He begins an experiment comparing the behavior of this spirit to the formation of snow and hail in the atmosphere.</summary>

# Section I. Portion III. Part I. Book II.

...a golden liquid, pleasing to the eye, and not at all unlike **potable gold** <note>Latin: *auro potabili*; a legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold dissolved in a liquid state</note>, it liquefies completely. This reveals to us the mind of the philosophers through a somewhat raw example, when they say:
> *That which is manifest in it is white and watery, but that which is hidden is red and fiery,*
And again when they say:
> *Make the hidden manifest, and the manifest hidden;*

The reason why common snow or hail of the "greater world" <note>The Macrocosm or the universe at large</note> does not obtain this tincture or manifest this hidden essence after its dissolution is the crude abundance of water within them. By the presence of this crude water, the nature of the congealed spirit is stained and contaminated. Therefore, after its dissolution, it appears to be nothing other than white water. Nevertheless, just as seeds or grains suck out this invisible and spiritual essence or "tincture" from raindrops after natural putrefaction in the earth, so too does this essence lie hidden in the secret workshops of the raindrops to aid both its growth and multiplication. This spiritual moisture, therefore, is nothing other than **air**, and for this reason, it is nourished by its own kind.

<image-desc>An alchemical engraving of a cylindrical furnace with a tiered upper section. A rounded vessel or alembic sits on top. The various parts are labeled with numbers and letters. The furnace rests on a square base with an arched opening at the front.</image-desc>

### The second experiment, by which it is proved that the aerial spirit is enclosed secretly within the watery element.

To prove that air is contained in every particle of water, no argument can be produced more pregnant and evident than this ocular demonstration: we may clearly perceive how this aerial spirit is present in every part of the universal water, just as the soul is said to move in every limb of the body. For this spirit in water is truly the **radical moisture** <note>The fundamental life-sustaining fluid of a living being</note> of the world, or that hidden and latent spirit which receives that vivifying light from the **Spirit of God** <note>Latin: *spiritu Elohim*</note> which moved upon the universal waters (from which both heaven and earth were made). By means of this spirit, they live, move, and receive their life-giving essence, as will be more clearly declared below. I have found it to be a matter of immense difficulty to separate water from its spirit, as the water is not at all prone to lose or leave behind its vegetable soul; indeed, it is quite difficult. What this spirit is, diffused everywhere through the waters, we have learned from another experiment besides the demonstration in our subject, which also confirms our assertion: for during an exercise in swimming (while I was staying in the French city of Nîmes), I submerged myself to the bottom of the river and struck two flints together with a strong collision. From this, a terrible crash was produced because of the air enclosed in the water. But since the medium or means of the sense of hearing is air alone, according to the doctrine of the philosophers, it follows from these concessions that air is abundantly contained in water, and it is proven by that experiment.

### The third experiment teaches that the aerial spirit abundantly incites vegetation.

Now we shall bring forward the reason by which it will be proved that this spirit is the sole and unique cause of vegetation in every seed or plant. Generally, we observe in the first place that celestial rains (which embrace much of this aerial spirit within themselves), when poured out in due time upon the parched earth, are the chief cause of the germination of seeds and plants. But I shall proceed to an experiment which, though it may perhaps seem impossible to the incredulous, I shall not fear to bring forward on my own faith, because I know it to be so and because I have beheld it with these eyes of mine. One day my operator, a Frenchman by nation, called me suddenly into the laboratory or **workshop** <note>Latin: *ergasterium*</note>. There he showed me a thin and simple **iron plate** <note>Latin: *lamina ferrea*</note> which well covered a clay pot, into which he had, by chance or fortune, placed part of those dregs from which this spirit had been extracted a second time. The time during which the pot stood thus covered by the iron plate was, if I am not mistaken, about five weeks—the very time when wheat committed to the earth and putrefied within it is accustomed to emerge again and sprout. At this time, I say, the **vegetable power** <note>The force responsible for growth in the "Great Chain of Being"</note> of the covered matter was observed to be so great (a thing I would not have easily believed myself before) that for lack of vegetable or animal substance, which is natural to it, it even worked upon the mineral body or iron plate itself. For this penetrating spirit, ascending upward from the pot in which it was enclosed, perforated its iron cover. By the effect implanted in it by nature, it worked so powerfully that it caused ten thousand little spikes or stalks, like saffron or like grain emerging from the earth, to rise up from the iron, to grow, and to sprout. All of these had grown to the length of a small needle.

<image-desc>An engraving showing a rectangular metal plate resting on a flat surface. Dozens of thin, hair-like sprouts or "spicula" are growing vertically from the surface of the plate. On the left edge of the plate, there is a small, crab-like figure or a cluster of material.</image-desc>

This vision truly seized us both with no small wonder, and it most clearly persuaded us that this is the unique and very same vegetative part of the plant. I conclude, therefore, with this maxim of the philosophers:
> *That which makes a thing such, is itself more such.* <note>A logical principle: if the spirit makes plants grow, the spirit itself must possess the essence of growth in a higher degree.</note>
This, moreover, is without doubt the substance from which animal blood is generated, as I have proposed to demonstrate more clearly in the following experiment. The present conclusion demonstrates to the eye, as it were, the manner through which plants and herbs grow and germinate from the earth, since this spirit is the vehicle of that **vital spark** which, after the corruption of the grain in the earth, strives with all diligence to ascend and return to that ethereal palace from which it takes its origin.

# On the Exact Anatomy of Bread or Wheat.

### *The fourth experiment reveals to us the true method of growth and multiplication for both vegetables and animals.*

Therefore, having taken this volatile spirit—which was white, and as transparent and clear as crystal—and having finally exposed it to the rays of the sun, I perceived a total mutual sympathy passing between them. This material spirit, by a certain magnetic power of attraction, drew out for itself a certain formal tincture <note>In alchemy, a "tincture" is a spiritualized substance capable of infusing its qualities into another body.</note> from that shining orb. I observed that within the space of a few hours, it was transmuted from its crystalline whiteness into a ruby red; indeed, I noticed that the longer it was exposed to the solar gaze, the more excellent its tincture became. From this experiment, I gathered the perfect reasoning for multiplication in both the vegetable and animal kingdoms.

For just as a woman (to whom we compare this spirit not inaptly) cannot conceive or multiply without the help or copulation of a man (to whom this formal light has a relation), so neither can this spirit have any increase or multiplication unless the act of light is joined with it. For a passive nature cannot suffer <note>original: "pati" - to undergo change or be acted upon.</note> within itself, and therefore it awaits the natural impressions of some agent previously well-prepared and elaborated by Nature for this purpose. The subsequent natural action and passion <note>The interaction between an active force and a passive receiver.</note> of these are the cause of increase and multiplication in the same species which they inhabit; and this happens in each of the three kingdoms of Nature, without which no generation or multiplication occurs in them.

Thus this spirit, once putrefaction has occurred in the earth and it is restored to its freedom, deserts that dark tabernacle in which it dwells and wanders more freely toward that celestial fire, by whose power it is multiplied, quickened, and effectively moved. For this is the only active fire which, by multiplication, moves toward generation; and this is that passive spirit or medium through which the quickening light moves in composition. By means of this—as if by the most precious juice and substance of all sublunary things—the species is best nourished. And because a tiny portion of the formal light of that spirit suffices to inform a multiplicative grain, it follows that this spirit sucks in matter for itself and its kind, and that matter, by a certain natural appetite, attracts the portion of light required for its formation. And this is the cause of multiplication, preceded by its liberation through putrefaction made in the earth, just as we are taught by experience every year.

Furthermore, even in animals, as this very spirit (clothed in this active nature) is continually introduced into the body both through nourishment and through inspiration (namely the attraction of this kind of spirit by the lungs), their individual members grow and multiply and expand in dimension, so that their spermatic substance is increased and rendered fit and liable for generation. It must be noted, however, that for the multiplication of an animal, a larger portion of this ethereal or celestial spirit and fiery form is required than for that of a vegetable creature. How this spirit attracts its like to itself we are taught by the example of Salt of Tartar <note>Potassium carbonate, known for its ability to absorb moisture from the air.</note>, which by a certain magnetic vigor allures to itself the hidden volatile spirit in the air, until on account of the attracted aerial substance it becomes so raw and liquid that it is accustomed to flow in the form of a liquor like common water.

### *The fifth experiment proves that this spirit is in the universal air, because it participates in water, fire, and the quintessence.*

I also discovered that this spirit is diffused through the universal space of the world and fills every part of the world, insofar as I perceived it to agree and mix with the element of water by natural instinct, not otherwise than the way form is accustomed to embrace matter. So also it had no less familiarity with fire, as it easily embraced it on the other side; indeed, I found this formal essence of the air to be nothing else than a sort of coarser and more material portion of the quintessence <note>The "fifth element," a pure, heavenly substance beyond the four earthly elements.</note>, supplying the place of a bond for the discordant elements in the sublunary region. For by diligent speculation, I observed that this spirit was received into a close and inviolable familiarity by the quintessence, and relates to it in the same way that water relates to air; as we shall explain in its proper place.

# Section I. Portion III. Part I. Book II.

In the same way, a certain spiritual <term>tincture</term><note>A transformative essence or spiritual dye</note> (most rightly compared to the fiery heaven or the <term>Empyrean</term><note>The highest heaven, composed of pure light or fire</note>) bestowed life and action upon the denser water. And just as these two heavens, before the creation of the third day, covered the immense depth of the <term>Chaos</term><note>The primordial unformed matter</note> which filled the cavity of the lower heavens, so also the water, mixed with the spirit of the tincture, moved like a deep abyss above my dark chaos, covering and submerging it, no differently than the heaven covers the earth. Therefore, having separated the double water from the black mass, I found that mass to be as dark as the blackest pitch and as tenacious as birdlime, namely on account of the deformed spirits and viscous slipperiness contained within it. I therefore took that double water and applied a very slow fire, observing with the greatest care I possibly could all the artificial degrees of heat; yet, I call God as my witness, it was only after a long space of time that I was able to distinguish them and separate them from one another. For this reason, I erred many times regarding this work and applied my labor in vain. Therefore, I diligently set myself to imitate that circular light of Nature, and I administered strength to my fire as reason persuaded me the task required. In the first place, I extracted a portion of the thicker water, which I compare with the aqueous element of the sublunary sphere; afterward, I drew out a portion of the aerial spirit. I omit a specific mention of this here because I have said enough words about it in the preceding sections, so that I may discuss more fully the element of fire, or the fourth element, and then afterward the <term>Ether</term><note>The fifth element or quintessence</note>, which is the fifth essence or fifth element, still drawn away from its thick garment. And finally, I shall bring an end to this book with a description and consideration of the earth, comparing it in this experiment of mine with that of the greater world. Because this will seem very difficult and (as I divine) obscure to those who are not well-versed in my volume on the Macrocosm, I refer them entirely to the first book of that work on this matter, where they will find all these things explained plainly and lucidly.

### CHAPTER VII.

->In which the appearance of the fiery Element following the aerial moisture, and also the<-
->inclination of that same nature toward the corruption and putrefaction<-
->of all things, are explained.<-

AFTER the spirit of the subtle Air succeeded the element of water, immediately fire in the form of a fiery liquor, or a thick and reddish oil, exhibited itself to my sight. This nature was thoroughly different from water, and of another form than air, exhaling also a foul stench and a heavy odor. When this was purified by circulation or <term>rectification</term><note>The process of refining a liquid by repeated distillation</note>, it took on a saffron or red color not unlike the flame of a kitchen fire; yet it refused to leave behind or lose its heavy odor, however much it was cleansed. Therefore, with due contemplation leading the way, I noticed that this was the only active element in the sublunary sphere, by whose hostile force those alterations of corruption in the world are produced, and that by its violence creatures are driven to rot. Indeed, this is the element that dominates the production of putrefaction in the body, and under its dominion the body itself especially putrefies. In the act of putrefaction, a most foul stench arises, so that the sense of smell is severely offended by the vaporous exhalations of this element from the rotting body. Furthermore, just as we find the aerial spirit (which I mentioned above) to be feminine, well-adapted, and passive for producing generation—whose agent or husband is the celestial fire, or that light of the quintessence, disposing the air as a passive subject for this kind of alteration in the course of nature—so the element of water is a passive subject serving chiefly for mortification or corruption, as it is liable to decay. Its agent, however, is the stinking elementary fire, urging and promoting the composite body toward the privative progress of alteration, which motion is contrary to the progress of nature. And although water seems to nourish, yet in truth it does not nourish by itself, but only that unique spirit lurking within it, which alone is retained by Nature for nutrition in the body; the useless superfluity of the water is emitted through urine. But where water in its own nature alone exults or overflows in the composite body beyond the laws of its natural temperament, there, because of its exuberance, "stupid" and <term>hydropic</term><note>Dropsical; related to edema or water retention</note> diseases are usually procreated. This happens especially when its agent, or the element of fire, holds the smallest place in the alteration; for following the possession of this kind of unnatural water are faintings or swoonings, <term>Lethargies</term>, <term>Apoplexy</term>, <term>Catocha</term><note>A rigid state similar to catalepsy</note>, <term>Catalepsy</term>, stupors, and others of that kind. But where the agent is of equal power with the patient <note>The "patient" here refers to the passive element being acted upon</note>, then false fevers, both phlegmatic and choleric, as well as composite <term>Apostemes</term><note>Abscesses or swellings</note> and such infirmities, predominate in the parts of the body, such as <term>Pleurisy</term> and every kind of <term>Phlegmon</term><note>Inflammatory tumors</note>. But if fire has dominion over the water, then all infirmities derived from salty or burnt phlegm are usually procreated. Yet if the agent is more simple and inhabits a thin vapor of an aqueous nature, then it excites those fevers which are called <term>Ephemeras</term> or <term>Diaries</term><note>Fevers lasting only one day</note>. Where the fire is destitute of its aqueous fuel, so that it is forced to act upon the thicker aerial spirit, there it procreates burning fevers arising from the corruption of the blood called <term>synochus</term>. And for that reason, it inflames the entire mass of the body's humors. Truly, where the corrupted humor of water abounds with the thicker aerial spirit, there a contagious putrefaction arises, which usually procreates smallpox and plagues; but where the corrupted water is thin and mixed with a similar aerial spirit, there pestilential fevers are produced with the spots which are called <term>Petechiae</term> by the Italians. Finally, all diseases, whether procreated from rawness or burning, are generated from a greater or lesser proportion of these two elements, the authors of corruption, so that the aerial spirit itself is frequently disturbed. And thus these two elements never work by themselves and by their own nature except toward destruction; whereas, conversely, the Solar virtue or celestial fire lurking in the aerial spirit acts naturally toward health and life. The Earth, truly, is the receptacle of all these.
