Just as seven princes of the angels are numbered who stand before Jehovah <note>original: "Iehoua"</note>—as we gather in the books of Tobit and Daniel from the mouths of the angels Raphael and Gabriel—so those more skilled in hidden Theosophy <term>Theosophia: divine wisdom or mystical insight</term> as well as the Kabbalah <term>Caballa: Jewish mystical tradition</term> have made these seven Angels presiding governors over the seven Planets. To four of these princes they have also assigned dominion over the four corners or regions of the world: namely, the Eastern Angle to Michael, the Western to Raphael, the Northern to Gabriel, and the Southern to Uriel. These are the good presiding governors who have power and rule over the winds, concerning whom the Kabbalists have written thus: "Angels or demons are called spirits, inasmuch as they are like winds." Wherefore also Rabbi Thedacus Levi, in his book on the ten numerations <note>likely referring to the Sephirot</note>, after he had made mention of the North, South, East, and West winds, continues speaking thus: *“And for those four winds He created four Angels who are appointed over them by day and by night. Michael, who is of the side of mercy and compassions, is appointed prefect over the East wind until midday; Raphael rules the West wind, who is likewise of the side of mercy; then Gabriel, by the power of judgment and severity, is prefect over the North wind; and Horiel (whom others call Uriel) presides over the South.”* He asserts here, moreover, that each of these contains many species or legions under himself. And in the *Gate of Light* <note>original: "Porta lucis," likely the *Sha'are Orah* by Joseph Gikatilla</note> it is read that on earth all the way to the firmament there is no empty place, but everything is full of forms, some of which are pure, and of those, others are capable of grace and mercies; and it is said that there are many foul, harmful, and tempting images below, all of which are said to dwell and fly in the air—some for peace, others for war, some for good, and some for evil, some for life, and some for death—and this is confirmed by Joseph of Castille <note>Joseph Gikatilla</note>. But to proceed, the princes purely called the governors of the four corners have four spirits under them, who are said to be the immediate leaders of the cardinal winds, to whom it is given to harm the earth and the sea. Those deeper in the mysteries of nature have called these Orient, Paymon, Egyn, and Amaymon <note>original: "Ammonium"</note>; the first is said to govern the wind of the dawn (the East wind), the second the West wind in the western angle, the third the North wind, and the last the South wind in the meridian. And it is undoubtedly concerning these spirits that this passage of the Apocalypse is understood:

<margin>Revelation 7.</margin>
*“I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree. And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”* From which we can elicit, first, that four malignant angels are ordained by God, under the command of the good ones, for the government of the cardinal winds; second, that malignant angels are accustomed to harm the earth and creatures by means of the winds or the medium of the air; third, that they cannot hasten to the ruin or harm of sublunary creatures beyond the permission of the Divine Majesty. Finally, it seems that this angel, whom those four spirits appeared to obey, is Michael, who is the leader of the heavenly host, whom the Kabbalists called Metattron <note>Metatron</note>, and they said that this Angel was the one who preceded Moses in the desert, in whom the name of the living God was impressed, as is read in Exodus. Wherefore he is also called here the Priest of Heaven, who is also the leader of the army of Christ, whom the Archangel <note>likely referring to a specific Kabbalistic authority or text</note> in the *Kabbalistic Dogma* affirms fights with his angels for the souls of all against the ancient serpent. It was likely, therefore, that this was that Angel who imposed the law upon those four malignant Angels, lest they harm the earth until the appointed time, and especially because Michael, as Tedacus says (that Rabbi named a little before), *“is of the side of grace and mercies”*; and also because, the serpent having been conquered by him, he and his angels were made obedient to him by force and arms. And yet Satan perpetually resists God and His angels with all his might, and unless the good angels were present for us by divine permission, the malignant spirits would immediately bring irrecoverable ruin to the human race, to whom they are most hostile, inasmuch as they observe that it bears the image of God (whom they hold in hatred). Hence we read among the Kabbalists that just as in the army of God there are four standard-bearers, namely Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Uriel, so also in the army of Satan the avengers Samael, Azazel, Azael, and Mahazael carry the widest sails: of whom Samael exercises his power in the element of fire, Azazel in the air, Azael in the water, and Mahazael in the earth. The aforesaid standard-bearers, therefore, receive their power from the winds or the air, since by means of them they are accustomed to carry out God’s pleasure for evil or punishment, according to the royal Psalmist: *“Stormy wind fulfilling his word,”* where under the name of wind is understood the moved air (which is the external motion of the wind) and the spirit or demon, with his spiritual troops or crowds (which is the internal mover of the wind). Whence Ezekiel says, speaking of the resurrection of the bones: *“Come from the four winds, O spirit, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live,”* where he seems to speak of good angels: for (as the gloss upon this place says) *“by the spirit from the four winds, the prophet understands the four angelic intelligences, which preside over the four corners of the world.”* And Daniel, speaking of harmful spirits, says: *“Behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea,”* by which he most aptly declares the nature of the winds, or the disturbance of the air: namely, that it is nothing other than the contention of spirits of contrary natures in the air. For thus we see waves excited and tossed in the sea by the violent motion of a multitude of fish, or even of one large one, and a great disturbance and noise of the waters occurs. But someone will object that this cannot happen in the case of fiery demons, who spend their lives in the element of fire, nor in those who inhabit the middle region of the air, because in those two spheres of the elementary world, *“wind (according to the opinion of the philosophers) is not found.”* But truly, first I would wish to remind those skilled in philosophy that the demons of any Element inhabit any part of the air at their own free will, and are present everywhere according to the permission of God, either for blessing or for punishment. Furthermore (let this be said with their leave), we frequently gather from the Holy Scriptures that there is wind in the middle region of the air, where we find that *“God makes the clouds his chariot, who walks upon the wings of the wind, who makes his angels winds, his ministers a flaming fire.”* Who is also ignorant

# On Mystical Anatomy.

Whoever is ignorant that the clouds, which are produced and moved in the middle region of the air, are driven by the winds from any quarter of the world toward their opposite, misses the truth. From this it is evident that even the wind (contrary to the opinion of the Peripatetics <note>The followers of Aristotle, who held specific views on the elements and the "sublunary" sphere.</note>) blows not only in the lowest region of the air, but also in the middle and highest; indeed, more so in its very center than in its lower part, inasmuch as it drives and moves clouds of every condition before it. Furthermore, we see that clouds gathered by the winds are filled with demons, whose aerial or external force creates noise, while their internal force produces lightning; for the manifest part of demons is air, but their hidden part is fire—hence arises the "marrow" or essence of thunder. 

In the highest region of the air, where the fiery element holds its dominion, the wind blows, but not so violently, because it finds less resistance there due to the thinness of the element and the company of the demons dwelling there. These demons, on account of their sharpness, have dominion over the coarser demons—namely the watery and earthly ones—and they mix with them and wage war, whereas conversely, the watery demons rarely ascend beyond the middle region of the air (where they wage war with those contrary to them). From this it happens that we see comets generated in this region of the air, which are produced from the denser part of that region, or from a more thickened fiery spirit, just as we observe clouds created from the condensation of air in the middle region. This gathering of aerial parts, in both the middle and highest regions, is usually caused by the various blowing of the winds; but they differ in color according to the disposition of the region and its demons, whether watery, aerial, or fiery. 

Indeed (to now reveal a great mystery), just as clouds and all other meteors (which are called "imperfectly mixed" by philosophers) are formed by the opposite or contrary blowing of the winds, coagulating and condensing the air by gathering it—in which the condensed air is the body, the wind is the spirit, and the soul driving it, carried immediately in the spirit, is a demon or angel—so also it must be understood and gathered that all "perfectly mixed" compounds, which are constituted from meteors or "imperfectly mixed" things, have the same internal agents and patients. Namely: the wind, which is composed of subtle air and angelic light or brightness, either hidden in the belly of the cloud and serving like a soul driving its spirit and body, or appearing openly and visibly leaping out of the cloud. 

From this it happens that infinite compounds are found in the nature of things, each of which has contrary natures and properties different from one another within itself. This is because that wind—the primary seed producing the visible thing by the power of the Word—is perfected and mixed by the blowing of opposite and side-by-side winds. The "sperma" or external part of this is visibly condensed air, but the "semen" (which is its invisible internal part) is born from various demons and spirits, and consequently of various natures and properties. 

For example, in opium or the juice of the poppy, we perceive a bitter nature which partakes of bile or fire, yet its "anodyne" <note>Pain-relieving or numbing.</note> disposition is contrary to heat and fire, as it stupefies, takes away sensation, and induces a deadly and deep sleep. From this it follows that the Northern blast prevails in the composition of that meteor. Similarly, we observe Fumitory to be cold and dry in its operation, and yet we gather that it is bitter to the taste; thus we see the spirits of different winds or elements are within it. Here also proceeds the mystery of that property of a thing which is called "occult," namely from those internal demonic forms which, due to the various mixing of winds in the composition of the meteor, seem more hidden and inscrutable. 

The Kabbalist seems to confirm this in these words: 
<margin>Reuchlin in *On the Art of the Kabbalah*.</margin> 
*An angel is like a middle power between God and nature, from which operations are performed in things which their nature either would not do, or would do in such a way that some say they come from an occult property, and others because it is simply so.* 

From this (I say) comes the reason for the sympathies and antipathies of things, with the air as the mediator. We conclude, therefore, that from the blowing of the four winds, all things are made that are in the heavens and the earth. For the first author is God himself, who acts diversely in this world; and according to his various properties in acting, various names are attributed to him—not essential names, but taken from his properties. For although many names are said of God, none is truly proper to him except the *Tetragrammaton* <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note>, as Rabbi Moses <note>Maimonides.</note> testifies, as it denotes the substance of the Creator in a pure signification in which there is no participation. But his other names denote a thing with participation, by reason or respect of the works or actions effected by him in creation. 

Thus he is called *Adonai* <note>Lord</note> from his dominion, and consequently the cause of glory and honor; he is also called *Ehies* <note>I Am / Ehyeh</note> as a father, or *Cheten* <note>Keter</note> as a crown. And *Hochmah* <note>Chokhmah</note> i.e., wisdom; and *Bina* <note>Binah</note> i.e., prudence; and *Chesed* i.e., mercy; and *Geburath* <note>Gevurah</note>, that is punishment; and *Tiphereth* which is grace; and *Netreth* <note>Netzach</note> which is Triumph; and *Hod* i.e., praise; and *Iesod* <note>Yesod</note> that is redemption; and *Malchad* <note>Malkuth</note> which is the kingdom. From this it is clear that these are, as it were, his surnames, which are ascribed to him in respect of those actions by which he works here in the world. 

And through the first of these attributes, namely *Cheten* (the Crown), God rains down his will immediately into the orders of the Seraphim angels, who commit the matter to the Archangel Metattron <note>Metatron</note>. Since he is the primary prince, he pours his influence into the *Primum Mobile* <note>The "First Moved" sphere of the heavens.</note>, from which he rains down the material essence of things—that is, the universal water—by the command of the Crown. 

His second name with participation is *Hochma*, that is wisdom, which pours its will into the sphere of the Cherubim angels, whose influence the Archangel Jophiel receives. He transfers its commands into the starry heaven as that formal essence, and thus gives life to every creature. 

The third is *Binah* or prudence, which sends its power into the heaven of the Thrones; they commit the will of prudence to the Archangel Zaphkiel, and he faithfully commends it here to the angels or demons of the heaven of Saturn. These, by the power of the lower spirits with the air as a mediator (moved here and there by them), carry out the final execution of the will of Binah, whether it be for good or for evil. 

The fourth is *Chesed*, that is Mercy, which sends its decree into the sphere of the Dominations; and these again commend it to the Archangel Zadkiel, who, transferring it into the heaven of Jupiter, causes it to be rained down fatally into the lower things by its spirits, where it is produced into action by the Demons swimming in the winds, according to God's pleasure—

Furthermore, Jupiter and Venus preside over the collateral western winds: whence Zadkiel and Hanael have power in the winds of that quarter, but the Prince of the place is Raphael; similarly, Jupiter and Mars look toward the South, no differently than she <note>Venus</note> and Saturn, its opposite, whence Uriel, who has the nature of Samael, is for the dominion of Jupiter on the part of the west, namely where the West Wind <note>original: "Zephyrus"</note> blows; similarly, the Moon and Saturn possess the north: whence Gabriel, who is the presiding officer of the lunar land, and Zaphkiel, who is the lord of the Saturnine land, preside over this Cardinal point; however, the governance of Hanael, the Angel of Venus, ought to be in that part where the West Wind <note>original: "Favonius"</note> blows and breathes, and inclines more toward the North, for Raphael (who is the angel of Mercury) holds the equinoctial point or cardinal direction in the west. Similarly, the dominion of the Angel of the Moon is between the western humidity and the Northern cold, where the North-West wind <note>original: "corus"</note> blows, just as the force of the Angels of Saturn is between the dryness of the east and the northern cold, that is, where the North wind <note>original: "Boreas" or "Aquilo"</note> blows, so that the Arctic pole participates in the nature of both, whence that Cardinal point produces both snows and hail. # On Mystical Anatomy.

Indeed, the empire of the winds is so vast that it extends even to the underworld; for Phlegeton <note>The river of fire</note>, which is the burning river therein, is infested by the East wind; Cocytus by the West; and Styx by the North—for just as Phlegeton burns with fire, so Styx is stiff with cold—and Acheron is subject to the South wind. Therefore, Phlegmatic diseases receive their nourishment or fuel from the South, Melancholic from the North, Choleric from the East, and mixed diseases arise from collateral winds (those situated between the Cardinals) or from contrary winds clashing into a single atmospheric phenomenon. 

From this, it is explained clearly enough (as it seems to me) how absurd are the opinions of the Pagan physicians, who wish the cause of this or that disease to be phlegm, bile, or melancholy. They make their disciples—who think only superficially—believe that if such humors are removed by purges, bloodletting, or sweating agents, the force of the disease will immediately cease. Thus they are led into extreme error; for those instructed by manifold experience are warned that even when the aforesaid humors are removed, the disease may worsen in the manner previously shown. For it is not the humor itself, but the **wind** within that humor, and a spirit—either a malignant light or an insane demon lurking in that wind—which remains even after the phlegm, bile, or melancholy is purged. It contracts itself into an internally hidden particle and joins with the spirit of the blood so that it cannot be eradicated without an "occult cure." 

This species of cure is performed either by vegetables, animals, or minerals constructed and created in the opposite "blast" (and consequently by spirits contrary to the author of the disease), or it is completed by the operation of a planet and its angel. This angel opposes that specific angel whose subject spirits harm the sick and afflict men with disease. The ancient sages were skilled in this kind of cure by means of seals, characters, and incantations—or words uttered in a fitting manner—with which they attempted to restore the sick to their former health, as may be seen in pestilential diseases, Epilepsy, Paralysis, hypochondriac wind, and others of this sort, which we shall discuss more copiously, God willing, in the following second section. 

For here I only wish the reader to be warned that Epilepsy is not to be treated solely by purges and vomiting of phlegm; practice teaches us these avail little or nothing. The nature of the spirit lurking in the body is such that it converts all nourishment into the humor most convenient to it, once it has gained dominion over the natural spirit of man. We see this also in pestilential fevers and other intermittent fevers: if thick phlegm and putrid humor are evacuated today by vomiting or purging, yet tomorrow we find the stomach just as full of putrid humors as if nothing had been removed the day before. Nor is the disease mitigated by such purging for the most part, except at its very beginning, while the malignant spirit introduced through nourishment still remains in the stomach and has not yet been dispersed through the spirit of the blood. At that time, it can happen that by removing the humor of the nourishment in which that spirit or malignant wind lurks, it may be ejected from the body with and in the humor (which is its receptacle). But more on these things below.

### CHAPTER IV.

#### Concerning moist atmospheric phenomena excited by the blast of the Liver or the microcosmic South, and that the Angel blowing from the South has dominion over it, to conduct its blasts either toward health or toward morbid imbalance.

The spirit now breathes me toward the Antarctic pole of the microcosm <note>The lower part of the human body</note> and turns the breath of my discourse there. Just as it is opposed to the Arctic position, so it is adverse to it in nature and disposition. Hence it happens that one wind usually cures and moderates the imbalances of another; for Northern winds are said to make the air (disturbed by the South) level and clear, and (as Isidore <note>Isidore of Seville, an influential medieval encyclopedist</note> affirms) it opposes the plague that comes from the South. Furthermore, what the North wind freezes, the South wind dissolves; and conversely, what is dissolved by the South is again thickened and hardened by the blast of the North wind. 

To take an example from the poles of the greater world <note>The Macrocosm</note>, the **Spleen** relates to the **Liver** as the North pole relates to the South: not only in site or position, but also in quality. For as the North wind is observed to be cold and dry, possessing a terrestrial complexion, so also the Spleen is of a terrestrial nature, being the receptacle of melancholy; experience testifies that it emits cold and dry vapors from its region into the microcosm. On the opposite side, we find the South of the macrocosm to be watery and phlegmatic, verging toward heat and moisture in its temperament, wherefore it emits winds of this condition—namely vaporous ones—producing perpetual rains in its imbalance. 

Do we not find the same conditions and qualities in the place of the microcosm opposite the spleen, namely the **Liver**? For if the South wind in its imbalance creates moist blasts and disperses them in the world, we sometimes experience rains arising with thunder (namely when Mars has equal dominion with Jupiter in that quarter). We also see that the Liver, by a no less similar reason, if affected by a moderate temperament, creates vapors very like mists—just as in winter time we see dense vapors or smokes created near rivers and ponds, which are then converted into dews and frosts beneficial for the vegetation of the earth. For so we read in the Holy Scriptures: <margin>Genesis 2:6</margin> *the whole earth in the beginning of the world (before any rain had fallen upon the earth) was watered* and brought to a convenient fertility, and that with no man laboring upon it. By the virtue of this temperament, Jupiter is accustomed to kindly water the earth from the South and refresh it with health-giving moisture, by which the earth becomes fruitful; hence it is said: <margin>Psalms 65:10</margin> *You have visited the earth and watered it; you greatly enrich it; the river of God is full of water.* Now, as for what kind of rains these are...

# Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book I.

<margin>Psalm 72:6 <note>The Latin text cites Psalm 71, but in English Bibles this corresponds to Psalm 72:6: "He shall come down like rain upon the mown grass."</note></margin> The prophet describes the ways in these words: *He shall descend like rain upon a fleece and like drops dripping upon the earth*, for such temperate rains or vaporous mists, penetrating into the small veins of the earth and plants, render the former rich and the latter fertile and fruitful. In exactly the same way, moist vapors and breaths of this kind, diffused into all the members of the body by means of the veins, are converted into salutary blood ordained for the nourishment of the whole. Such is the breath of the <term>Liver</term><note>original: Hepar</note> according to nature, which consists in a balanced state, being neither too hot nor too moist, but temperate. 

But if the vapors are too watery and, due to a defect of the liver's heat, become very thick (which happens when the state of the liver is hindered by cold—that is, when it turns from a warm temperament to a cold imbalance), then they are immediately condensed into stagnant waters. These produce those species of dropsy which they call <term>Anasarca</term><note>generalized swelling of the skin</note> and <term>Ascites</term><note>fluid buildup in the abdomen</note>. This is no different than how the thicker part of vaporous air, by means of winter cold—partly in the northern region and partly in the southern, due to the weakness of heat—is converted into thick and heavy rains or snow and hail. When a great quantity of these is converted into rain, the springs, rivers, lakes, and pools are filled, and floods and marshes occur on the earth, so that an entire portion of the land becomes "dropsical," and its veins swell with water instead of most fertile sap. 

Such waters in the <term>microcosm</term><note>the human body</note> generally arise just as heavy rain does in the <term>macrocosm</term><note>the universe</note>: which happens because of the meeting of two opposing winds, namely the South and the North, condensing and thickening the intervening air into a cloud through constant opposition. Nevertheless, the <term>South Wind</term><note>original: Auster</note> is predominant there, and for this reason that breath is called Southern; hence it receives coldness from the north and moisture from the south, which joined together produce a watery nature. Concerning this matter—namely the generation of clouds—a very full mention was made against the opinion of the Peripatetics in *Tract 1, Book 7, and Chapter 4 of our History of Physics*.

Furthermore, if the vapors are light and fiery, but not of an ignited nature, they generate a "hot catarrh" and acute defluxions, and this without an evident fever, yet not without a sensible hot imbalance. We see the same in the macrocosmic air from Southern blasts, and even when the <term>South-East wind</term><note>original: Euro-austro</note> blows, showers fall abundantly from the middle region of the air in the month of April, even when the earth is as yet minimally touched by the evident heat of the sun. 

But truly, if it occurs with flashing, lightning, and thunder, a Southern wind of this kind inflames the air and produces sweltering or putrid effects. So also the "Martial" or bilious lightning residing in the gallbladder of the microcosm flies out from the hepatic region with dry vapor; it dries and corrupts the intermediate air flowing in the stomach and viscera, and in this way induces putrid fevers with rumbling and belching. Indeed, it procreates those true <term>Apostemes</term><note>abscesses or swellings</note> which are called phlegmons and carbuncles, arising here and there from excessive phlegm condensed by the blast, with the fiery nature enclosed within it reduced to purulence. 

But if this southern breath is governed by the Dog-star and its demon, and especially by Mars and his Angel <term>Samael</term>—or to speak with the Holy Scriptures: by the *Prince of the power of the air* <margin>Paul to the Ephesians <note>Ephesians 2:2</note></margin>, whom the Magi call <term>Meurim</term>, that is, the midday demon or the spirit sweltering and raging at noon—then this wind is very subtle and more dry than moist, and of the nature of the element of fire. Such is the South-East wind of which Moses speaks: *Behold, seven ears of corn, thin and blasted by the East wind* <margin>Genesis 41:6</margin>. Breaths of this kind give birth to fiery meteors, such as comets, glowing spears, etc. To these, in the lesser world <note>the human body</note>, correspond the Plague and the <term>petechial</term><note>spotted</note> or pestilential fever, which is said to spring from a most subtle and hot wind (similar to that which blows in the fiery element). 

And from this it also happens that when such meteors appear in the highest region of the air, famine, plague, and epidemic diseases usually follow. The reason is ready at hand: namely, because fiery demons, malignant by nature, are now rendered free and strong by the blast of the sweltering wind (for fiery spirits avoid Northern winds, just as cold and watery spirits resist the blasts of the East or South winds). Being freed from the prison of Aeolus <note>the mythical keeper of the winds</note>, they contaminate the air with their breath and scatter the seeds of their contagion—indeed, they scatter themselves everywhere in the air. They mix themselves with the spirit, either by means of the juice of nourishment drawn into the stomach (and then the diseases are usually very acute and last longer before they bring death, occurring with extreme sensation or labor), or by means of the air drawn through inspiration into the left chamber of the heart. In the latter case, even while the sick feel almost nothing and seem well enough in the judgment of those standing by, <term>Petechiae</term><note>purple or red spots on the skin</note> nevertheless appear, and they die of a sudden plague. For in this case, the heart and the spirit enclosed in the arteries are contaminated by the poisonous breath of these demons; and thus, even with the natural parts untouched, they perish miserably and almost without knowing it, and that right away. The appearing spots proceed not only from the orifices of the veins, but also from those of the arteries, which are evident signs of the infection of the vital spirits. 

Therefore, the cause of pestilential and acute fevers are fiery demons enclosed in very light and dry winds. For in truth, since man is the son of the world, it is necessary that he participate in the paternal members and be sustained by them; indeed, that the parts (which man received from his father <note>the Macrocosm</note>) should perform the same offices in man as they do in his father. Therefore, the North wind blows, and the South wind blows in the world by the power of spirits; so also a wind breathes in man by means of a worldly demon, leading either to disease or to health. Thus the worldly wind is not divided from the human wind, but they are, as it were, continuous with one another. Whence the demons having dominion over the winds of the world are simultaneously presiding over and present within the winds of the microcosm. For such spiritual forms in the air are so infinite that they are like infinite little fish swimming in the great sea; for by the Philosophers, and indeed by the Holy Scriptures, the spirit of the world is considered a great sea. If a portion of it is contracted into a cloud, these spirits also contract themselves, and with the cloud they show themselves visible in the form of lightning. 

For these demons are like bright forms which, according to the nature of the wind, drive the passive air at their will. Whence it is observed that cloud meets cloud, and with a certain crash one collides with another, from which thunder is heard; this happens because of the struggle of different troops or crowds of spirits of diverse natures. # On Mystical Anatomy.
## S 3
<note>The signature "S 3" indicates the position of this leaf in the printed gathering of the book.</note>

...of which some are pure, others capable of grace and mercy, others are foul and harmful, tempters both lingering and flying in the air. But truly, how these diabolical spirits, moving in the sea of the world, mix themselves with the human spirit, Artephius <note>A medieval alchemist often cited in Hermetic texts.</note> teaches us in *The Major Key of Wisdom*, where he says: *there are certain infirmities in which the devil joins himself to a humor departing from its proper temperament and disturbing health itself; and this happens most especially in infirmities arising from choler <note>Yellow bile, associated with fire, heat, and dryness.</note>, the cause of which is this: because the cause of choler itself is hot and dry, like fire, while the substance of the Devil is composed of two things—namely fire, which is his hidden part or form, and air, which is his manifest part or body. Whence it happens that in a disease of choler, the Devil is easily present and mixes himself with the bile, from which it follows that his malice increases daily until the soul departs from the body.* Thus he spoke, as if he had said that a wind or malignant fiery spirit is most easily joined with its like, and by its burning malice destroys the temperament of the bodily fabric. For bile is nothing other than fiery air condensed by a wind like the East Wind <note>original: "Euro"</note>, in which that wind also dwells with its hidden good spirits, so long as they are kept within the limits of health; but truly, if an evil spirit or burning demon mixes itself with it, it immediately becomes raging, and straightway flies beyond the margins of health, and the body burns with a Phaethontic fire <note>A reference to Phaethon, who nearly burned the earth by losing control of the Sun's chariot.</note>, and dries up with decay and parching heat.

I am able in this place to declare the various effects of the blasts of opposing winds: namely the North and South, that is, of the Spleen and the Liver; the East and West, that is, of the heart and the spermatic vessels, as well as the viscera; the Southeast and Northwest <note>original: "Iuri & Cori"</note>, or the right Hypochondrium and the left spermatic vessels, as well as the flanks; the North-northeast and Southwest <note>original: "Aquilonis & Africæ"</note>, that is, the left hypochondrium, and the right spermatic vessels and the colon. Moreover, the stomach is like a common medium through which these contrary winds blow, and by blowing they procreate "meteors" <note>In this context, "meteors" refers to internal bodily phenomena like vapors or inflammations, mirroring atmospheric weather.</note> of diverse conditions, so that their effects tend as much toward infirmity as toward health. For the Boreal wind <note>The North Wind.</note>, which is cold and dry, meeting the Auster <note>The South Wind.</note>, which is hot and moist, produces sperm and blood in the microcosm (or clouds and thick air in the macrocosm), and they make mixtures from such things; and the complexion will be tending or verging more toward that quarter which has dominion in the region of the air—that is, whichever is seen to blow more strongly and with excellence. For example, if the South Wind prevails, it makes a disposition more moist and verging toward false or burnt phlegm; if the North, then it renders the nature of the sperm or cloud inclined toward a drier and colder blast, but mixed with a certain moisture, which is all the more viscous, icy, or glassy, the greater the force and virtue the North wind has over the South. And so the matter also holds in the human world. Thus, various degrees of this complexion are observed to arise from the opposition of these two winds, according to the greater or lesser dominion of one over the other. Whence it arises that if demons or depraved spirits of a suppressed wind invade the spirit of the wind exulting at birth, and have dominion over the natural spirit of the one born, then indeed they convert that natural habit—convenient for a healthy life—into a morbid disposition which physicians call "preternatural." Do we not see this same thing happen in the air of the world? Namely, when sometimes the Boreal or Northern wind or the Northwest wind drive clouds from the North toward the South, and in the opposite point of the horizon one sees the contrary South wind. We see the clouds—the vehicles or chariots of contrary demons—carried and driven by a violent motion against the clouds and blasts of the Boreal wind predominating in the hemisphere; whence the air, which a little before was peaceful enough and not covered by storms and great clouds, is now suddenly disturbed by darkness, thunder, and lightning, and the entire nature of the hemisphere seems to be disturbed preternaturally and to fall ill. We say, therefore, that the natural state of the winds in the composition of the sperm—or rather in the time when that air is attracted through inhalation, which is afterwards converted into seed—will be the disposition of the one born, according to nature while he lives here; and that every wind contrary to this disposition will weigh down the spirit of the one born, and will struggle with it no differently than a wind with its opposite in the greater world; and in these winds are demons, who are accustomed to move them for and against. We could bring forth infinite demonstrations of these things here, but a fuller discourse on this matter is destined for the second section. But truly, I will say now in a single word, that the truth of this matter is proven by the effect; for the nature of the Northern wind (as was said before) is accustomed to cure the unhealthy effects of the South wind's blasts, to correct its putrid breath, to dry its dampness, to moderate its heat with cold, and whatever the latter has attempted to dissolve, the former immediately binds and congeals with a contrary breath. And so the matter holds in the blasts of the spleen and liver in the lesser world <note>The human body.</note>. Furthermore, because the natural spirit of the one born is on the side of the predominating wind, therefore if some demon of the opposite wind inhabits him, it vexes him and strongly attacks his demons; and hence it is that if anyone is affected by Epilepsy, that malignant spirit is observed to afflict the human spirit more when that wind blows from whose governance and society it belongs. Hence also it is, that in a time of plague many escape untouched—that is, those whose natural spirit is of the nature of the wind bringing the disease: since with them the harmful demons are familiar. Just so was that woman (according to Galen's history) who from her infancy was accustomed to drink the juice of Hemlock, and at last could not be intoxicated by it, even though all men feel the madness of the contrary blasts of these pestiferous demons even unto their last breath. But let us proceed to the matter: the East wind <note>original: "subsolanus"</note> also, which blows against the West wind <note>original: "Fauonium"</note>, is hot, dry, and fiery, but in a temperate manner, because the Boreal coldness mitigates its intense heat, and the Southern moisture moderates its fiery dryness; whence the Angel of the Sun, namely Michael, has principal dominion over this quarter, who is the giver of life. This is most rightly accommodated to the spirit of life, since it consists in an equality between the extreme coldness in the North and the moisture in the South; and this is the reason why, according to the annotation of Tedacus Levi, the Angel Michael who rules that quarter is on the side of clemency and mercies, and the Sun, over which Michael presides, is the source of life, as all philosophers testify; for also its...

The wind that is opposite also tempers the hot blasts sent forth from this region, over which **Raphael** (which means "the medicine of God") presides. For the heat and dryness of the East embrace the coldness tempered with the moisture of the West; from this, a sanguine and healthy temperament and constitution is produced in the "aerial seed." Therefore, **Michael** breathes the innate heat from his solar kingdom in the East, and **Raphael**, as the messenger of Jupiter, breathes the radical moisture from the West. However, from the temperament of the **North Wind** <note>original: "Boreas"</note> and the **South Wind** <note>original: "Auster"</note>, a morbid constitution arises, because the Angels of these regions act severely upon the intervening air. Consequently, the "seed" is mostly distant from the health of life because of the unnatural war waged between these two winds. It is worth noting that whichever wind holds dominion over its opposite will have the prerogative and priority in the complexion of the person born. For example, if the North Wind prevails over the South, the complexion will be more cold and dry, or **Melancholic**; if the South Wind prevails, it will be more phlegmatic and watery. If the East Wind prevails over the West, it will be more hot and dry, or vice versa, moderately cold or moist and spring-like. Furthermore, among the side-winds, if the **South-West Wind** <note>original: "Africus"</note> blows more strongly than the **North-East Wind** <note>original: "Aquilo"</note> opposite it, the complexion will be tempered more by moisture than dryness, yet the coldness of the North-East moderates the Southern heat of the South-West; this complexion approaches the nature of Jupiter somewhat. But if the blast of the North-East prevails, the complexion will be more dry and cold than hot and moist, and this kind of complexion often produces melancholy from "burnt phlegm." Similarly, the **South-East Wind** <note>original: "Euro-auster"</note> blowing against the **North-West Wind** <note>original: "Corus"</note> and holding dominion produces a **Choleric** nature, which, because of the opposing blasts of the North-West, frequently produces bilious diseases. But if the North-West Wind is dominant, it procreates burnt bile and melancholy.

# On Mystical Anatomy.

In the macrocosm <note>the universe</note> there is cloud and vapor, ordained to sustain the life of animals and plants, just as blood and sperm exist in the microcosm <note>the human being</note>; consequently, the flesh and the fetus procreated from them are subject to the assaults of contrary winds. From this, therefore, arise diseases and passions of both body and mind, just as, conversely, when a naturally behaving wind blows, animals are refreshed and usually recover. And hence was the observation of Hippocrates and Galen <note>famous ancient Greek physicians</note> concerning the winds; instructed by the outcome according to their blowing, they predicted such future diseases, although they nevertheless remained ignorant of the internal reasons or causes of these diseases and winds.

### CHAPTER V.

#### How God is the prince of spirits, and that the various properties of angelic spirits depend on the various names of God and the properties of His actions in this world. Testimonies concerning the breathing or action of demons or spirits, both good and evil, in both the macrocosm and microcosm. And finally, the rationale for the supernatural meteors of both worlds is explained.

**A**s God is a living spirit (from *spirando*, "breathing"), so He Himself breathes life and essence into His spirits. Insofar as He is God, having dominion both in the light (whence He is called the "Revealed God" and the "Luminous Aleph" <note>Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, used here to represent the First Cause</note>) and in the darkness (as the "Hidden God" and the "Dark Aleph"), He is God breathing through the latter toward generation and life, as well as toward health—both temporal and eternal, which is called salvation—just as through the former He breathes toward the infirmity, deprivation, and languor of creatures. 

In His latter property, therefore, He is called by the wise men and Hebrew Rabbis *Chesed*, that is, Mercy, over which presides the name of God full of kindness, *El*; and *Tiphereth*, or Grace, in respect to which property He is called *Eloah*. The first of these titles precedes the commission of error or sin—namely, the Mercy which was always with God before any time—furthermore, it is also called *Iesod*, that is, Redemption, over which presides the name *Shaddai*, by which the effect of divine mercy and grace is proven, and this latter is brought into effect after the commission of sin. 

But indeed, in the first property He is called *Geburah*, that is, Punishment, over which presides *Elohim Gibor*, proving severity. And also *Netzach* or Triumph, and *Malchut*, that is, Kingdom. Whence through the first He avenges Himself upon His enemies or rebels; through the second, having gained victory, He fixes the trophy of His victory; and through the last, having conquered the malignant spirits, He reigns forever and ever over His subjects or creatures. 

Just as He is a spirit flourishing in the darkness, so He hides His face from creatures, and then, because of the absence of that face, there breathe from the region of darkness blasts of infirmity and death or deprivation; but indeed, when He shows His face, health and life are restored, according to that saying of the Prophet: <margin>Psalm 104:29</margin> *When God hides His face, the creatures are troubled; when He sends forth His spirit, they breathe again.* But this has been so from the beginning of the world; namely, we prove the divine breathing in the world and in creatures, both toward life and toward death, and toward health as well as toward disease, by instances from the Bible in the following order of facts, and first I shall begin with the testimonies of the blessed, merciful, and benevolent breath.

First, as for the creation of the world, the spirit of the Lord (which is named from breathing) was carried over the waters, giving form to the shapeless substance of the black abyss; so also for the fabrication of the microcosm, after its exterior was fashioned from the dust of the earth, He breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, by which man was made a living soul. That this spirit always remains until the disjunction of body and soul, and breathes the function of life into him, is clear from what follows: <margin>Gen. 6:3</margin> *For God said, My spirit shall not remain in men forever, for his days are 120.* Nor indeed was this divine wind in man alone, but also in all other creatures, wherefore God said elsewhere: <margin>Gen. 6:17</margin> *I will cause a flood of waters to come upon the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the vital spirit under heaven; whatever is on the earth shall expire.* And elsewhere it is written: <margin>Wisdom 12</margin> *The incorruptible spirit of God is in all things.* Whence also Solomon said elsewhere: <margin>Eccles. 3:19</margin> *The spirit of man and of beast and their end are the same; as this one dies, so dies that one.* But the whole is confirmed in this: <margin>Wisdom 1</margin> *The spirit of the Lord fills the whole world.* 

That this spirit in the world is sometimes good and sometimes evil toward us (although in truth it is always the same and permanent, though it is accustomed to blow where it wills) may be gathered from many places of Holy Scripture, according to that: <margin>Ecclus. 11:14</margin> *Good and evil, life and death, honor and poverty are from God.* In the better sense, it is called the "breath of life," with which God adorned both the macrocosm and the microcosm. I say the macrocosm, whence it is said: <margin>Job 26</margin> *God created heaven and earth by His uncreated spirit, and the spirit of the Lord filled the whole world*; and the microcosm, as into which God breathed the breath of life. And by the grace of this spirit it is said: <margin>Wisdom 1</margin> *that God created all things that they might exist, and made the nations of the earth healthy*; whence David also said: <margin>Psalm 23:3</margin> *God makes my soul quiet; I cried to You and You healed me, and brought me up from hell.* And elsewhere: <margin>Psalm 104:29</margin> *When God sends forth His spirit, His creatures are refreshed.* And elsewhere: <margin>Psalm 90:14</margin> *Prolongation of life is the kindness of God.* And elsewhere: <margin>Prov. 3</margin> *Through the spirit of wisdom days are multiplied, and years of life are added to man.* And the royal prophet speaks thus: <margin>Psalm 18:24</margin> *If You light my lamp, O Jehovah my God, You make my darkness shining.* In Job we also read: <margin>Job 10:12</margin> *Your visitation has preserved my spirit.* And David says: <margin>Psalm 106</margin> *He whom God has visited with His salvation shall enjoy good.* 

But indeed, in the worse sense, this is called the evil spirit of God, whence the wise man said: <margin>Wisdom 11:21</margin> *Since they can fall even by a single breath from pursuing justice, and be winnowed by the spirit of Your power.* And elsewhere: <margin>Wisdom 5:24</margin> *A spirit of power and a spirit of virtue shall stand against the impious, and like a storm and a whirlwind it shall cast them away.* Furthermore, it is said elsewhere that <margin>1 Sam. 16:15</margin> *the spirit of Jehovah had departed from Saul, and an evil spirit of God, or an evil spirit from Jehovah, troubled him*; similarly, the Devil struck Job with a most grievous ulcer, whence he himself cried out: <margin>Job 16:23</margin> *My spirit is corrupted, my days are extinguished.* And elsewhere he says: <margin>Job 30:22</margin> *You lift me up into the wind, You set me upon it, and You cause my substance to dissolve.* And elsewhere, God speaks in rebuke through pain upon the bed: <margin>Job 33:19</margin> Whence it is clear that God...

Similarly, although it is said in the same chapter <margin>Exodus 12:29</margin> that the destroyer of the Lord struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, yet afterward we read in it: *And it came to pass at midnight that Jehovah struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt.* Where the ordainer and prime mover is taken for the executor and the one moving immediately into action—that is, God is taken for his minister. Moreover, it has been said elsewhere that an angel or demon is a spirit, and that a spirit is a wind, and that a wind of this kind works in the air. And here the movement of spirits, both malignant and good, occurs in the air either manifestly or by a secret breathing. For the Devil used a breathing both manifest and tempestuous to execute the will of God against Job. Whence it was said: *The fire of God fell upon the cattle and the servants and consumed them,* where he speaks of thunder and lightning; and afterward: *A great wind came from the region of the desert, which, striking the four corners of the house, collapsed it upon the children.* Whence in the first assault the Devil, to whom dominion in the air is given, mingles himself with the lightning or thunderbolt and the storm to execute the will of God; and in the last, he disturbs the air and becomes as it were the soul to the violent wind, moving the air impetuously before him. From this it is also clear that the Devil does not know how to move unless he is moved by God, for he himself acknowledges: *Thy actions are the works of the hands of God.* Whence Satan said: *But put forth thy hand now, I pray, and touch all that he has, unless he curse thee to thy face.* And Jehovah answered Satan: *Behold, all that he has is in thy hand,* as if he had said: "Make my commands my own," etc. Furthermore, the Devil sometimes works by a secret breathing. And by this kind of secret breath of his, he moved the spirits of the Sabean people so that they might strike Job’s servants with the edge of the sword, and that the Chaldeans might rush upon Job’s camels to capture them and kill his servants with the sword—who, before this kind of breath or secret motion, did not dare to attempt such a thing against Job. So also God said: <margin>2 Kings 19:7</margin> *Behold, I will put a spirit in him, so that having heard a rumor he may return to his own land.* Such also was the lying spirit which Jehovah <margin>2 Kings 22</margin> put into the mouth of all the prophets of King Ahab. And an evil spirit from God troubled Saul; which indeed was done by <margin>1 Samuel 16</margin> divine permission. For the nature of the human spirit is so close to that of these aerial demons that a demon very easily joins itself with it, seduces it, and draws it where it wishes, unless God defends the spirit of man <margin>Job 1:10</margin> against their insults; whence Satan says to Jehovah: *Hast thou not hedged him in, and his house, and all that he has on every side?* etc. <margin>1 Kings 18</margin> Furthermore, the good spirit or angel also works in the air by a breathing both manifest <margin>2 Kings 2:17</margin> and secret. For so Elisha says to Elijah: *The spirit of Jehovah shall carry thee away I know not where.* Similarly: *Let us see lest perhaps the spirit of Jehovah has taken him up.* And in the history of Daniel we read that the angel of the Lord (who is also called wind and spirit) took Habakkuk by the crown of his head and carried him to Babylon. That an angel is a formal wind has been said clearly enough in <margin>Acts</margin> the preceding pages. Similarly, after the Eunuch was baptized, Philip was transported through the air by the spirit, <margin>Matthew 4:1</margin> just as Christ was led by the spirit into the desert for the sake of being tempted. Similarly, he saw the spirit of God descending like a <margin>Matthew 3</margin> dove and resting upon him. Finally, the same spirit breathes secretly into the spirit of man and inspires him with divinity; <margin>2 Samuel 18</margin> whence Samuel says: *The spirit of Jehovah spoke in me.* So also it was said that the spirit of Jehovah was in Joseph, <margin>Genesis 1:38</margin> and elsewhere, that Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom, and elsewhere, *The spirit of Jehovah began to be with Samson in the camp of Dan, and the Lord blessed him.* <margin>Deuteronomy 34:9</margin> Similarly, Jehovah stirred up the spirit of Cyrus the king. <margin>Judges 13:25</margin> But now at last we shall show how the spirit <margin>2 Chronicles 36</margin> naturally enclosed in human blood suffers passions both good and evil, according to the approaches of preternatural good or evil spirits to it. As far as the passions of good spirits are concerned, we read first: *My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my savior,* <margin>Psalm 106</margin> that is, my spirit delights and is exalted in the spirit of God. And elsewhere: *Whom God shall visit with his salvation shall enjoy good.* And elsewhere: <margin>Psalm 65:8</margin> *Bless our God, O peoples, who has restored our soul to life.* And elsewhere: *The soul of the righteous is lifted up to God.* <margin>Psalm 25:1</margin> And elsewhere: *My soul rejoices in God.* And elsewhere: *Make my spirit glad.* And elsewhere: *Return, my soul, to thy rest, for Jehovah has been <margin>Psalm 33</margin> beneficial toward thee.* And elsewhere: *I lift up my soul to thee.* And elsewhere: *There was no more spirit in the Queen of Sheba.* <margin>Psalm 116:7</margin> Where "soul" is understood for the "bloody spirit" <note>the vital spirit residing in the blood</note> in which life exists, all of which passions are inspired <margin>1 Kings 10</margin> by the good breathings of the spirits of God; in which passions the heart is said to be dilated, as we shall declare more clearly in what follows. <margin>Psalm 142:4</margin> Furthermore, the human spirit is also afflicted with preternatural passions by means of the evil spirits of God. <margin>Psalm 143:7</margin> In such a sense King David speaks: *My spirit overwhelmed itself within me.* And elsewhere: *My spirit is consumed within me.* So also <margin>Job 21:4</margin> Job said: *My spirit is narrowed.* And elsewhere he says: *The poison of the arrows of the Almighty drinks up my spirit.* And elsewhere: <margin>Job 6:4</margin> *My spirit is corrupted, my days are extinguished.* And Christ said: *My soul is sorrowful even unto death.* And Job says <margin>Job 16:23</margin> that a fool tears his soul or spirit in his fury. And elsewhere: *God softens the soul of the impious and disturbs him.* And elsewhere: <margin>Matthew 26:38</margin> *My soul is affected with bitterness.* Furthermore, it is said in the same sense: *That the impious man turns his spirit against the mighty God.* <margin>Job 18:4</margin> In which way it is also said: *That God hardened the heart of Pharaoh.* And he also hardens the spirits of men <margin>Job 23:16</margin> according to his pleasure. Finally, an evil spirit of Jehovah is said to have vexed the spirit of Saul; all of which passions of the soul <margin>2 Kings 4</margin> are to be taken in a worse sense, as those which happen from a malignant spirit of God to the spirit of life in man. <margin>Job 15</margin> <margin>Deuteronomy 2:29</margin> <margin>1 Samuel 16</margin>

There is also another state of the soul, which is more moderate, closer to the internal being, and devoted to the human will. And in this manner Job said: <margin>Job 19:17, Job 15</margin> *My spirit has become a stranger to my wife*; and in this sense the saying is understood, *the impious man turns his spirit against the mighty God.* Sometimes "spirit" is also taken in the abstract and not in the concrete, and so it is written: <margin>1 Sam. 28, Wisdom 16</margin> *The spirit of Samuel ascended from the earth*, and addresses Saul; and elsewhere, *Man knows not how to bring back the spirit once it has departed from the body.* And so we gather the infinite actions of breathing and their various effects in the microcosm <note>The human being as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>, all of which certainly proceed from the properties of the macrocosmic winds, or the natures of the divine breaths and their effects. Although it is most difficult for man to explain all these things (according to the word of the wise man: <margin>Eccles. 11:5</margin> *Man knows not the way of the spirit, just as he knows not how the bones grow in the womb of a pregnant woman: so he knows not the work of God himself, by what way He makes all these things*), it is nevertheless very easy to draw from the sacred fountain that God is the source of the winds and meteors <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, wind, and lightning.</note>, both natural and supernatural. His breathing ministers are the angels themselves, to whom are subjected infinite legions of demons—both good for doing good, and evil for doing harm and punishing. These angels breathe the commands of God into the heavens, the elements, and the earth. A certain angelic intelligence presides over every quarter of the world and its cardinal wind. By means of the impulse of the winds (which derive their strength from the angelic spirit), meteors—fiery, airy, watery, and earthy—are produced in the world. These meteors bring alterations to the microcosm, some favorable to health and generation, others leading to disease and corruption. The flows of the microcosmic spirit follow the pattern of those in the macrocosm, both in the procreation of natural meteors and the production of supernatural ones. The origin and beginning of all these breathings proceed from the blast of the spirit of the nostrils of Jehovah <note>original: "flatu spiritus nasi Iehouæ"</note>, as the Prophet Samuel testifies, speaking these words: <margin>2 Sam. 22:8</margin> *And the earth is shaken and moved, the foundations of the heavens are moved; they are shaken when anger is kindled in Him, whose smoke descends through His nose, and fire from His mouth consumes, glowing coals from Him; and lowering the heaven, He descends with darkness under His feet. And He sits upon the Cherubim, and flies and is visible upon the wings of the wind, and puts around Himself huts of darkness, the blackness of waters, the densities of the upper clouds; by the splendor that is before Him, fiery coals burn; Jehovah thunders from the heavens, and the Most High utters His voice, and sends forth arrows with which He scatters the enemies, the lightning with which He routs them; and the lowest channels of the sea are seen, the foundations of the habitable world are revealed by the rebuke of Jehovah, by the blast of the spirit of His nostrils.* From which it is gathered that from the blast of the spirit of the nostrils of Jehovah in His anger, first the earthquake and the vibration and disturbance of the entire air arise. Then the winds or smoke through His nose, then afterwards the consuming or flashing fire is breathed out from His mouth, and also glowing coals or thunderbolts. Then the darkness or dense black clouds under His feet; and that God Himself, sitting upon the Cherubim or His aerial angels, flies in and upon the wings of the wind. The black clouds arising from the smoke in His nostrils surround Him, which are nothing other than the black density of the thinner air. Whence they are called "blackness" and "density of the upper waters of the clouds," that is, of the pure aerial heaven. Then He also produces thunders, with His arrows and lightning. And finally, deep chasms in the earth; from which it is clear that the primary force is attributed to the breath of Jehovah, the secondary to the Cherubim or angels upon whom He sits, and the third to the winds, which are the smoke of the nostrils of Jehovah, upon whose wings He Himself flies. Whence it is clear that the immediate power of God is in Himself, as also in His angels; and the angels are in the winds and produce the winds; the clouds contain the angels, God, and the winds or spirits of a lower nature. The winds produce clouds by thickening, and the clouds emit flashes and rains, and the flashes produce thunders which accompany the lightning; and finally, at the sight of the Lord in His fury, the heaven and earth are moved, and the foundations of the earth and sea are revealed. By these things, the degrees of progression of actions from God Himself—the Actor and Fountain of Light—are notably explained: from simplicity to those mixed compositions called "imperfectly mixed" or meteors, which are immediately converted into "perfectly mixed" things.

But here, reader, I wish to explain an admirable mystery to you: I want you to consider that man himself is nothing other than such a dense cloud in which Jehovah sits upon the Cherubim, and flies upon the wings of the wind—that is, the vital spirit—or kindly breathes the breath of life into our nostrils (whence it is said by the Prophet): <margin>Ps. 90:14, Ps. 106:4, Deut. 28</margin> *The Sun giving life and glory*; and elsewhere, *life is the prolongation of the kindness of God.* And elsewhere, *God follows His people with benevolence and His salvation.* And elsewhere, *he whom God has visited with His salvation shall enjoy good.* Or, He speaks and breathes in us in wrath and rebuke, whence it is said: *Jehovah shall make the pestilence cleave to you until you are consumed; Jehovah shall strike you with a hot and burning wasting disease.* And Job says: *You lift me up to the wind, you set me upon it, and you cause my substance to flow away*, that is, so that my corporeal cloud may be converted by dissolution into air or wind, from which it originated by thickening. We conclude, therefore, that God inspires the angels, the angels inspire the demons, the demons inform the winds, the winds produce meteors—both healthy and unhealthy. The meteors, by a certain inseparable kinship, infect the air; the air is the fodder and food of the spirits, both vital and natural, by which man is nourished. This air is continually introduced into the body, both through breathing and by means of nourishment. Once introduced, it fills the body either with good juice or with contagious seeds, according to the kindness or severity of the wind blowing from the quarters of heaven. Both qualities are derived from the properties of the names of God, which are attributed to Him from His actions in the world. For in His nature, insofar as He is *Chesed* <note>Hebrew: Loving-kindness</note> or Clemency, through the Angels Raphael and Zadkiel, He breathes health from the West or the temperate spring; as also in the nature of *Tiphareth* <note>Hebrew: Beauty/Balance</note> or Grace through the Angel Michael, He breathes the benefit of life and benevolence. But indeed, in His property of *Geburah* <note>Hebrew: Strength/Severity</note> or Punishment, through Samael and his subject Meririm, He breathes plagues and contagious diseases and burning fevers from the South. And in the disposition of *Malchut* <note>Hebrew: Kingdom</note>—that is, the kingdom and the "tree of lopping off" among the Kabbalists—through Gabriel, because (as Tedacus Levi witnesses) he proves severity in the North. Whence cold and numbing diseases are induced. But concerning these things, God willing, we shall argue effectively and clearly in the book on the causes of supernatural diseases.

The microcosmic East Wind <note>original: "Subsolanus"</note> or the Heart (for the Heart is the principle of life, just as the sun is to the day) breathes vital spirits toward the west through the Aorta; this Aorta scatters its rays laterally through small branches to the south and north. This breath of life is the wind which God breathed into Adam. The microcosmic West Wind <note>original: "Favonius"</note> breathes benevolent vapors from the seminal vessels toward the east; for the seminal vessels are most rightly likened to the western region, insofar as the seed <note>original: "sperma"</note> remains within them, which does not take on a new form nor rise again unless it first decays—just as the setting sun seems to die and be extinguished, and would not be said to rise again in the east unless it had first set. Furthermore, we shall declare below that the shining form of the seed proceeds from the Heart, just as western splendor or lightning arises from the east. Moreover, the West Wind blows a benevolent vapor from the intestines, which it sends through its twisting passages, by means of the mesenteric vessels, partly to the Liver and partly into the stomach, by which the stomach itself is lightly distended and ventilated.

The microcosmic North <note>original: "Septentrio"</note> or the Spleen, sends its dry breaths, by means of the splenic branch, to the Liver (or the South), and by means of the first and second branches of the Portal Vein <term>Porta: the "gate" or portal vein carrying blood to the liver</term> and the short vessel into the stomach, by which it is distended; there it congeals and thickens the humors. By means of the fifth branch, it sends breath into the Colon, and by the sixth into the small intestines. Hence these intestines are subject to windy diseases, namely the Colon to Colic, and the Ileum to the Iliac passion <note>a painful intestinal obstruction</note>. The South or the Liver, the source of the natural spirit, blows directly toward the North or the Spleen, and drives dark blood before it into that region, not otherwise than the macrocosmic South Wind <note>original: "Auster"</note> blows dark clouds toward the North, which the North is accustomed to dissipate and purify with a contrary breath, as Isidore <note>likely Isidore of Seville, a medieval encyclopedist</note> says. The Liver also blows its moist vapors into the stomach through the first and second portal branches, into the Omentum <note>the fatty lining of the abdomen</note> through the third (whence it sometimes produces dropsy), into the colon through the fifth, and into the small intestines through the sixth; and if a breath of this kind be dense and thick, it generates a "Hepatic flux" <note>liver-related diarrhea</note>.

The North-West Wind <note>original: "Corus"</note> participates in both the North and the West; it is produced partly from the movement of the intestines and the seminal vessels—for in widows and virgins, corrupted seed produces a "hysteric" breath <note>referring to the historical medical belief in "wandering womb" or vapors from the reproductive organs</term>—and partly from the North, on account of the flatulence exhaled into the intestines through the fifth and sixth portal branches. Because this breath blows against the South-East Wind <note>original: "Eurus"</note>—that is, toward that region where the bile has its seat—it induces Hypochondriac breaths, the Colic passion, the Iliac, and others of this kind. Due to the repercussion of the South-East Wind (or the hot and fiery vapor of the bile), it affects the Hypochondriacs with heat around the diaphragm and the viscera. ### CHAPTER VII.

### On the position of man according to the doctrine of Pythagoras, Plato, and Aristotle, and on the Cardinal winds of the same according to it.

But because this discourse of ours might perhaps seem harsh and new to someone—wherein we made the Spleen the North of the microcosm, and the Liver its opposite South—since the seat of the Heart (being above the region of the elementary world) is hardly to be believed as the beginning of the East wind. Furthermore, they may reply that I am too arrogant in this discourse of mine, daring to refute men of such fame and authority as Pythagoras, Plato, and Aristotle in their opinions, and refusing their doctrine which constitutes the Eastern quarter of the world as the right side of man. But truly, I answer those objecting in this way: that in my positioning of man in relation to the world, I have followed not my own opinion, but the sense of the written fact, as was explained in the preceding pages. And all the more because since the Spleen participates in melancholy, what can be more aptly compared to the Northern quarter in man than the Spleen, since that quarter is cold and moist <note>The author likely means cold and dry, the traditional qualities of melancholy, or is referencing a specific meteorological theory</note>, and consequently the seat of worldly melancholy? Just as the South is hot and moist, like the mass of the Liver. However, this is certain and proven by experience: that the microcosm enjoys its own quarters and cardinal winds, no differently than the macrocosm does its own, and that those cardinal winds of man are governed by the breaths of the world and are affected by health or imbalance according to their properties.

For if we were to admit the position of the microcosm in relation to the macrocosm according to the opinions of the aforementioned philosophers, we would find indeed that its cardinal points do not differ much from our aforementioned intention. Let the East, therefore, be the right side of man, and consequently his left side must be the West, the front the North, and the back the South. When it stands thus, it follows that the Liver corresponds to the Eastern quarter, the Spleen to the Western, the stomach to the Northern, and the viscera or intestines, the salt sea of the bladder, and the womb in a woman to the Southern. 

For first, the Liver (which is the source of the natural spirit conducive to life and growth) can not inaptly be compared to the rising sun, which refreshes the creatures of the earth by its sight, and tints the hemisphere and its waters and earth with its rays; and so also the liver breathes its tinted and ruddy rays, by means of the veins, into the whole body, to which it gives life and growth. Similarly, just as the East Wind <note>original: "subsolanus"</note> blows directly into the quarter of the West Wind <note>original: "Fauonii"</note>, so also the liver sends out its spirits through the Splenic branch into the Spleen (which is the quarter of the microcosm opposite to it). Furthermore, the Spleen is clearly of the nature of the west: namely, dark, cold, and slimy. Yet it contributes to life, as it is said by some to purify the thick blood and also to contribute to life and nutrition, wherefore it can be held as the Western quarter.

We can also clearly refer the stomach to the North, since in it raw, viscous, and thick matter and humors abound, and coldness has dominion in it by itself, although heat works within it because of the warmth of the surrounding organs. And hence it is that although the Liver is hot and very glowing, we nevertheless observe the stomach to be affected for the most part by cold. Furthermore, after the administration of an emetic medicine, we have noted very viscous matter, like water congealed by cold, rising and being carried upward, and this in almost everyone. From which it is argued that this part of the microcosm can not improperly be referred to the north: or if not the stomach, let us propose the very substance of the brain. For in the brain, southern vapors or those rising from the viscera are condensed into icy and viscous humors, as is evident in Epilepsy, rheum <note>original: "coriza": a cold or runny nose</note>, and other such diseases. 

Finally, we can adapt the viscera and intestines, and also the Bladder, and the womb in a woman, to the southern quarter, as from them moist vapors continually rise; indeed, we even observe storms to arise from that part, just as the clouds, whirlwinds, and thunders of the macrocosm are usually brought forth from the south by its glowing and raging spirit. Hence come the Colic and Iliac passions; hence the stones of the kidneys and bladder, compared to lightning-stones <note>prehistoric stone tools once believed to be thunderbolts</note>; hence those Diabolical diseases which are stirred up by the womb, whose habit it is to suffocate the microcosm, or to deprive it of its natural motion for some space of time, as if some malignant demon were raging from the south. Indeed, even in men, an Epileptic demon attempts to bring forth this same thing or worse, and for the most part it is distinct from the demon of the womb. Furthermore, as we see the position of the South <note>original: "Austru"</note> of the microcosm is "under the earth" <note>referring to the lower torso</note>, and consequently its breaths are carried upward, as Isidore says, so also the matter stands with this quarter.

By which things one may see that even by this position of the philosophers, the quarters of the lesser world can be quite properly adapted to those of the greater; and yet if we look at the matter with sharper eyes, some doubts are to be found even in this kind of comparison: namely, whether the nature of the stomach is cold and dry, like that of the North—
