# Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book II.

<margin>Ecclesiastes 3:19</margin> Regarding this, Solomon speaks thus: *The spirit of man and of the beast is the same; as the one dies, so dies the other.* <note>original: "Spiritus hominis & bestiæ idem est..." This refers to the "breath of life" shared by all creatures.</note> For it is the elementary spirit that dies, but truly that celestial and super-celestial spirit is immortal; it is to that elementary spirit what the soul and life are, and when it is taken away, the spirit is said to die.

I conclude, therefore, that antipathy—whether between different things or within the same subject (namely in the airy substance of both the macrocosm and the microcosm)—consists in the contrariety and opposition of natures or souls. This occurs especially where a demon or some perverse spirit hostily attacks the spirit of another. Thus also the gaze of the **Catablepha** <note>A legendary beast, likely a wildebeest or basilisk-type creature, said to kill with its look.</note>, filled with poisonous spirits, is said to kill a man from a distance; that is, the spirit within it is so malignant and contrary to the good spirit of man that it suddenly penetrates the man's external spirit expanded in the blood, infects it, absorbs his radical moisture, and forces the spirit of life to flee from the body. And yet, nonetheless, this spirit which is ruinous to man is healthful and favorable to the Catablepha. Such also is the antipathy of nature between the spirits of the wolf and the lamb, the lion and the rooster; just as, conversely, such is the principle of sympathy between the magnet and iron, gold and quicksilver <note>mercury</note>, amber and chaff. However, the leader and first fountain of Sympathy is the Word or the highest Light, which is fiery love and everlasting peace. But the origin of Antipathy is the Devil, who is also called Strife. He participates in darkness and death, while the former participates in light and eternal life. The former tends toward divination <note>or divine union</note>, just as the latter tends toward destruction and ruin. The latter is the occasion for diseases and disturbances in the creature; the former is the fountain of health and the author of restoring it to its pristine health.

### CHAPTER XI.

->On the Antipathy between the blood of one person and another. From whence it proceeds.<-

Through those things said in the preceding pages, it is manifest that there is as great a discrepancy between the sympathy and antipathy of things as there is between the consonance and dissonance of harmony. Certainly, if we look at the matter a little more accurately, we will perceive that the principle of Antipathy is the same as that of symphonic discord, and likewise for sympathy and concord. Whence it happens that between blood that is well-disposed and similar to itself, the best harmony is found. So also between healthy and poisonous blood there is a contrary relationship, and their effects are found to be hostile. For example, that blood in women is called "menstrual," which is nothing other than a superfluous part of the whole blood mass; if it be retained in the body beyond the proper time and custom, we observe it to be the cause of many sicknesses and preternatural affections. Because it sometimes seems to suffocate the principal parts, it induces cachexia <note>wasting syndrome</note>, which is followed by dropsy, frenzy, difficulty breathing, suffocation of the womb, and a universal corruption of the blood mass—

<margin>Book 10, ch. 16</margin> —follows. Indeed, there is such great poisonousness in the substance of this kind of blood that, as Isidore <note>Isidore of Seville, a medieval encyclopedist</note> testifies, growing fruits lose their greenness and power of growth by its mere touch; their natural moisture will be dried up and seem to waste away. Similarly, if herbs are contaminated by it, they immediately lose their vigor, trees cease to bear fruit, and even iron itself infected by it is destroyed by rust, and copper contracts a blackness. As for other animals, dogs eating of it become rabid; indeed, I have heard that if a portion of this blood is given to a man in a drink, it induces leprosy in him. The cause of the malignancy of this blood is a certain malignant spirit procreated in it by excessive retention; for the effects of putrefaction produce wonders, just as we see in flesh which is converted by rot into worms and innumerable tiny animals. But truly, this malignant spirit produced by such putrefaction takes on the nature of a most infested demon, since women in the suffocation of their wombs are affected no differently than if they had been disturbed by some demon. In a clearly similar way, the semen behaves in the body of either a widow or a virgin, or any other woman, and also in men who abstain from intercourse for a long time; for instead of procreating its human species, it often produces a malignant offspring, most hostile to its parents, which like a demon afflicts both sexes with epilepsy (or the falling sickness) and seeks to affect the female sex with hysterical passion or suffocation of the womb. And these demons or malignant spirits seem to be lunar, as they especially rejoice in exercising their powers and malice during the new moon and full moon, and in treating such miserable people mercilessly. For we see, by diligent observation, that just as semen contributes to the production of the essential nature of man, so also the substance of menstrual blood seems primarily to lead to the elementary subject of the body and its nutrition. From these things it is right to conclude that both concur in the generation of man: namely, the seed and its internal [part], and the semen as the beginning of the external [part], and the menstrual blood for the vegetation and augmentation of the same into the external substance or mass of the fetus. However, the place of generation of that malignant demon, both in the ill-applied spermatic mass and in that of the menstrual blood, is the sublunary part; because in the celestial part of the semen, no malignant spirit can be produced or penetrate into that region, except insofar as it pertains to its life. But in menstrual blood, there is nothing, or certainly not much, of the "fifth essence" <term>Quintessence: the purest, celestial element</term>. Whence it happens that it produces far worse effects than the semen.

As for the antipathy of different bloods or of various persons, that which takes on the nature of an evil demon is accustomed to infect healthy blood, either at a distance or by contact alone. Those who transfer their contagion at a distance use the air as a medium; and of such a kind is he whose elementary spirit is intoxicated by the seeds of pestilence, smallpox, or consumption <note>tuberculosis</note>; for to the pestiferous blood, the pestilential spirit—

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Blood.
## X 2

A pestilential [spirit] is present, which is under the dominion of a malignant angel, to whom it is given to harm the earth. Such was that angel 
<margin>1 Chronicles 21</margin> whom David saw, having lifted his eyes, standing between heaven and earth with a drawn sword in his hand extended against Jerusalem, 
at which time so many thousands of Israelites died of the plague. For to each of these leaders ordained for the vengeance of God, there are infinite 
legions that mingle with this or that air according to the will of God. Since this air was originally ordained as the food of life <note>pabulum vitae: a common Paracelsian and vitalist term for the life-sustaining quality of air</note>, it must necessarily be introduced to the heart by breathing for the sustenance of the living creature. When this is done, it follows that these pestilential and malignant spirits are drawn into the body along with it, whereby 
the spirits of the good blood are corrupted by the evil of the malignant [spirit]. And this seems to be confirmed by this speech of the royal 
<margin>Psalm 77:49; Psalm 90:7</margin> Psalmist: *He cast upon them the fierceness of his anger, wrath, and indignation, and trouble, by sending evil angels.* And elsewhere he says, *We are consumed by thine anger, and by thy wrath are we troubled.* So also Job, struck by the Devil from the sole of his foot to the crown of his 
<margin>Job 6:4</margin> head, said: *The arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.* From which it is clear that by the "arrows of the Almighty," he understands malignant spirits invading under the conduct and command of the Devil or the harming angel (of whom it is spoken in Revelation ch. 7); hence he also calls them the "terrors of God set in array." Moreover, he relates that the place where they remain in the body is his spirit, which elsewhere he said was in the blood. He also teaches there how they afflict, namely, in the consumption of the spirit and the diminution of the radical moisture <note>humidi radicalis: the innate fluid believed by medieval physicians to be the fuel of life</note>. Hence he said, *Their poison drinks up my spirit*, and from this it follows that the spirits which affected Job were fiery; for among all other elements, that of fire is the most sensible, and 
consequently brings greater pain with it. 

There are, however, malignant spirits in the blood which are so gross and earthy that they cannot contaminate the blood of another at a distance; but indeed, spirits of this kind are accustomed to pour their poison heavily into healthy blood through contact. Such poison is observed to be in those afflicted by the venereal plague <note>lue venerea: Syphilis</note>, and also in both men and women defiled by virulent gonorrhea. In these cases, an unhealthy man may heavily infect a healthy woman, or vice versa, with discharges, ulcers, and other accidents of that passion, such as Buboes, scabs, decay <note>carie: bone rot</note>, inflammation, burning of urine, and other such things. Likewise, a leper rejoices to infect a healthy person by contact, which contagion indeed is only to be made by touch alone. And the internal principle of this kind of contagion seems to lurk in the external spirit of the blood, since an earthy nature cannot ascend into the sky. Therefore, these two kinds of contagions differ: because that which performs its actions at a distance is more fiery and airy. Hence, it mixes most easily with the intervening air between the infector and the infected, and participates in the nature of fiery spirits. But that which strikes only through contact is more earthy with dryness, like leprosy, or watery and heavy, like the venereal plague. Hence, it does not disperse itself so easily into the nature of the outer air, and this kind seems to participate in the nature of demons both terrestrial and aquatic; indeed, some demon or malignant spirit of the nature of the aforesaid elements is the cause of such a disease, as you will have more fully in the following chapter.

### CHAPTER XII.

#### ->On the antipathetic mystery of the blood, as much choleric and phlegmatic as melancholic,<-
#### ->and how demons are able to mix themselves with<-
#### ->their spirits.<-

As four complexions <note>The four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note> of man are recounted by physicians and philosophers, so indeed concerning the truly sanguine one, it is not to be disputed in this place, as it is that in which Antipathy does not exist; for it continually enjoys a temperament, if not in exact weight, yet in justice <note>iuſtitiam: a medical term for a functional balance of humors</note>. The common physicians and philosophers have placed the complexions and their elements, or the primary qualities of the elements, as the causes either of health, if they are kept within their limits, or of diseases, if they depart from the just limits of their temperaments. Thus they have treated the body as a thing moved instead of the soul as the mover. For when they say a disease arises from heat, cold, moisture, or dryness, they have explained nothing here except the hot, cold, moist, or dry effect of the agent or motor; but they have remained utterly ignorant of the nature of the internal agent. So also, immersing themselves deeper into the multitude [of details], they said the cause of this or that disease was either non-natural phlegm—whether glassy, crude, sweet, acid, or salty; or Bile—whether yellow, yolk-like, leek-green, rusty, or woad-blue; or melancholy (which they also call black bile)—whether scraping acid or arising from burnt phlegm. Thus they make the external element or humor the cause of the disease, but not the internal agent; nor were they ignorant of its acts, whether raging, or in stupor, or in pain. And this is the reason why physicians today are so uncertain and ignorant in their cures, since they have respect for the effects rather than the primary cause. But we, looking a little deeper into the nature of this matter and beyond the grasp of the pagans and Heathens, recognize first of all that just as God is the primary cause of the life of both the world and its creatures, so also He has a regard for their destruction. For the punishment of sins, He is accustomed to afflict and punish them with diseases, as the primordial author of both life and death, and in life, of both health and diseases and the disturbances of living things, according to their merits and His pleasure. This seems to be confirmed from many 
<margin>Psalm 104:29</margin> places of the Holy Scriptures, one of which cited above is of this kind: *When God hides his face, the creatures are troubled; when he takes away their breath, they die and return to their dust; when he sends forth his spirit, they are 
<margin>Psalm 90:7</margin> created.* Furthermore, it is said, *that by thy anger we are consumed, and by thy heat we are troubled.* Likewise, in another place it is written, *Blessed* is...

# Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book II.

<margin>Job 5:17</margin> Blessed is the mortal whom God corrects; therefore, do not despise the chastening of the Almighty, for he wounds and heals, he strikes and his hands will make whole. <note>original: "beatus est mortalis quem arguit Deus..."</note> And elsewhere, <margin>Job 6:4</margin> *The arrows of the Almighty are within me, the poison whereof drinks up my spirit, and the terrors of God set in array against me do war.* And elsewhere, <margin>Job 21:17</margin> *God distributes sorrows in his anger.* And elsewhere, <margin>Job 33:22</margin> God speaks through rebuke by pain upon the bed, and makes all his bones waste away; his flesh is consumed, and all the bones that were covered shall be laid bare. *His soul shall draw near to corruption, etc.* And elsewhere, <margin>Genesis 12:14</margin> Jehovah afflicted the house of Pharaoh with pestilence and plague because of Abram’s wife. He will strike with the ulcer of Egypt, and with hemorrhoids, and with scabs, and with the itch, from which you cannot be healed, and even with madness and blindness, and astonishment of heart.* And elsewhere, <margin>1 Samuel 2:6</margin> Jehovah brings death and restores to life, he sends down to the grave and brings back. <margin>1 Samuel 5:6</margin> Likewise, *Jehovah struck the people of Ashdod with hemorrhoids, etc.* <margin>1 Samuel 6:19</margin> Likewise, God struck the men of Beth-shemesh with a great slaughter; and Jeremiah, addressing God, said: *Correct me, O Jehovah, but with judgment; not in your anger, lest you bring me to nothing.* <margin>Jeremiah 10:24</margin> The hands of Jehovah God were against him for evil. <margin>Judges 2:15</margin>

But truly, it must be known that God works in the punishment of the wicked not immediately <note>directly</note>, but mediately <note>through intermediaries</note> and as the primary source; for whatever things, whether good or evil, happen to creatures, all those are brought about by God’s ordination but not by His execution. Just as it belongs to a king or emperor to decree and ordain all things according to his mind and conception, but afterwards those things which have been ordained are executed by ministers and subordinates, so also God, the disposer of all things, has his angelic ministers who, according to his will, deal either well or ill with creatures, and especially with men. God, therefore, is said to act according to ordination, while the angels, according to execution, set about performing what has been ordained by God. And this we have confirmed in many places both of the Holy Scriptures and of authors worthy of trust. For in the Royal Psalmist we find this written: *Bless the Lord, all you his angels, mighty in strength, who perform his word, hearkening to the voice of his speech. Bless the Lord, all you his hosts, you ministers of his who do his pleasure.* <margin>Psalm 102:20</margin> And elsewhere in the same author we have it thus: *Who makes your angels winds, and your ministers a flaming fire,* <margin>Psalm 103:4</margin> from which it is right to gather that angels are ministers and powers of God, who either in the form of winds, or of burning fire or lightning, do the will of God. For there are seven princes of angels, as witnessed by Daniel and Tobit, who stand before God, ready to carry out his commands, whether for the consolation of a creature or for punishment. Thus the angel of Jehovah was a help to Moses on his journey through the desert: <margin>Exodus 23:20</margin> *Behold (says Jehovah), I send my angel before you, to keep you in the way.* <margin>Genesis 21:17</margin> Similarly, the angel of Jehovah raised up Hagar; and was a help to Elijah when he was exhausted by hunger in the desert. <margin>1 Kings 19</margin> Furthermore, it is said *that the angel of the Lord encamps round about those who fear him, and delivers them.* <margin>Psalm 32:7</margin> And elsewhere: *No evil shall befall you, and no plague shall come near your dwelling, for he has given his angels charge over you in all your ways; they shall bear you up in their hands, lest perhaps you dash your foot against a stone.* <margin>Psalm 91:9</margin>

Furthermore, that angels also act for destruction and punishment is right to gather from these things: First, therefore, we read in the Holy Scriptures that God sent upon them the wrath of his indignation, anger, and trouble, through evil angels. <margin>Psalm 77:47</margin> From which it is clear that God executes wrath and indignation through evil angels. And elsewhere: *An evil spirit of God came upon Saul, etc.* <margin>1 Samuel 18:10</margin> From which it is evident that an evil angel is a spirit of God, one of his ministers. Similarly, it is said that a lying spirit stood before Jehovah, whom he chose to seduce the prophets with lies. <margin>2 Chronicles 18:21</margin> The Devil was also God’s instrument by which he afflicted Job with ulcers and pains. <margin>Job 1</margin> God also struck the firstborn of the Egyptians not by himself, but through the mediation of his destroyer. <margin>Exodus 12:23</margin> Thus Jehovah sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, to strike it; and when it was being struck, the Lord saw and took pity on the magnitude of the evil, and commanded the angel who was striking: "It is enough, now stay your hand." And David, lifting up his eyes, saw the angel standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword. <margin>1 Chronicles 21:15</margin> Thus Jehovah, sending his angel, cut off every mighty man of valor, and the leader and prince in the camp of the king of the Assyrians. <margin>2 Chronicles 32:21</margin> But what, I pray, is clearer than that passage in the Apocalypse <note>The Book of Revelation</note>, in which we read these things: *I saw angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth that they should not blow, not on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree; and I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God, and crying with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, saying: Hurt not the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the servants of God in their foreheads.* <margin>Revelation 7</margin> These things being so, let us hear the opinions of some well-versed in <term>occult philosophy</term> <note>The study of hidden natural and spiritual forces</note> concerning this matter, what they judge regarding the primary causes of diseases, and whether they disagree with the sentiment of the Holy Scriptures or not.

<margin>Psellus on Demons</margin> Psellus <note>Michael Psellos, an 11th-century Byzantine scholar</note> recognized six kinds of demons, the first of which he called *fiery*, which he said wanders about the higher air; and this kind, without doubt, mixes itself with and acts in thunder, lightning, comets, and other meteors, both of the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>the universe</note> and <term>microcosm</term> <note>the human body</note>. The second is *aerial*, and such demons wander in the air near to us; these demons are the causes of windy meteors, and they live and delight in the air, agitated in the manner of winds. The third is *aquatic*, which kind of demons immerse themselves in both salt and fresh waters, and gladly dwell around lakes and rivers, and indeed in the sea, and they desire to destroy and drown many in the waters. Similarly, they stir up waves and storms in the sea, and sink ships laden with men to the bottom, and overwhelm many with waves. The fourth is *terrestrial*, which for the most part dwells around the earth and opposes earthly things by many means and engines. The fifth is *subterranean*, as it lurks under the earth, and floods those who dig wells and mines, causes chasms in the earth, shakes foundations, and stirs up flame-vomiting winds. The sixth and last kind he makes *light-shunning* <note>original: "lucifugum"</note>, inscrutable and utterly dark, violently destroying things and animals with cold passions. And he says that all these kinds of elementary demons are so disposed that they both hate the Gods and are hostile to men.

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Blood.
->X 3<-

<note>The author is discussing the views of Michael Psellus, a 11th-century Byzantine philosopher known for his classification of demons.</note> ...is seen. But one thing is worse than another, nor indeed does this assertion of Psellus seem to differ from the sense of the Holy Scriptures; for in the passage of the Apocalypse <note>Revelation 7:1</note> mentioned above, it is said that four angels standing upon the four corners of the world hold the four winds of the earth so that they might not blow. From this it is clear that these are the governors of the winds, where it is also explained that it is given to them to harm the earth and the sea. Now, the Northern wind has a terrestrial nature, most cold and dry, and to this are referred the terrestrial spirits or demons, and consequently, the Angel presiding over this wind is the leader of these legions, namely the earthly, subterranean, and light-shunning demons. The Southern wind with its prefect has dominion over spirits partly aquatic and partly of a gross aerial sort; the West regards the genus of aerial spirits, as the East does the fiery ones.

To begin, therefore, with the nature of the malignant spirits: just as in the higher region of the Macrocosm <note>The universe</note> fiery meteors are produced, and sometimes mix themselves with the middle region of the air, producing thunder and lightning therein, so also in the choleric blood of the Microcosm <note>The human being</note> fiery meteors are generated. Of such a kind are burning and pestilential fevers, and for the most part putrid fevers produced from corrupted bile and phlegm, and even false tertian fevers with a rumbling of winds (which we compare to the thunder and lightning produced in the middle aerial region of the microcosm) by reason of a certain malignant spirit inhabiting the region of fire and air. And this seems to be established by the words of Artesius <note>A legendary alchemical figure, often identified with Artephius</note> (a man most profound and well-versed in the mysteries of the philosophers). <gloss>There are certain infirmities to which the devil joins himself, namely when a humor departs from its proper temperament and disturbs health itself; and this happens mostly in infirmities proceeding from <term>cholera</term> <note>Yellow bile, associated with fire</note>, and the cause of this is because the nature of cholera is hot and dry like fire. Now the substance of the Devil is composed of two things, namely fire and air; therefore his apparent part is air, but his hidden part is fire. Whence it is manifest that in this he is contrary and opposed to human nature, which is of a nature of equality. When, therefore, a sickness happens to the body which is of the nature of Cholera, it is likely to proceed from the Devil, inasmuch as his hidden part is fiery and choleric; and for this reason he most easily joins himself through harmony with cholera, and so increases his dominion over the other humors or elements which concur in the composition of the body and especially of the blood. Whence it happens that by reason of this departure from the natural temperament, and the rebellion of cholera against the laws of nature, the soul departs from the body and is separated from it.</gloss> Thus he speaks. From which it is demonstrated clearly enough that the opinion of that wise man is that the admission of the Devil or a fiery spirit into the bilious blood (which is accustomed to happen frequently and easily because of the similarity of their natures) is wont to excite fevers of every condition, according to the degree and power of the fiery demon. For as cholera participates in fire and air, so also the fiery nature of the Devil is most easily united to fire, and his aerial nature to air, for like is most aptly associated with like. This, then, is the manner—this, I say, is the reason—that fiery meteors of whatever kind are kindled in the body or blood, and from this it arises that bilious complexions are more afflicted by the presence of such preternatural meteors. But this is also clearly demonstrated through our experiment concerning the element of fire in the "Anatomy of Bread," where we indicated an aptitude in it for the attraction of blackness and darkness and for the reception of the malignant nature of the Devil. And for this cause we proved that elementary fire is the cause of corruption, just as celestial fire is the origin of life and generation. Therefore the complexion <note>The individual's constitutional balance of humors</note> is not to be blamed, because (as Ecclesiastes says) God made man upright and most temperate in regard to both body and soul, between which two the aerial spirit is the medium, joining both with a bond of love. For (as Solomon says) <margin>Wisdom 1:13</margin> *God did not make death, nor does he rejoice in the destruction of the living; for he created all things that they might exist, and he made the nations of the earth healthy, and there is no medicine of destruction in them, nor a kingdom of the underworld upon the earth; for justice is perpetual and immortal, but injustice is the acquisition of death, which is from the Devil.* For God created man inextinguishable, and made him in the image of his own likeness; <margin>Wisdom 2:23</margin> but through the envy of the Devil, death entered into the world. Now the aerial element of the blood—whether it participates more in fire, water, or earth—is the vehicle of the malignant spirit as well as of the soul. For (as the Archangel says) <margin>Kabbalah</margin> the cause of disease and death is sin, which is an error produced in the elementary part of the living being—which part does not perceive the things of God—but not in the spiritual part, which judges all things. For the reason for injustice or intemperance is in the external and aerial spirit of the soul, which is mortal, and not in the internal and ethereal spirit of the soul, which is eternal. Whence also the wise man says, <margin>Wisdom 9:15</margin> *The body which is corrupted weighs down the soul, and the earthly habitation presses down the sense that muses upon many things.* But truly this aerial or animal spirit participates in the body, inasmuch as it is the medium between the soul and the body. It is therefore this spirit which is deluded by the Devil; it is this spirit which suffers his violences; whence David speaks of it thus: <margin>Psalm 143:7; Job 21:4</margin> *My spirit is consumed, and is like those descending into the pit,* and Job: *My spirit is narrowed, etc.* Indeed, insofar as this spirit is affected by wicked and foreign spirits, so far does it communicate its painful passions both to the body (which truly suffers with it) and to the soul (which is immune to passions, yet nevertheless burns so vehemently with love for its prison that it seems to be sharply afflicted by the pains of the same). The soul, which in itself knows not how to grieve or suffer, fears destruction though it knows not how to perish; it fears defects, though its divine nature truly cannot fail. But let us return to our subject and prove from the Holy Scriptures that evil angels mix themselves with the blood and inflame it with their fiery disposition. The Psalmist says: *He sent upon them the wrath of his indignation, anger and tribulation through evil angels,* where it is clear that by "wrath" he understands a febrile heat, and by "evil angels" the ministers executing his will upon rebellious minds. Concerning this kind of demons, or their nature, those of whom Alzarabius <note>Likely referring to an Arabic medical authority like Al-Zahrawi</note> made mention are not much different, when he says: *Sicknesses invade men from transgressions and from cursed demons, who are called Alhabinabiles, whom the ancients were accustomed to cure through certain sciences now hidden from men; for these, by their subtlety, mix themselves with the blood, and the whole...*

# Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book II.

...and they corrupt the mass of humors in the same way that the Devil afflicted Job with a plague, against which no human medicines could prevail; for divine aid was required for the healing of such a stroke, which Christ and the Apostles used in their healings.

**Psellus** <note>Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine philosopher known for his writings on demonology</note> says that the aquatic kind of demon, by its very nature, is accustomed to affect the bloody spirit of a man so as to excite in him the "falling sickness" or **Epilepsy**, and madness. But he says that demons, both aerial and terrestrial, are accustomed by a certain occult art to fashion false thoughts in the animal spirit <note>The "animal spirit" was believed to be a subtle fluid in the nerves that governed sensation and movement</note>, to deceive human minds, and to bend them toward the most foul, unjust, and ruinous disturbances. And as it seems to me, such was the evil spirit from God that invaded **Saul**, by whose instigation Saul threw a spear with which he might have pinned **David** to the wall. Indeed, the effects of these kinds of demons are best expressed in **Hypochondriacs** and other types of melancholy. Whence **Albahati** <note>Likely referring to Al-Buhayti or a similar Arabic astrological authority</note> dared boldly to assert that melancholy is from a demon. Finally, subterranean and even light-shunning demons are by their nature exceedingly mischievous and destructive; for these not only deprave and hurt the souls of men with evil fantasies and devices, but also, wandering about in the manner of wild beasts of the forest, they hasten to the destruction of men.

Furthermore, aerial spirits do not act upon us through domination, but through delusion: for they are close by their nature to our elementary spirit (which is the organ and medium of our fantasy), since to them the invisible bodily mass is the "microcosmic air." Whence, just as fiery demons most easily adhere to the spirit of the choleric humor through harmony, so also air joins itself to air by a certain natural instinct. This is the reason why demons of this sort affect the spirit in man with various dispositions, tending as much to his disturbance as to his pleasures and joy. For if they are urged by wicked influences, such as those of **Saturn** or **Mars**, they are afflicted with sadness, fear, or vexations, or are incited by them to wrath, fury, and strife. But when **Mercury** is reigning, they vex with various "blasts" <note>flatibus: can refer to winds, breaths, or intestinal vapors</note> according to the nature of the planet to which the aspect of Mercury applies, whom they hold as their chief patron. 

But conversely, if Mercury looks upon planets that are good for human life, such as **Jupiter** and **Venus**, then they are more favorable to the human spirit, and they sound with a certain imperceptible whispering of pleasure, gladness, or carnal joy. For by a hiss and sound peculiar only to that person in whose spirit they dwell, they are accustomed to produce their words and voices, imperceptible to any other spirit, since spiritual things are not at all, or only with difficulty, subjected to the bodily senses. But because the voice of that kind of occult sound is joined with the spirit of the soul, the soul itself catches it immediately, just as one person is accustomed to catch the voice of another speaking in a whisper while those standing by are unaware. Hence it is that a hostile war is waged by demons of this sort, yet we are entirely ignorant of the authors of such contention, which the Wise Man seems to argue in these words:

<margin>1 Samuel 18:11</margin>
<margin>Wisdom 9:15</margin>

> For the corruptible body burdens the soul, and the earthy habitation weighs down the mind that muses upon many things. And hardly do we guess aright at things that are upon earth, and with labor do we find the things that are before us: but the things that are in heaven, who hath searched out? And who shall know thy counsel, except thou give wisdom... <note>Quoting the Book of Wisdom 9:15-17</note>

For in truth, because of the inclusion of the soul in a dark prison, it seems to understand almost nothing of those things which are spiritual and invisible; and unless God had opened the eyes of David, he would not have seen the evil angel of the Lord pursuing the Israelites with a drawn sword, whom no one besides him could behold. 

But let us proceed to the action of aerial spirits, and show the reason how they are accustomed to imprint feigned images of things, or icons and likenesses, into the human spirit. We see that if a sword or dagger is moved toward a well-polished **concave mirror**, the sword or dagger will seem to tend outside the mirror into the eye of the mover by a certain reverberation; indeed, the feigned image of that dagger or arm in the air will be as apparent as if it were the true substance of both, and not a likeness, so that I confess at first sight I was struck with a little fear, by which I was forced to step back suddenly. In this kind of perspective <note>term: perspective - the historical science of optics and light</note> conclusion, four things are found: namely the **object**, which is truly seen (the dagger); the **eye** of the beholder; the **mirror**, receiving the false idea of the true thing and emitting it into the aerial medium; and finally the **aerial medium**, which, receiving the false object created in the mirror into itself, presents it to the eye of the beholder as true. 

Therefore, we compare the sharpness of the soul of a deluded man to an eye touching the air; the bloody air immediately enclosing and surrounding it desires to propose its false likeness, fashioned by an aerial demon and impressed in it as if in a polished mirror. The mirror fashioned out of air is the body of the spirit or aerial demon. For as the good angels of God are called by **Dionysius** <note>Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite</note> "Images" (*Agalmata*), the clearest mirrors of things, receiving the light of God and representing His image, so the evil and harmful demons are mirrors in which falsehood and prestiges <note>term: prestiges - illusions or juggling tricks of the senses</note>, and those things which seem to be and are not, are impressed. But the prince of these was that lying spirit mentioned in 2 Chronicles 18:18:

<margin>1 Chronicles 21:15</margin>
<margin>2 Chronicles 18:18</margin>

> I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left. And the Lord said, Who shall entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead? And one spake saying after this manner, and another saying after that manner. Then there came out a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will entice him. And the Lord said unto him, Wherewith? And he said, I will go out, and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.

For spirits of this kind, being fashioned out of dense or windy air, receive the colors and fantastic figures of any thing, and reflect and transmit them into the animal or aerial spirit located in the blood, so that these kinds of fictions appear visibly to the eyes of the soul, so that it believes them to be true and essential. And thus they provide the soul with many but vain affairs, suggest imaginary counsels, show deceptive figures, offer ideas of pleasures, and represent likenesses of passions, either to anger and revenge, or to fear, sadness, and vain terror. Such was that spirit of which it is said:

<margin>2 Kings 19:7</margin>

> Behold, I will send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a rumor, and return to his own land...

For the nature of these spirits is to disturb and delude the soul, as far as possible, by a certain sophisticated and fraudulent art; the medium into which these feigned likenesses are extended...

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Blood.
->X 4<-

In those demonic mirrors, there is an airy spirit within the human blood, by means of which the soul is joined with the body; and this spirit is in itself fantastical, and like a celestial mercury <note>The author refers to the alchemical/astrological Mercury, known for its fluidity and ability to take on the properties of other substances.</note>, it is capable of any impression, however slight, for all the impressions of things are present in the worldly air. Furthermore, because of the close disposition of their nature with that of the demons, the bloody air (which we have elsewhere called the "animal spirit") is fit to receive all impressions similar to itself. Therefore, the spirit in which the soul is immediately carried is accustomed to judge these false impressions—of the healthy as well as the sick, both in dreams and even while awake—which for this reason the soul considers so true and infallible, because of that close relationship between the soul and this spirit of its own. From this, the worst and most astounding effects are produced, such as experience clearly demonstrates in cases of dementia, delirium, the hypochondriac passion, mania, and other species of melancholy.

Indeed, I confess that I myself, when I was affected almost lethally by a pestilential fever, experienced the effects of such malignant spirits; in which I was oppressed by perpetual wakefulness for 7 or 8 days, and whenever I frequently attempted to settle myself for sleep, I suddenly heard the distinct ringing or striking of several bells, by which all power of sleeping was always hindered, and the forced company of wakefulness was present with me through that whole space of time. Also, music composed of wind instruments <note>original: "instrumentis ventosis"</note> penetrated my ears so exactly from many directions during the time of my vigils, that it was even in my power to take down any symphonic part with pen and ink. Furthermore, they represented before my eyes the most foul images of monstrous men, as if they were true and living, and even little men <term>homunculi: miniature human-like beings often discussed in alchemy and folklore</term> appeared to me riding on horseback, communicating seriously among themselves about some secret matter, so that unless God by His grace (to whom immortal thanks be given) had applied a sound mind to me, they would have led me into despair, and finally into madness. But I recognized the frauds of these spirits, and that their delusions were vain and of no moment or danger, as I experienced in reality, and thus by divine goodness I was restored to my former health. But in this place, I wish to signify to you in passing, that where a melancholic wind joins with a burning fever <note>original: "Causonide," a Greek-derived term for a high, parching fever</note>, there also such spirits are accustomed to be present with fiery ones; for just as fire and air are united by a sympathy of nature and connected to one another, so also the spirits of both come together and are joined by bonds of peace, as is seen in thunder and lightning, at which time wind-whirlwinds are most frequent.

Finally, as pertains to the demons of the lower spheres, namely the aquatic, terrestrial, subterranean, and light-shunning <note>original: "lucifugos"</note>, *these (says Marcus <note>Referring to Michael Psellus, an 11th-century Byzantine scholar who wrote "De Operatione Daemonum."</note> addressing Psellus) do not devise anything wisely, nor do they undertake anything by craft or sophistry, because such subtlety is not in them; wherefore they are more foul and vile, and more subject to the senses, and consequently they harm in a more open and visible manner, but they act malignantly against human bodies. The reason for this is ready at hand, since their bodies participate more in water and earth, which are visible elements, than in air and fire, which are invisible elements.*

To begin therefore with those aquatic ones: these are accustomed to occupy the spirit of pituitous blood or the phlegmatic complexion, and they render the aquatic humor more dominant than the others. And since the bodies of such demons are coarser and more aquatic than those of the airy ones, as soon as they have crept into the airy spirit of the pituitous blood (which is denser than that of true blood), they are accustomed to fill up and block the passages between the natural and vital faculties, and even between those and the animal faculties. For they thicken the airy or animal spirit (which is dense by itself and of an aquatic condition) by their presence, because (according to *Psellus*) the animal spirit is constrained by the thickness of the bodies of such demons. From this it happens that the more principal powers of the body do not perform their functions or actions, whence motions are slow, stupid, and sometimes entirely interrupted; for in this kind is the first degree of cold, whose property is to thicken and congeal humors. Whence these spirits are chiefly the cause of Epilepsy or the "Comitial disease" <note>A historical name for epilepsy, so called because the Roman assemblies (comitia) were dismissed if someone had a seizure.</note>, which happens because of the obstruction of the passages of the brain, which is caused by phlegm condensed by the presence of a malignant spirit. But lest some scrupulous people mock this opinion of mine, affirming that a demon is the hidden cause of Epilepsy, let us hear Christ himself speaking: <margin>Matthew 17:15</margin> *"Lord (said a certain man to him), have mercy on my son, for he is a lunatic, and suffers badly, for he often falls into the fire, and frequently into the water. And Christ said, bring him to me; which being done, he rebuked him, and the demon went out of him, and the boy was cured from that hour."* The Moon has dominion over such spirits, whence it happens that in the full moon and new moon the possessed are more frequently affected, and also that they give off foam and viscous phlegm. There are also southern spirits who produce catarrhs and defluxions, and also aquatic diseases tending toward heat and saltiness. But with these, in this case, the airy spirits join themselves, namely while Mercury looks toward the Moon; for just as the angel of royal Mercury is the presiding officer of the airy spirits, who is a shape-shifter and changes himself according to the nature of the planet to which he applies, so also the prince Gabriel, the angel of the Moon, according to the applications of his planet, permits the spirits subject to him in the sublunary world to change and vary their actions.

Let us now approach the terrestrial demons, over whom the angel of Saturn presides, and therefore such are observed to be exceedingly mischievous and pernicious: and most opposed to the vital nature. Of these there are three kinds: of which the lower is worse than the higher, and the worst of all is that of the light-shunners. Their nature is to adhere to the airy spirit of melancholic blood. The highest kind of these is that of the terrestrials, who are more lively than the rest because they are of the earth, and therefore are more watchful than the others, and they agitate melancholy of the first species, make men foolish, and produce many such infirmities, according to the applications of Saturn with the other planets. However, the nature of the subterranean demons is to render men hypochondriacs and maniacs, and these exercise their powers most while Saturn is received by Mars, or some unlucky radiation is made between them: For just as these spirits are accustomed to produce horrible disturbances in the earth, inasmuch as they make gaps in the earth, and shake its foundations, and [vomit] flames...

# Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book II.

just as they stir up winds, which are therefore called Typhons <note>original: *Typhones*; referring to the mythological giant Typhon, associated with storms and chaos</note>, so also they sometimes shake the entire structure in the earth of the microcosm <note>The "microcosm" is the human body, viewed as a miniature version of the universe (the macrocosm).</note>, and are accustomed to produce hypochondriac blasts excited from the Spleen—or the center of the microcosmic earth—mixed with fiery heat. From this, they excite mania and Lycanthropy <note>The delusion of being transformed into a wolf.</note>, in which diseases these possessed persons or patients use a spirit as if it were their own instrument; through it they cry out and sometimes speak in languages not understood by the patient. However, the worst of all these kinds is that of the light-shunners, inasmuch as they bring sloth and numbness to the body and restrain the voice (as *Marcus taught us*), rendering the possessed man as if dead. The reason for this is that this kind is more earthy than the others, and consequently excels the others in coldness and dryness; it takes on in every way the nature of Saturn, who is most hostile to the human race. Whence it happens that into whomever this kind creeps, it mostly blunts, dulls, darkens, and destroys his animal power. And for this reason, these species of demons are called deaf and dumb not only by Marcus himself, but also by the Sacred Scriptures, because men possessed by them are made so, as their reason is utterly deprived. We believe, therefore, that these demons are the cause of Apoplexy, Paralysis, Stupor, Catalepsy, Lethargy, Coma <note>original: *Caros*; a deep, death-like sleep or stupor.</note>, and other such diseases, among which Apoplexy is the worst of all.

May the most kind reader grant me pardon if at first glance these things seem harsh and impossible to him; but indeed, I wish him to inquire into the matter with a slightly more accurate sense. Let him see first whether there is any action in raw humor by itself, or in mere imbalance from quality alone, which is able to inflict such injury and violence upon human nature (which is strongest in its balance)? Namely, in raw phlegm, or bile heated beyond nature, we do not find such power by itself that it could so manfully resist nature, or in 4, 7, or more days obtain such a victory over the presiding forces of human life, or erect and fix the trophies of such great spoil. It is necessary, therefore, that the principle of that preternatural action be internal to the animal or living nature, by which it can blunt and destroy the vigor of the vital soul. Since, therefore, the origin of all action is light, which is the principle of heat, just as that is the act, so also God is the fountain of light. He rains down His acts by means of the human spirit—first upon the Angels according to His will, either for blessing or for punishment—then from them to the stars of the ethereal heaven by means of the angels of the first rank, and then to all sublunary creatures. From this it is clear that every victory is obtained by the stronger; but the angels have governance over lower things and execute God's ordinances in them, inasmuch as they are His ministers, ready to perform His will for the good or evil of the creature. Let us not believe, therefore, that human life can be extinguished by a thing more ignoble: but only by one stronger and more powerful than itself.

But I know many respond that this is the opinion of Hippocrates and Galen <note>The two most influential physicians of antiquity, whose theories of "humors" dominated medicine for centuries.</note>, whom we have found to be truth-tellers up to this time. They teach us that the causes of diseases are imbalances of hot, cold, moist, and dry, or the rebellion and overabundance of humors, or their depravity, or a multitude of breaths and winds. But I will now boldly say that they did not produce a falsehood in this matter, yet it is said improperly—just as one says a candle illuminates a room, for it is not the candle, but its flame; nor indeed can a cannon <note>original: *bombarda*</note> do any harm where there is no powder in which its action resides; nor is a sword properly said to have killed a man, but the man as the primary agent. Indeed, the ancient physicians looked at the elements, but they either were ignorant of their primary agents, or did not wish to reveal them to the world, or at least to very few. We Christians say, if anything prosperous or adverse happens to us (even neglecting the external instrument), God has done this to us. Nay, truly, both in the investigation of the principles of diseases and in the search for the origin of health, one must proceed from God, who is the Being of beings and the Act of acts, by descending step by step. One must look to the secondary virtues, namely the Angels, then descend to the act upon creatures governed by the angels and their influences, and finally proceed to the sensible subjects, such as qualities, humors, and other such things, as passive elements. But let us hear what Psellus <note>Michael Psellus, a Byzantine monk and scholar known for his work on demonology.</note> says in addressing Marcus, after he had made mention of the preternatural dispositions of demons in the human spirit: *Psellus seems to reply thus: O Marcus, the followers of physicians lead us to believe certain more recent things, asserting that passions of this kind are not the effects of demons, but of humors, vapors, and winds being in a bad state; and so they are accustomed to approach this with medicines and diet, not with songs or the expiations of incantations. To whom Marcus replied: It is no wonder that physicians say this, who know nothing beyond the senses and have dwelt only on knowing bodies. It was perhaps fitting for them to think the inconveniences of bad humors were the sleep-inducing heaviness of the head, the distress of black bile, frenzy, and delusions, which they were accustomed to soothe with baths, potions, evacuations, or plasters. But inspirations and occupations <note>In this context, "occupation" refers to a spirit taking possession of a space or body.</note>, by which he who is possessed can do nothing—not by intellect, nor reason, nor imagination, nor sense—it is another thing that moves and leads him. And he says, moreover, that the occupied person knows things he did not know, and sometimes predicts future things; in what way (I say) shall we say that these are the erratic motions of matter?* Thus he spoke. And in truth, I myself have known many suffering from a burning fever, some of whom, with delirium preceding, divined the day and hour of their death. And a certain man suffering from the plague understood through a vision that he would shortly die; and it seemed to him that after his death he contended with another as to who should first enter through a certain narrow way. In this contention of his, two men of honest gravity came upon them, to whose judgment this controversy was recommended, and thus the privilege of entering first was granted to him. When this sick man died a few days later and was carried to the grave, a contention arose between his friends and those of another dead person over the burial place; and so at last the dispute was settled by two senior parish priests of St. Andrew, and the grave was adjudged to the one who had dreamed it. Alzarabius <note>Likely referring to the Arab physician Albucasis (al-Zahrawi).</note> also seems to confirm this opinion of Marcus in the place cited before—

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Blood.

It appears, where he asserts, that diseases invade men both through transgressions and through cursed demons—whom they were accustomed to cure through ancient sciences now hidden from men—for by their subtlety they mingle themselves with human blood, corrupting the entire mass of humors. This is evident from the most cruel plague inflicted by the Devil upon Job, where no human remedies were of any use. Sometimes, however, it happens that a malignant spirit, creeping into the blood and disturbing the entire mass, may exit during a bloodletting along with the spirit of the departing blood, and thus the patient suddenly recovers. But if it still remains in the mass of the blood, that bloodletting usually brings no benefit or relief. Furthermore, let us hear Augustine speaking on this matter: "Truly, what is written in Ecclesiasticus chapter 40: *A heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam from the day of their coming forth from their mother's womb, until the day of burial into the mother of all* <note>original: "mater omnium," referring to the earth</note>, must be fulfilled to such an extent that even <margin>The City of God, book 21.</margin> little children—already released through the bath of regeneration <note>Baptism</note> from the bond of original sin by which alone they were held—suffer many things, and some endure the incursions of malignant spirits." And Jerome, concerning the death of Blesilla in a letter to Paula, says: "What is the reason that infants sucking at the maternal breasts are corrupted by a demon?" Also, concerning the aerial spirits and their subtle way of operating within us, he speaks clearly and lucidly in the Decree set forth in chapter *sciendum* 36, question 4. Where, after he had spoken some words concerning their excellence over men and other creatures on account of their subtle and aerial composition, he proceeds thus: "They often receive power both to send diseases and to render the air itself morbid by tainting it, and to persuade the perverse and lovers of earthly comforts to evil deeds; persuading by wondrous and invisible ways, penetrating the bodies of men without them feeling it through that subtlety, and mingling themselves with their thoughts through certain imaginary commands, whether they are awake or sleeping." And elsewhere he says: "They often <margin>Augustine, On the Divination of Demons.</margin> receive power both to send diseases, and to render the air morbid by tainting it, and to persuade the perverse to evil deeds." Similarly, John Chrysostom says: "The Devil does not tempt men as much as he wishes, since as far as he is concerned, he would never cease from temptation; <margin>On Matthew, book 1.</margin> for he has no other occupation—he does not eat, nor sleep, nor perform any other work, except to tempt, deceive, and subvert: this is his food." Finally, we gather from the Book of Revelation cited above that power has been granted to demons over both the earth and men, by permission, to subvert the air and the waters. Whence I think it can be hidden from no wise man that all diseases proceed from those four angels to whose power the governance of the winds has been committed. And this even the Pagan <note>original: "Ethnici," referring to non-Christian Greek and Roman physicians</note> physicians perceived by diligent observation through a demonstration *a posteriori*—that is, from the effect—and not *a priori*, inasmuch as they were unable to penetrate to the internal agent of the disease. Hence Hippocrates says: "Changes of the seasons especially produce diseases, and in certain seasons great changes of either <margin>Aphorisms, book 3, 1.</margin> cold or heat."

He himself saw that the changes of the seasons in heat and cold were the cause of diseases; but they were ignorant that either fiery or earthly angels were the principles of these alterations acting in the winds; therefore, they mistook the effect for the efficient cause. And elsewhere: "In seasons when on the same day there is now heat, now cold, one <margin>Aphorisms, book 3, 4.</margin> must expect autumnal diseases."

For by the conflict of demons of contrary conditions, the seeds of contention are left in the air, which, entering into bodies through breathing or nutrition, produce through hidden opposition false and putrid fevers; the causes of which they therefore claimed were corrupted phlegm (or suffering phlegm) and acting bile. And elsewhere: "In dry heats, acute fevers occur; and if the year has been for the most part of such a kind, whatever constitution it has made, <margin>Aphorisms, book 3, 7.</margin> such diseases for the most part must be expected." And elsewhere: "Regarding the seasons, if indeed the winter has been dry and Northerly, but the spring rainy and Southerly, it is necessary that in summer there be acute fevers and eye inflammations, and difficulties of the intestines, etc." <margin>Aphorisms 3, 11.</margin>

Here, however, he makes the winds the causes of these diseases; and yet he was ignorant of the Angels who are the procreators of the winds, of whom mention is made in Revelation. And so, that entire book makes mention everywhere of diseases arising from the blasts of the winds and vain constitutions of the air. By which it is evident that if the Angels, who have the power either to restrain or release the winds, are malignant and harmful both to the earth and its creatures, by means of the blasts of the winds—to which are subject infinite legions of harmful ministers who, obeying their command, mingle themselves with the winds and disperse themselves everywhere in the air, polluting and contaminating it with their poisonous breaths, and with it also longing to pervade the inner chambers of the human heart by divine permission, and thus transfer a healthy disposition into a morbid one—if, I say, these angels have power over the acting or burning fire (with due consideration), it would have been better for those Pagan physicians to have searched out the secret natures of those angels and the method of loosening those knots (as they are the primary agents in diseases), rather than, like blind men, to torment the elements and humors themselves in a vain manner. It is as if some madman (having no regard for the acting or burning fire) wished to beat a piece of wood with a whip or strike it with a sword or axe because it has been reduced to flame, thinking that in this way he would take away the harm or damage of the fire; when nevertheless the violence of the fire is not hindered by this, and it continues nonetheless in its action. By a similar reasoning, physicians name and look upon the passive sensible things, but they are ignorant of and neglect the internal acting essences. Hence, therefore, for the most part they purge in vain, they draw blood in vain, they administer altering potions in vain, so that they have observed more people die under their hands and endure the ultimate suffering than return to the boundaries of their former health by the virtue of common medicine. And if some are restored to their former state, the vigor of Nature itself—which is able to endure the trial of the expected crisis—has usually brought more utility than the faculty of the medicine itself; and this indeed happens because the hidden properties of herbs and animals, to which it is given to expel this or that demon and suppress its malignancy in the body, are hidden from the common crowd.

### CHAPTER I.
#### *In which it is proved that the spermatic vessels correspond to the fourth quarter of the Western sky. Similarly, various opinions on the origin of sperm and seed are explained.*

At last, we turn the sharp point of our needle or stylus—touched by the magnetic desire of the soul—toward the Western point, and it comes to mind to set forth words, though few, yet sufficiently clear, concerning the setting of the microcosmic sun. Just as in the first part of the preceding sections we made mention of the northern and southern poles of the microcosm <note>The "microcosm" is the human body, viewed as a small-scale map of the entire universe or "macrocosm."</note>, and then in the second part of its bloody air in general along with its mysteries: so now we shall approach its western angle or hinge. For just as we shall describe the rising of man or the eastern region below in the secrets of the heart, so in this place we compare the seminal vessels to the point of the west; thus the sperm or seed contained in them is compared to the Western sun, and the organs hiding them to the earth.

For what else, I ask, is the seed but the quintessence <note>The "fifth essence" or purest, most concentrated spiritual force of a substance.</note> of life, descending from the place of the sun or the heart where it rises in the microcosm into these vessels? The seed contained in them is like the sun descending or setting, prepared for the uterine tomb in which it dies—or at least appears to be changed—until it rises again and produces a new creature similar to the first. So too the setting Sun appears to us to die, and to lose its life or light, and the night (which is likened to corruption) comes over it, until the sun rises again in the east as before. In plainly the same way the seed (which is the Sun of life and generation) which previously rose in the heart to illuminate the life and the human earth, now sets in the seminal vessels, where descending into the womb it seems to die; and yet it lives secretly, and acts continually to produce a new creature, in whose heart it seems to rise to illuminate its earth no differently than the macrocosmic sun does to its own.

But since this cannot be well considered by the common people, because it is most difficult to investigate and explain the secret generation of the seed (so uncertain is the opinion of philosophers and even almost all physicians concerning it, being so unstable and inconstant in their judgments), I have judged it worthwhile to explain some of their opinions in the first place, with some arguments opposing them, and then afterwards I will explain the sentiment of my own mind. This view, although new and (as far as I know) never heard of until this day, I shall prove to be certain and to be received beyond any controversy by the clear evidence of untainted truth.

Albertus Magnus <note>A 13th-century Dominican friar and philosopher who wrote extensively on natural history.</note> in *The Secrets of Women*, says that sperm is nothing other than the surplus of nourishment, which recedes into a substance not intended for the nourishment of the body. He is indeed a man most prudent in philosophy, but in this definition of his (as it seems to me) not at all just, and inconsistent with himself; he dared to assign the origin of a thing so divine (such as is the seed, in which so many gifts of the heavens and such great vigor of spirits lie hidden) to the superfluity of food. Thus he unwisely believes that that vile matter (which cannot be reduced back into the nature of blood) is reduced into the precious sperm whose soul is the seed—as if the entire power of the fetus, its living soul, and its specific virtue consisted in the excess of food and drink! There are also others who are more senseless in their judgment of the procreation of seed, and wish it to be made from the substance of the brain: which, if it were likely, it would follow that those who engage in much intercourse would have very little brain,

Finally, who is so weak in philosophical speculation as to be ignorant that the vital and natural spirits differ in location and nature from those animal spirits (which abound in the brain)? But since like is usually procreated by like, he who is generated from sperm gushing only from the brain would undoubtedly not be a "hearted" man (as they say), but purely intellectual, being generated and fashioned entirely from cerebral substance. Others (among whom I name Galen, in his booklet—or at least one attributed to him—*On Sperm*) affirm **that sperm descends from every humor of the body which is made from the subtler nature of the four humors.** And indeed, they seem to denote the visible part of the sperm, or its mass; but they have not even thought of its celestial soul or its internal and invisible part, which we call the "seed" <note>original: *semen*</note>, since they seem to speak in this place only of sublunary humors. Others well-versed in philosophy recognize an internal acting cause in the sperm, **which they confess to be a certain quality and occult power, grafted into the seed by nature, which they say arises from the principal parts of the body; and they wish this power to inform the matter of living bodies with a similar form and species.** (For I have read Curium, among others, alleging this.) By this confession, however, the unknown is gathered from the even more unknown; for who is so absurd as not to know that the form in every thing is that internal agent by which the external is driven and moved, or that it is some occult and formal thing which attributes a specific essence to a visible creature? Furthermore, these men fall into the same absurdity as the others, wishing that a specific form (which is of celestial substance) could be derived from the parts of the body (which are elements or fashioned from elements). Aristotle also among the philosophers, and Fernelius among the physicians, declare sperm with a more cautious and broader definition: that Seed is that from which those things which are constituted according to nature first arise. These men, therefore, define it by its effect, and not in its essence.

But we, indeed, with a clearer method and a slightly more elevated style, shall explain the origin—both celestial and elemental—not only of the sperm but also of the seed hiding within it, along with the manner of their mutual mixing and preparation. We shall demonstrate that it is nothing other than an airy spirit driven from all the four winds <note>literally "breaths"</note> of the microcosm into the form of a macrocosmic cloud by the power of the spirit, or celestial wind (which also has its own internal, shining demon or genius, moving it by the instinct of God presiding over it). And it is a composite: the external part from the elemental, and the internal from the celestial. Thus it is also said in Ezekiel: <margin>Ezekiel 37:5</margin> **The Lord said, Behold, I will send spirit into you, and you shall live; and I will lay sinews upon you, and will cause flesh to grow upon you, and cover you with skin, and give you spirit, and you shall live. And the Lord said:** breathe from the four winds upon these slain, that they may come to life; and the spirit entered into them and they lived. From which it is evident that the sperm itself is a cloud or air naturally collected and condensed from all the winds, the internal part of which is an angel appointed by God, who holds the protection of life. Indeed, three angels concur in the being of the sperm: one is the intellectual wind or spirit, which has power over the animal spirit sent from the empyrean heaven; the second is the ethereal breath, which presides over the vital spirit; and the last is the elemental, which is the wind or spirit having power over the natural faculty. Whence also three bubbles are accustomed to appear in the sperm after it has remained in the womb for six days.

### Chapter II.

#### ->That sperm is composed of two things, and that it is contracted into the form of a cloud by the spirit or wind in the natural body; and concerning the manner of the generation of sperm.<-

**A**s it is certain and known to all that man is composed of body and soul, so also it is not hidden from the skilled that sperm is fashioned from two things: namely the external and visible, which is drawn from the purer substance of the elements (and in this place acts as its body, being called "sperm" by its proper name), and the internal or invisible, which descends from heaven by means of the air, concerning which we shall speak below.

But before we speak of the origin of these parts of the humor rooted in generation, and the manner of their joining, it is necessary first that we consider the four "preparing vessels" of the sperm, of which two descend on each side toward the testicles: namely a vein and an artery. On the left side, another descends from the left emulgent vein, namely the artery or aorta, or great artery, proceeding near the left kidney and likewise tending downward. Also on the right side, one vessel—namely a vein—stretches downward from the trunk of the vena cava, but the artery exits from the same place of the aortic trunk as the left one, and likewise inclines toward the testicles in the manner of the left. It must be known, however, that each vessel of either side, fashioned from a vein and artery (as was said), weaves and entangles itself in its descent toward the testes in a wonderful union or plexus in the form of a net; and the Greeks call this inseparable texture <term>Anastomosis</term> <note>A connection or opening between two things; here referring to the pampiniform plexus</note>. This kind of entanglement of the vein and artery lasts from about the middle of the descent down to the testicles themselves, which we have previously called the "expurging vessels" in common anatomy. These things being rightly considered, we shall proceed to what follows.

An uncertain author in a certain manuscript treating the nature of sperm left this: **that the sperm of man is a seed compacted and derived from the more principal substance of all the limbs.** And he is indeed right, if he had mentioned the external part of the sperm; but he spoke irregularly insofar as he called the sperm "seed," as if one were to confuse form with matter. # On the Mystical Anatomy of the Sperm.

The substance of the members composing the body is said to be formed by the most occult action of nature; but the **seed** (which is a certain central, formal, and invisible thing within the sperm) relates to the sperm as the soul relates to the body. It is formed not from elementary matter, but from a celestial and ethereal substance, along with its light—indeed, even with a super-celestial essence. Therefore, that common definition is incongruously stated, as it confuses elementary matter with its form—namely, confusing the **sperm** with the **seed**—since these two differ no differently than matter and form, where one acts and the other is acted upon.

We say, therefore, that the **sperm**—that is, the visible mass—is like a cloud or air. By a natural breath, following the nature of the breath of spirits or winds (both super-celestial and celestial as well as elementary) blowing from all corners or regions of the **microcosm** <note>The "microcosm" refers to the human body as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>, it is condensed into the visible form of a white and fertile little cloud. For as we see in the air of the **macrocosm** <note>The "macrocosm" refers to the great world or universe.</note>, clouds change color due to the greater purity of their substance. According to the opinions of ancient philosophers, if the substance of a cloud or mist is procreated from a subtler vapor that is not so condensed, then its color will be white, and its substance more rare, transparent, and lucid, thereby denoting aerial purity. But if it is denser, proving a multitude of terrestrial fumes or waters, then it will be dark or black, so that the solar rays cannot penetrate it. Therefore, this latter species seems to exist preternaturally in the world and brings about great rains or floods.

The former species of clouds, however, seems to exist according to nature; they incline toward the nature of those fertile mists which are said, in the beginning before any cloud appeared in the sky, to have ascended from the earth to water its surface,

<margin>Genesis 2:5</margin>

so that it might become fertile and more fit and convenient for the increase and vegetation of plants. In this same way, a white mist of this kind exhales from the quarters of the body or "earth," and by the power of the internal spirit seizing it and condensing it into a white little cloud, it is introduced into the seminal vessels as if into the "western corner."

The manifest substance is therefore like the pure essence of the four elements constituting the members of the microcosmic earth. This is first decocted and prepared in its members or vessels into a most subtle substance of air, which retains within itself the power of the four elements and consequently the four humors, from which the body of the offspring is fashioned—no differently than the divine soul emanates from the heart into the seed.

That this elementary and visible sperm is extracted from all the members of the body (as the essence of a composite thing from its **uichymic** <note>original: "vhychimica" - likely a reference to alchemical or vitalistic chemistry</note> mass) for the composition of the born body, and not from any particular part, we gather from three arguments:

1.  **First:** After much intercourse, we see all the members of the body exhausted, numbed by a certain torpor, and as if fatigued; we notice the spirits of the brain dulled, the feet and even the muscles of the arms weighed down, and finally the entire mass sluggish and almost inanimate. Indeed, if a person who indulges too much in intercourse was previously afflicted by **gout** <term>podagra: gout of the foot</term>, **hand-gout** <term>chiragra: gout of the hand</term>, or hypochondriac wind, even if they seemed completely cured, they will immediately feel pains and weariness in those members above all others after much intercourse. This is a most certain sign (as it seems to me) that the pure extract of the members, or the essence of the four elements, is drawn out from them by a certain magnetic power and spirit (or wind) and introduced through the orifices of the small veins into the **vena cava** <note>The main vein returning blood to the heart.</note>. Flowing through the blood mass, it is led downward and poured into the seminal veins or vessels. There, by the power of the elementary spirit seeking a new form, it is contained for complete preparation, so that it may better receive the impressions of its seminal form flowing from the heart through the great artery.
2.  **Second:** Experience proves that a son participates in the incurable diseases of the parents. If any member is affected by such a deformity in the father or mother, we often observe it similarly affected in the child: namely, gout in the feet, gout in the hands, a stone in the back or bladder, etc. The reason for this is that nature rejoices and longs to procreate like from like.
3.  **Third and most certain:** A son or daughter for the most part displays the appearance and image of their parents—namely, a likeness in the face, symmetry in the arrangement of members, and even the gesture and icon of the entire body.

We conclude, therefore, that the **sperm**, or the more visible portion of the generative humor, is the essence of those four elements which constitute the members of the body. The members are the vessels in which it is decocted and prepared into the form of a cloudy smoke, breath, or elementary spirit seeking a new form. It drives this smoke before it with successive motion, like wind drives smoky air, first from the fleshy parts into the blood mass of the vena cava through the orifices of the small veins rising from the trunk of the cava, and then afterwards into the spermatic veins, in which that smoke gradually coagulates into a white little cloud.

From this it is manifest that the sperm, being in this place of the body, is also the origin and beginning of the body of the fetus. Although it may appear to be a thick and bare mucus or matter, it nevertheless contains within itself the invisible parts of the whole thing to be begotten, which is the fruit of the members of the parent's body—no differently than an apple is the fruit of an apple tree, or a grape of the vine. Although the fruit is plucked from its tree, the tree does not die, but daily seizes from the Elements a new power of generating for itself. And this is what the Philosophers mean when they say that the seeds of all things lie hidden in the elements.

The immediate way in which this elementary spirit is nourished and refreshed (which flies immediately from the extreme members after the emission of sperm into the womb, to successively fill the place of the emitted sperm) is through the blood, which is procreated from the chylous juice of nourishment. Regarding the mixture of this sperm with its seed, we shall deal with that point by point in the following chapter, after we have first dealt with the form of the female or her sperm.

Others (among whom I name Galen, in his booklet—or at least one attributed to him—*On Seed*) affirm **that the sperm descends from every humor of the body which is made from the subtler nature of the four humors.** And indeed, these thinkers seem to denote the visible "mass" or body of the sperm; however, they have not even considered its celestial soul or its internal and invisible part, which we call the "seed" <note>original: *semen*</note>, since in this passage they seem to speak only of sublunary humors. Others well-versed in philosophy recognize an internal acting cause in the sperm, **which they confess to be a certain quality and occult power, grafted into the seed by nature, which they say arises from the principal parts of the body; and they wish for this power to inform the matter of living bodies with a similar form and species.** (For I have read Curium, among others, alleging this.)
