Furthermore, these men fall into the same absurdity as the others, wishing that a specific form (which is of celestial substance) could be derived from the parts of the body (which are elements or fashioned from elements). Aristotle also among the philosophers, and Fernel among the physicians, declare sperm with a more cautious and broader definition: that Seed is that from which those things which are constituted according to nature first arise. These men, therefore, define it by its effect, and not in its essence. But we, indeed, with a clearer method and a slightly more elevated style, shall explain the origin—both celestial and elementary—not only of the sperm but also of the seed lurking within it, along with the manner of their mutual mixing and preparation. We shall demonstrate that it is nothing other than an airy spirit driven from all the "four winds" of the microcosm into the form of a macrocosmic cloud by the power of the spirit, or celestial wind (which also has its own internal shining *daemon* or genius, moving it by the instinct of God presiding over it). Indeed, three angels concur in the being of the sperm: one is the intellectual wind or spirit, which has power over the animal spirit emitted from the empyrean heaven; the second is the ethereal breath, which presides over the vital spirit; and the last is the elementary, which is the wind or spirit having power over the natural faculty. Whence also three bubbles are accustomed to appear in the sperm after it has remained in the womb for six days.

**AS** it is certain and known to all that man is composed of body and soul, so also it is not hidden from the skilled that sperm is fashioned from two things: namely the external and visible, which is drawn from the purer substance of the elements (and in this place holds the role of the body, and is called by the proper name "sperm"), and the internal or invisible, which descends from heaven by means of the air, concerning which we shall speak below.

But before we speak of the origin of these parts of the radical humor in generation, and the manner of their joining, it is necessary first that we consider the four "preparing vessels" of the sperm, two of which descend on each side toward the testicles: namely a vein and an artery. On the left side, from the left emulgent vein, another descends, namely an artery or aorta, or "great artery," proceeding near the left kidney and likewise tending downward. Also on the right side, one vessel, namely a vein, extends downward from the trunk of the vena cava, but the artery emerges from the same place of the aortic trunk as the left, and likewise inclines toward the testicles in the manner of the left. It must be known, however, that each vessel of either side, fashioned from a vein and an artery (as was said), in its descent toward the testes, weaves and entwines itself by an admirable union or plexus in the form of a net-like web; and the Greeks call this inseparable texture <term>Anastomosis</term> <note>A "joining" or "opening"; here referring to the complex network of blood vessels (pampiniform plexus) leading to the gonads</note>. This kind of entangling of the vein and artery lasts from about the middle of the descent down to the testicles themselves, which we have previously called the "expurgating vessels" in common anatomy. These things being rightly considered, we shall proceed to what follows.

An uncertain author in a certain manuscript treating the nature of sperm left the opinion that the sperm of man is a seed compacted and derived from the more principal substance of all the limbs: and rightly so, if he had mentioned the external part of the sperm; but he spoke irregularly insofar as he called the sperm "seed," as if one were to confuse form with matter. For sperm is that visible part in the generative juice, which is from the purer of the four elements...

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Sperm.

The substance of the members composing the body is said to be formed by the most hidden action of nature. However, the **seed** (which is a certain central and formal thing, and invisible within the sperm) relates to the sperm as the soul relates to the body. It is formed not from elementary matter, but from a celestial and ethereal substance, along with its light—indeed, even with a super-celestial essence. Therefore, that common definition is incongruously stated, as it confuses elementary matter with its form—namely, confusing the **sperm** with the **seed**—since these two differ no differently than matter and form, of which one acts and the other is acted upon.

We say, therefore, that the **sperm**—that is, the visible mass—is like a cloud or air. By a breath, according to the nature of the breath of spirits or winds, *both super-celestial and celestial as well as elementary, breathing from all corners or regions of the microcosm* <note>The "microcosm" refers to the human body as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>, it is condensed into the visible form of a white and fertile little cloud. For as we see in the macrocosmic air, clouds change color due to the greater purity of their substance. According to the opinions of the ancient philosophers, if the substance of a cloud or mist is procreated from a subtler vapor that is not so condensed, then its color will be white, and its substance more rare, transparent, and bright, thereby denoting aerial purity. But if it is denser, and proves a multitude of terrestrial fumes or waters, then it will be dark or black, so that the solar rays cannot penetrate it. Therefore, this latter species seems to exist preternaturally in the world and brings about great rains or floods.

The former species of clouds, however, seems to exist according to nature, and they incline toward the nature of those fertile mists which are said, in the beginning before any cloud appeared in the sky, to have ascended from the earth to water its surface,

<margin>Genesis 2:5</margin>

so that it might become fertile and more fit and convenient for the increase and vegetation of plants. So also a white mist of this kind exhales from the quarters of the body or "earth," and by the power of the internal spirit seizing it and condensing it into a white little cloud, it is introduced into the seminal vessels <note>The "venalia" or seminal ducts</note> as if into the corner of the west. Therefore, the manifest substance is like the pure essence of the four elements constituting the members of the microcosmic earth, which is first boiled and prepared in its members or vessels into the most subtle substance of air. This air retains within itself the power of the four elements and consequently the four humors, from which the body of the offspring is forged—no differently than from the seed which first emanates from the heart, its divine soul.

That this elementary and visible sperm is extracted from all the members of the body—as the essence of a composite thing from its mass by a chemical power for the composition of the newborn body, and not from any particular part—we gather by three arguments.

The first is that after much coitus, we see all the members of the body exhausted, and as if numbed and fatigued by a certain torpor; we perceive the spirits of the brain dulled, the feet and even the muscles of the arms weighed down, and finally the entire mass sluggish and almost inanimate. Indeed, even if one who engages in too much coitus was afflicted in past times by <term>podagra</term> <note>Gout in the feet</note>, <term>chiragra</term> <note>Gout in the hands</note>, or hypochondriac wind—even if he were now almost completely cured—nevertheless, after much coitus, he will immediately feel pains and weariness in those members above the others. This is a most certain sign (as it seems to me) that a pure draw from the members, or the essence of the four elements, is elicited from them by a certain magnetic power and spirit or wind, and is introduced through the orifices of the small veins into the <term>vena cava</term> <note>The main vein returning blood to the heart</note>. Flowing through the blood mass, it is introduced and poured downward into the seminal veins or vessels. There, by the power of the elementary spirit seeking a new form, it is contained for complete preparation, so that it may better receive the impressions of its seminal form flowing from the heart through the great artery.

The second argument is that experience proves that a son participates in the incurable diseases of the parents. Thus, if any member is affected by such a deformity in the father or mother, we frequently observe that same member so affected in the child: namely, gout in the feet, gout in the hands, a stone in the back or bladder, etc. The reason for this is that *nature rejoices and desires to procreate like from like*.

The third and most certain argument is that a son or daughter for the most part displays the species and image of their parents: namely, a likeness in the face, symmetry in the arrangement of the members, and indeed the gesture and icon of the entire body.

We conclude, therefore, that the **sperm**, or the more visible portion of the generative humor, is the essence of those four elements which constitute the members of the body. The members are the vessels in which it is boiled and prepared into the form of a cloudy smoke, a breath, or an elementary spirit seeking a new form. It drives this smoke before it with successive motion, as wind drives smoky air, first from the fleshy parts into the blood mass of the vena cava through the orifices of the small veins rising from the trunk of the cava, and then afterwards into the spermatic veins, in which that smoke gradually coagulates into a white little cloud.

From this it is manifest that the sperm, being in this place of the body, is also the origin and beginning of the body of the fetus. Although it may appear to be a thick and bare viscous matter, it nevertheless contains within itself the invisible parts of the whole thing to be begotten, which is the fruit of the members of the parent's body—no differently than an apple is the fruit of an apple tree, or a grape of the vine. Although this fruit is plucked from its tree, the tree does not die, but daily seizes from the Elements a new power of generating for itself. And this is what the Philosophers mean, namely, *that the seeds of all things lie hidden in the elements*.

The immediate way in which that elementary spirit is nourished and refreshed (which flies immediately from the extreme members after the emission of sperm into the matrix, so that it may successively fill the place of the sperm's emission) is through the blood, which is procreated from the chylous juice of nourishment. As for what pertains to the mixing of this sperm with its seed, we shall deal with it point by point in the following chapter, where we shall first have treated the form of the seed or sperm,

### CHAPTER III.

#### Concerning the seed, or the hidden form of the sperm, and its mystical procreation: and how it is the true gold of life sent down from the heavens: Likewise, what constitutes the essence of the offspring.

How stupendous and admirable a creature the air is, how filled with influences of both life and death, and likewise how it is the source of vegetation and the formal nurseries of generation—indeed, truly the receptacle of God as well as of angels and demons—has been demonstrated by us clearly enough in the preceding sections. But truly, insofar as the sparks of life and generation swim in that alone (namely, the aerial spirit), without which creatures cannot live for even a moment of time (among whom we understand man especially as the prince), it is therefore necessary that the inhalation of this air occurs every minute of time. For without it, the animal is immediately suffocated, since when the aerial spirit is taken away, its soul is also removed—which is the ethereal light joined with such a spirit. By the former [the light], the innate heat of life is nourished and refreshed; by the latter [the spirit], the decreasing radical moisture is successively restored. Therefore, the animal—but more effectively man—breathes this spirit into the left chamber of the heart. This occurs by the reason explained by us in our common anatomy: namely, by the contraction of the straight fibers of the heart, and consequently by the dilation of the oblique and transverse fibers. This movement is called *Diastole* <note>The phase of the heartbeat when the heart muscle relaxes and allows the chambers to fill with blood</note>, during which interval the heart introduces air from the lungs, through the venous artery <note>The pulmonary vein</note>, into its left ventricle for the nourishment of the vital and generative spirits. This is observed no differently than how the liver is seen to attract the juice of nourishment to its cavity to regenerate the natural spirits destined for growth. In this laboratory of the microcosm <note>The human body viewed as a miniature universe</note>, therefore, perfect Nature sets about completing the "anatomy" of the air and dividing it into its parts by equal partition. For here, she distinguishes the fiery substance of heaven and the ethereal spirit (which is its vehicle) from the sooty and morbid heterogeneity of the air. The celestial parts she hides away in her sanctuary called the aorta; the elementary parts, however, being subject to change and corruption and thus useless for the business of life, she turns into smoke and emits them as superfluous through the same path by which they were introduced. These are the radiant atoms swimming in an invisible manner within the ethereal spirit and reserved in the microcosmic perfume-box <note>original: "myrothecio"</note>. These are the "Phoebian nurseries" <note>Seeds or influences related to the Sun/Apollo</note> flowing in from the fountain of the Sun, which are said to differ from the nature and essence of the sun no differently than a ray differs from the whole sun. Then those cervical, humeral, and thoracic branches, providing life to those parts, carry with them the spiritual impression of the life of those parts; the Coronaries bear the internal likeness of the heart and its spirit; and so with the rest. Whence it happens that heaven and pure earth, constructed by a natural chemistry, are the materials of the human structure; wherefore the philosopher—ignoring that the uncreated divine spirit inhabited that created solar spirit, but attributing all things to nature—acknowledges that "the sun and man generate man," as if he had said that the solar nurseries, attracted by means of the air through inspiration, and the essence of the members of the man or father having been fused, generate man. ### CHAPTER IV.

->*On the exact method of mixing the seed with the sperm, by means of that wonderful network which the Greeks call* <term>Anastomosis</term> <note>A "coming together" or "interweaving" of vessels.</note>.<-

In my common anatomy, it was declared that two of the four preparatory seminal vessels are veins, of which the right one buds from the *vena cava* below the emulgent <note>renal</note> vein, while the left is led down from the emulgent itself; the other two are arteries from the trunk of the great artery <note>the aorta</note>, and they emerge below the emulgents. One of these turns to the left side and joins with its downward-tending partner, just as the right meets the venous one on the right side. For although these four vessels are divided into a right and left pair (for the vein relates to the artery on each side as a female to a male), at first the veins and arteries are somewhat distant from each other, but afterward they are so entwined that the veins enter the artery and the arteries the vein in a wonderful network. Thus occurs that noble and, in appearance, delightful and pleasant mixture which the Greeks called <term>anastomosis</term> <note>original: "ἀναστόμωσιν"</note>. This entanglement is prepared by the highest craftsmanship of nature, not only (as the Anatomists will have it) so that they might convert the "red seed" (as they call it) into a whitish color, but first, so that it might divide the spermatic substance in the venous vessels and the seminal substance in the arterial ones from the mass of the blood—both the natural blood springing from the liver and the vital blood which has its origin in the heart. Afterward, it acts so that they might mix the seminal form with the spermatic matter according to the likeness of the species, not otherwise than we observe the form of a thing poured through its entire elementary substance by a natural mixing. This network or *Anastomosis* is a structure like the impression of a notable seal, which in man is human, in a lion leonine, in an eagle aquiline, etc. According to this barely perceptible impression, the sperm is formed like clay, and is irrigated by its seminal spirit as if by water, and by the divine power lurking in that spirit, it is reduced into a living soul. And so the sperm and its seed are tempered to one another according to the laws of nature, and the seed is agitated by the hidden divine power within it, in the manner of a breath from a breather, so that it might set about fabricating the sperm according to the image of its created species. But the internal agent of this work is God or the divine spirit, whence the royal prophet rightly said: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all the power of them by the spirit of his mouth.* So it is that the spirit of man (which is his power of sensation) was originally formed by the divine spirit, and is moved and governed by the same according to the will of Him *who breathes where He wills*, as John testifies. And hence it was said by the <margin>Ecclesiastes 8:7</margin> wise man, that *no man has lordship over his own spirit.* Hence also Job said: *There is a spirit in man, but the inspiration of the Almighty gives him understanding*, as if he had said: in the created spirit of man there is also the uncreated spirit, which is its first act. Whence Saint Paul concludes, not without consideration, that *man is the temple of the Holy Spirit.* We say, therefore, that the mixing of the celestial form (which is the vehicle of the mind) with the elementary essence (by which the generative spirit becomes a participant of both sexes) occurs in a wonderful network of this kind. In this, the spirit—previously barely perceptible as airy or distinguishable from the venous blood, as well as that ethereal spirit not yet selected from the arterial blood by the extraction or chemistry of nature—is reduced into the form of a mist, or a whitening cloud. This division of the generative spirit from the mass of the blood, and the [union] of the sperm with its soul or vivifying spirit...

The mixing, in order to become more exact and refined, was ordained by nature through the divine will, so that this kind of entanglement descends all the way down to the testicles, and having perforated the epididymis <note>The duct behind the testis</note>, it penetrates into the very substance of the testicles. Thus, having been perfectly purified and mixed with the least amount of this kind of "cloud" <note>original: *nebula*; likely referring to a refined vapor or spirit</note>, it holds its own wind within itself, just as that greater force of the macrocosm <note>The universe</note> breathes for the motion of the internal principle, or as angels are said to move at the nod of God, whose ministers they are. And so it descends to the testicles, by which that serous and foreign substance—which was exuding from the blood mass through *diapedesis* <note>The passage of blood cells through intact vessel walls</note> along with the generative spirit—is purged and separated from the cloud or mass dedicated to generation. Thus, the "potential human" is now ready to be emitted by ejaculation from its preparatory vessels into its natural vessel or its "philosophical egg"—namely, the female womb—and be enclosed therein until perfect maturity; that is, until it is brought into the state of an actual human being.

### CHAPTER V.

->*What the philosophers think regarding the method of injecting the sperm into the womb, and the operation or progress of it once injected: and then afterwards the author's opinion on the matter is explained, relying on the testimonies of both Philosophers and Theosophists, as well as the Holy Bible.*<-

Regarding the sperm enclosing its seed, and its injection or ejaculation into the vulva, it must be understood that two actions are required for this work: namely, a **spiritual** one, which concerns the intellect and its servants or handmaidens (memory and phantasy, or imagination), and a **corporeal** one, which operates through contact. The first action, the spiritual one, concerns the soul of the sperm, or the seed. Hence, either through the sense of sight or through the imagination, the rational spirit acts upon the consideration of the desired or loved object; for the impression of the loved thing or its image is painted in the phantasy. This phantastic faculty is directed by the rational faculty both before the act of generation and during it, and in this kind of operation of the soul, the ethereal seed is prepared. Its source is the heart itself, which previously introduced it from the "aerial sea" <note>The atmosphere/breath</note> into its left ventricle by inspiration in the manner mentioned above. Therefore, through a strong imagination, the erection of the virile rod <note>The penis</note> occurs; for the animal spirits mingle themselves by means of the carotid arteries, and the fire of celestial love excites the flame previously conceived in the imagination. This flame, flowing downward through the trunk of the great artery into the private member or its "magical inner chamber," fills its capillary arteries with its breath. Thus, this member is vigorously erected by the power of the animal spirits diffused throughout it from the vital parts. By means of this erection, the sperm is drawn from the testicles through the *vasa deferentia* <note>The ducts conveying sperm</note> into those vessels called the *prostates*, or the "glandular overseers."

The second action, the corporeal or elemental one, proceeds from material contact—namely, from the motion or friction that occurs in mutual copulation, in which delight and pleasantness are excited in the whole body. Meanwhile, the purest marrow of the elements is accustomed to leap forth from its foundations and is precipitated into the spermatic vessels, and the seminal spirits descending step-by-step from the parts of the body are mixed with it. From this it happens that the well-prepared and tempered sperm is urged to give place to those newly succeeding parts, and also that it is enticed to go out into the depths of the matrix <note>The womb</note> or into the light of the air by the strong friction exciting heat—not otherwise than fire is struck from a flint by the collision of iron or steel with it. In this action, the celestial spirit also acts reciprocally and is delighted by a wonderful sympathy. From this it is clear that in this twofold action, the spiritual relates to the material as the soul to the body, or heaven to the earth.

Therefore, once the sperm with its celestial soul has been cast into the womb, it is necessary (as some maintain) that the female sperm also meet this injected sperm at that very instant; if this does not happen, they conclude that no generation can occur. Just as in the male sperm the invisible seed was like the soul to the visible sperm, so also the whole mass of the man's sperm is like the **form** to that of the woman. In this, human generation agrees with the creation of the macrocosm; for the soul of the celestial world is the lucid spirit of the super-celestial heaven, in which fire or light abounds in a most simple spirit. For in this way, the seed of the man, which is pure fire in a most limpid spirit, is compared with the nature of the sperm (the visible part of the generative moisture in the man). Similarly, just as the substance of the informed heaven, or the ethereal spirit, is the soul to the elementary world, so also the sperm of the man relates to that of the woman. Finally, just as God is present in the center of the world as **Unity**, from which both the watery matter and the lucid form (that is, duality and trinity) proceed:

So also the matter stands in human sperm: namely, the act of both its internal formal part and its external elemental part consists in its center or unity, because it is the "breath of the Almighty" <note>original: *spiraculum omnipotentis*; a reference to Job 33:4</note>, as the Holy Scriptures testify. Similarly, the menstrual blood observes the same proportion in respect to the sperm of the man and woman as the earth does to the more liquid elements and the celestial spirit. Hence it is that the philosophers have recognized that the female sperm is thicker and more humid than that of the man; thus they behave in the matrix as male and female, since that of the man imprints the **form** upon the offspring, and this of the woman receives that form, not otherwise than...

As for the preparations of the seed made in the womb by condensation and maturation, Galen maintains that in the beginning, after the complete mixing of the seeds in their vessel or "philosophical egg," a certain foam arises. <margin>Galen in the booklet *On the Seed*.</margin> From this, it seems to be argued that the secret spirit enclosed in the seed is a certain wind working slowly toward perfection. Next, he relates that by the power of this kind of enclosed wind of a triple nature, three prominent vesicles are fashioned from the said foam, in each of which a different spirit is enclosed, by which the mass or matter may be moved by every kind of motion. He says that each of these spirits intends the generation of its own material cause: namely, the middle one, which is **vital**, for the generation of the heart; the lowest, which is **natural**, for the completion of the liver; and the highest, which is **animal** <note>In this context, "animal" refers to the *anima* or soul/mind, relating to the brain.</note>, for the procreation of the brain. He concludes, therefore, that as the windiness enters into the depth of the seed, by the action of the three spirits, a certain bladder is born in the middle, another vesicle lies above near it, and another next to the lower one: from the first vesicle the heart is formed, from the second placed above, the brain, and from the third, the liver. These are his words. From which it is evident that the internal spirit is nothing other than a triform wind, which is driven by a triple internal agent, all of which have a relation to the unity of life, which all three winds with their agents seem to obey. But our Galen elsewhere describes the time of the preparation of both the foam <margin>Galen, *On the Anatomy of the Living*.</margin> and the bubbles in these words: *"During the first six days, foam appears in that matter at the end; during these, three bubbles are set over the principal members; then, through the three following days, they begin the internal outlines and punctations of the other members. During the first six days, nothing is drawn from the matrix <note>The womb.</note>, because little or nothing is lost from that matter; but during the six following days, as the windiness penetrates and the spirits tend toward the exterior, the ramifications of the veins and arteries are perfected. During the twelve following, blood enters through all the fleshy members, which is why in an abortion at that time, fleshy lumps appear; and in this space also the spinal marrow is divided in the brain through the spine of the back. Likewise, during the nine following days, the members are distinguished from one another, namely the sides from the neck, the neck from the brain and head, the hips from the buttocks, and so in each of the others; and so in total there will be 35 days, for the most part, although sometimes later, namely 40 days, sometimes faster, namely 30 days, so that five days always intervene. But truly the reason for the slowness is the remission of heat, and for the haste, its intensity."* Thus far he speaks. Others, however, maintain that once the seed is received in the matrix, the matrix is immediately closed, and from then in <margin>From Giuseppe Rosaccio, the Italian.</margin> the space of 7 days, they say three sufficiently manifest bubbles are raised and formed, from which the three principal members of the body arise, namely the Heart, the brain, and the Liver; afterward, they recognize the said members, still in potential, are reduced into visible act and their natural figures quite evidently in the space of fifteen days, so that the veins springing from the Liver, the arteries from the Heart, and the nerves from the brain are in some way perceived; and then afterward, by the working of internal heat, the lungs, stomach, intestines, bladder, and finally all other members of the body are brought to light by the thirtieth day in a man, and the thirty-seventh in a woman; and so the fetus, retaining all its organs for the completion of maturation, is accustomed to remain nine months in the womb, receiving its nourishment through the umbilical vein descending from its mother's liver. But truly, because the fetus, having completed that nine-month space of time, begins to desire a wider distance of air and more copious food, it longs by a certain natural instinct to go out from the uterine darkness into the worldly light, and tends with the greatest effort to obtain its liberty; which indeed Astrologers claim happens because of the predominance of the Moon in that month of birth. Concluding that it cannot live in the eighth month because of the governance of Saturn, nor in the sixth month as that in which Mars has his dominion. But truly the seventh month, because Jupiter presides over it, grants it life. From these things, therefore, according to the opinions of almost all philosophers and anatomists, it is clear that the triple spirit—of one essence but different in property—is the operator and fabricator in the microcosmic machine of the world, after the manner of the divine trinity. But truly, concerning the action and increase of the seed in the womb, and also concerning the order and preparation of the parts to be produced, we shall now say a few words according to our own opinion. First, therefore, we say this seed is clothed with a triple spirit, for the representation of the greater world <note>The Macrocosm.</note>, in which three spirits are found, differing in position, nature, and dignity: namely the **intellectual** or **supracelestial**, which has an angelic and discursive nature; the **ethereal** or **celestial**, in which its vital soul resides, namely in the sun; and the **aerial** or **elementary**, where the faculty of growing and nourishing changeable things predominates. To these, therefore, are referred in man that rational or animal wind or spirit raising and blowing the region of the brain; the vital spirit by which the heart is filled and fabricated; and the natural spirit, by whose breathing the liver is established. We say also that an angel or spirit <note>original: "daemon"</note> presides over each of these spirits, each of whom excels the other in dignity and office, not otherwise than the angels of a worthier spirit in the world are observed to have dominion over those spirits of the inferior spirits. Namely, Michael the Archangel of the ethereal Empyrean Heaven over the solar spirits, as these again over the elementary spirits, which are accustomed to blow from the eastern quarter in the elementary world; for angels are the ministers of GOD, who perfect all that is ordained by GOD. For GOD says, <margin>Ezekiel 37:5</margin> *"Behold, I will let spirit enter into you and you shall live, and I will give you sinews, and make flesh grow over you, etc."* And the Lord says, *"Come, spirit, from the four winds and breathe upon these slain, that they may live; and the spirit returned into them, and they lived."* From which it is clear that this spirit had the nature of many spirits. And yet Job said, <margin>Job 33:4</margin> *"The Spirit of GOD made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life,"* that is, by the mediation of his angels, who are his winds...

<margin>Bartholomew on the Variety of Things</margin> The Hebrew Doctors, setting forth nine orders of angels, called the first of them *Chayot Ha-Kodesh* <note>original: "Haioth Kadosch"</note>, that is, "holy animals" or "living beings," through which angels the God of Being <note>original: "Elieh" (Eheieh/I Am)</note> bestows the gift of existence. When we are purified and live tranquilly, then that demon is perceived by us; he seems to speak with us and clearly communicates his voice to us, though previously he was present in silence. By such a spirit, therefore, the lowest or "natural" vehicles of the sperm are inflated, which are condensed into the liver by the blast of a freezing wind. Proclus is also of this opinion, believing that one demon rules the body, another the soul, and another the mind. All the Platonists similarly placed three things in man, which they call the highest, the middle, and the lowest. By the highest, they understand the Mind or the illuminated Intellect, which Moses called the "breath of life" <note>original: *vitæ spiraculum*</note>, breathed into man by God or by His Spirit. By the lowest soul, they understood the lowest or elementary spirit, which is occupied with the flesh and worldly things; Paul calls this the "animal man" <note>referring to the *homo animalis* or natural man in 1 Corinthians 2:14</note>. The middle spirit, however, is that ethereal and vital one, participating in both extremes and connecting them both together—namely, the Mind with the corporeal spirit. Whence it happens that it tastes of the nature of both extremes. They conclude, therefore, that just as that highest portion never sins, never consents to evil, and always resists error and exhorts toward the best things, so that lower portion—the animal or carnal soul—is always submerged in evil, sin, and concupiscence, and drags one toward the worst things. Of this, Paul speaks thus: *I see another law in my members, and leading me captive in the law of sin.* But the middle spirit, since it is free by nature, can adhere to either at its will; if it adheres constantly to the higher portion, it is finally united to it and made blessed until it is taken up to God; but if it adheres to the carnal spirit, it is depraved until it becomes an evil demon.

The Platonists seem to confirm these preceding opinions. But since we made mention of angels above, I will show in a few words what Rabbi Moses <note>Maimonides</note> and Rabbi Bereshith think of them. Rabbi Moses calls the "Active Intellect" an angel from whom forms flow; he also calls him *Metattron* <note>Metatron</note>, who is the prefect over the universe, by whom all individual human virtues are governed—namely the animal and vital as well as the natural ones, which are likewise called angels, and whose multitude is infinite. For (says Rabbi Bereshith) the Creator daily creates a host of angels, whom others call "forms," inasmuch as they are formal substances with which the entire sphere of things subject to birth and decay is filled without number. Even *Hesiod*, that divine poet, seems to recognize this, speaking in this sense: *There are thrice ten thousand immortals upon the earth, guardians of mortal men for Jove, who indeed observe both justice and wretched deeds, clothed in air, going everywhere over the earth.* Furthermore, the two powers of the will in man are called angels by the wise—that is, the author of good and the author of evil, as Rabbi *Asse* testifies in his *collection*. And these are the aforementioned guardians in Hesiod, who in Latin are called spirits, any one of whom is destined for the care of lower affairs.

Indeed, in <margin>*Portalucius*</margin> it is read that from the earth even to the firmament there is no empty place, but all is full of forms, some of which are pure and capable of grace, and others foul, harmful, and tempting. *Joseph Castaliensis* also testifies to this. These spirits nevertheless correspond to one another, and the lower obey the higher regarding the actions of life, no differently than elementary demons obey celestial ones, and celestial ones obey the super-celestial, all of whom belong to the same kingdom and dominion.

For example, the seven spirits who stand before the throne of God are those princes who have dominion over the spirits of the seven Planets, upon whom they pour those illuminations which they received immediately from God. For example, the presiding Archangel or ruler of Saturn is Sabathiel; of Jupiter, Zedekiel; of Mars, Samael; of the Sun, Michael; of Venus, Anael; of Mercury, Raphael; and of the Moon, Gabriel. And so it is with the others. # Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book III.

Whether by means of angels or his formal winds <note>original: "ventis suis formalibus" — likely referring to the Platonic or Neoplatonic idea of "form-giving" breaths or spirits</note>, it is evident that although anger, mercy, and the protection of the Israelites in the desert are attributed to Jehovah, it was nevertheless his angel who performed all things in the camp of the Israelites, whether for punishment or for mercy and blessing. For Jehovah said: <margin>Exodus 23:20</margin> *Behold, I send an angel before you, to keep you in the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him and obey his voice; do not provoke him, for he will not pardon your transgressions, for my name is in him.* It is clear, therefore, that where the leading angel acts, there the divine essence is also present; and consequently, **GOD** is said to have performed this or that, since **GOD** is present by his name both in the execution carried out by the angels and in the ordering of the same, decreed in his Archetypal counsel. For an angel is like a mediating power between God and nature, by which operations are performed in things that their own nature could not have achieved without it. The act of this power is the splendor of the divine will, which drives and agitates the angel (or wind) toward the goal proposed by God, no differently than a wind is observed to move a cloud from one quarter of the world to the opposite side.

As for the order of the parts or members arranged and produced in the divine womb by such an instinct, and the manner of the inflation <note>The process of "breathing life" or expanding the form</note> of each of them into the human likeness, there is no need to consult Heathen authors for this, since it is most exactly declared in the Sacred Scriptures themselves. Indeed, it was described by the divine spirit in these words: *who formed the members of man when none of them yet existed. Have you not poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese? You clothed me with skin and flesh, and fenced me with bones and sinews, when you exercised the kindness of life toward me, and your visitation preserves my spirit. But these things you have hidden in your heart; I know that this is with you.* <margin>Job 10:9</margin> Furthermore, it is said elsewhere: *I will put spirit into you and you shall live, and I will lay sinews upon you, and will make flesh grow over you, and cover you with skin, and give you spirit so that you may live.*

By these passages of the Holy Bible, we are taught first that God is the author of the human structure. His acting instruments are a twofold wind or spirit: the first acts toward the completion of the body and its organs, and is created from the angelic nature of the three regions of the world; the last is the God-like breath of life <note>original: "Deiforme vitæ spiraculum"</note>. Hence Job said in the place cited above, after the members of his body were already finished and formed: *when you exercised the kindness of life toward me.* And Ezekiel, after the completion of the body: <margin>Ezekiel 37:5</margin> *I will give you spirit so that you may live.* But in the sequel of Ezekiel, this is declared even more clearly; for after he had concluded these words: *And as I prophesied, there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, bone to his bone. And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them. Then said the Lord: Prophesy unto the wind, come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So the spirit entered into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet.*

From this it is plain that the spirit of life entered into man—made thus from muddy seed <note>original: "spermate lutoso"</note> and adorned with all organs—from the four winds or the power of God filling the entire universe, namely after his fabrication. Thus also in the perfection of Adam, it was said that his exterior was first formed by God from the mud of the earth. And Job said: *Remember, I beseech you, that you have made me as the clay.* But then afterward it was said that God breathed into the face of man, and man was made into a living soul. From this it is clear that the "wind" by divine agitation was involved in the shaping of the seed into the human fabric and image, but in the quickening of the same, the God-like breath was present. This is also clearly declared by the speech of that suffering man <note>Job</note>: *There is a spirit in man, but the inspiration of the Almighty gives him understanding.* <margin>Job 33:4</margin> And elsewhere even better: *The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty has given me life.*

By the office of the first spirit, the body or external man with its organs is fabricated, by reason of which man is called "flesh, a spirit (or wind) that passes away and comes not again." <margin>Psalm 77:39</margin> And elsewhere: <margin>Psalm 144:3</margin> *What is man, that you acknowledge him? or the son of mortal man, that you take account of him? Man is like to vanity, etc.* And elsewhere: *Naked came man out of his mother's womb, and naked shall he return thither.* And elsewhere: *Man is miserable and most abject.* And elsewhere: <margin>Job 14:1</margin> *Man decays like a rotten thing, as a garment that is moth-eaten. And: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.* Similarly, man is elsewhere called weak and of short life. But in respect to the latter spirit, man is said to be created in the image of God <margin>Genesis 1:27</margin>, and elsewhere it is asserted that he is a little lower than the angels themselves <margin>Psalm 8:5</margin>, and that God has crowned him with glory and honor, and made him lord over the works of his hands, putting all things under his feet. Therefore, by the power of the former, he fashioned the members of the body from the male seed by a hidden power or hidden inspiration in this manner:

First, he poured out the hidden and latent form of the external man like milk—that is, he reduced it into a spermatic nature similar to milk. Then he curdled <note>original: "coagulauit"</note> that substance like cheese into a foamy substance, which, as the sinews, veins, and arteries first grew, he finally condensed into flesh and covered it with skin. Then he distinguished and stabilized the fleshy parts and members with bones and ligaments. Finally, once the members of the external man were thus produced, the Lord breathed into this mass the spirit of life, by which man was not only brought back into a living soul, but also by reason of the inspiration of the Almighty was endowed with intellect and reason, as has been confirmed from the passages previously brought forth from Holy Scripture.

The reason for the instigation of man to such an act, and the time of the maturation of the seed in the mother's womb, the wise man <note>Solomon, in the Wisdom of Solomon</note> described to us thus: <margin>Wisdom 7:2</margin> *In my mother's womb I was fashioned into flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man and the pleasure that accompanies sleep; and being born, I drew in the common air, etc.* In which speech he acknowledges the cause of intercourse to be pleasure joined with sleep, and the effect to be the seed cast into the womb, which is reduced into perfect flesh in the space of ten months. Finally (which is indeed worthy of note), the spirit of life denotes the food for its preservation, which it incessantly draws to itself, namely the common air, into which the gifts of life from God...

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Seed.

They are continually filled by God, and by their protection, creatures are maintained in their being and life. Hence Job also said: *Have you not curdled me like cheese, and clothed me with skin and flesh, etc. You have granted me life and favor, and your visitation preserves my spirit.* <note>Job 10:10-12. The author interprets "visitation" as the constant influx of divine breath.</note> That is to say, by your daily bread or the manna hidden in the air, through the medium of breathing, you refresh my hungry spirit, which without such favor of yours would languish. And in this way we see how God, through the mediation of the winds or his ministers, acts both toward the procreation of man and toward the preservation of that which is procreated.

### CHAPTER VI.

### *In which it is declared that the seed is air in a meteor, or a little cloud, or a dense mist thickened by two opposing health-giving winds, and that (contrary to the opinions of some) it is not nourished by menstrual blood in the mother's womb.*

The temperament of the West Wind is likened by philosophers to the springtime; for it is temperate and fertile in its nature, which is why it most easily produces herbs and flowers by its breath. Therefore, it is called *Favonius* <note>The Roman name for the West Wind, associated with the start of spring.</note>, as it favors the life-giving natures of natural things. For this reason, by its constant breath, all species of animals apply and devote themselves to the generation and procreation of their own kind. Hence this wind, blowing from the western equinox, is called *Zephyrus* <note>The Greek name for the West Wind.</note>, as if one were to say, "carrying life and vigor with you." And thus this wind is attributed to the lord among spirits, Raphael (whose name translates as "the Medicine of God"), and to the planet Venus, which is fertile and gracious to vital nature. Furthermore, the East Wind, called *Subsolanus*, is that wind to which all temperate things are attributed; for its spirit or breath is sweet, pure, subtle, and healthy, especially in the morning time, as it does not tolerate poisonous spirits. Thus it happens that this wind blows properly for both bodies and spirits, as we shall discuss more extensively in our treatise on the causes of health. For as Tedacus Levi says: *Michael, who is the spirit governing the Eastern winds, is on the side of mercy, and the Sun, which is his planet, is on the side of life.*

<margin>Book on Numbering.</margin>
Therefore, the most excellent Doctors—not only of the Hebrews but also of the Philosophers—make these two opposing winds merciful and favorable to life and generation. These winds, blowing together, act upon the intermediate air (just as the male spirit acts with the female in the womb) for the generation of a "meteor" <note>In this period, "meteor" referred to any atmospheric phenomenon, including clouds, rain, or mist.</note>, namely the production of the spermatic humor. In this way are produced those yellowish little clouds, evidence of clear air, which are frequently driven from west to east and vice versa by the force of the spirit predominating in the air. For contrary winds of equal vigor blowing together condense the intermediate air into a disposition similar to the winds themselves. However, the nature of the predominant wind will prevail more in that aerial meteor than the nature of the opposite one. For example: if the West Wind blows more strongly, the nature of the cloudlet will be moderately cold and moist, in the manner of the female seed (which is the temperament of Venus), and then the meteor will migrate toward the East. But if the East Wind blows more strongly, the nature of the cloudlet will participate more in the disposition of that wind; thus the air condensed in that way will be hotter and drier, participating in the life-giving disposition of the Sun, and will be like the male seed. Nevertheless, the nature of the opposite wind will perhaps still have dominion within it. Therefore, the meteor procreated from the breaths of such healthy winds leads to generation in both the macrocosm <note>The universe as a whole.</note> and the microcosm <note>The human being as a reflection of the universe.</note>. In this process, the eastern spirit acts as the hidden active principle in the seed, and the western spirit as its hidden passive principle; their common womb is the milky or misty air in which the mysteries of these winds are enclosed. Hence, in the macrocosm, such cloudlets or mists falling upon the earth provide the seed for plants and vegetables, by which they grow and produce their likenesses, and their seeds are impregnated for new generation.

In the microcosm, however, and also in other animals, prolific meteors of this kind are brought forth in the blood-like or aerial spirit by the most hidden breath of these spirits. These fall into the microcosmic earth—that is, into the seminal vessels hidden in the viscera—and then, leaping from them into the female wombs, they strive to procreate likenesses of their species. For there are two direct winds in heaven that blow toward generation, namely these two, insofar as they are on the side of life and mercy. But the other two direct winds, namely the North and South, tend mostly toward corruption (as they are on the side of severity and disease) unless they are tempered by the other winds. Hence, according to Rabbi Tedacus in the place cited above, Gabriel presides over the North in the power of judgment and severity, just as Noriel or Uriel presides over the South, in which region the great demon Meririm is said to rage and seethe, producing almost all corrupt and putrid infirmities. Therefore, from the heart in man, as if from the rising of the Sun, a generative and healthy breath is blown toward the west—that is, into the seminal vessels. This breath, after being inspired by the East wind or the breathing Heart, also condenses the air (or the subtle part of the elements) attracted from the entire body into the spermatic vessels. Thus is produced the "meteor" of generation; for its coagulation into bones and flesh, the North wind is required, by whose breath the seed...

# Section I. Portion III. Part III. Book III.

The seed is curdled just like cheese, for Saturn, who dominates there, is cold and dry; and so, for its irrigation and growth, a bloody rain descends from the liver. In this way, the spirits of all the winds <note>The author uses "winds" as a metaphor for the vital breaths or forces of the four elements.</note> concur in the composition of the fetus. Thus it is said to be composed of the four complexions or elements. Therefore, two healthy winds concur for the generation and health of the fetus and preserve it in its being, while the other two afflict it with diseases and corruption.

Once the seed is enclosed in the womb, it is necessary to understand by what nourishment it is fed so that it may reach the completion of a fetus. However, in the resolution of this doubt, philosophers and some physicians seem to disagree. Some believe that the substance of retained menses <note>Menstrual blood.</note> concurs to compose the external or bodily part of the offspring; they believe this all the more because the menses usually cease in pregnant women. But others reject this reasoning for two reasons: first, because it is not likely that a thing so poisonous as the female menses could construct flesh so tender and fresh, rather than destroying and corrupting it. For (as Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, Roman naturalist.</note> testifies) the aforementioned menses are of such great malice that by their touch alone nettles wither, seeds become sterile, a mirror loses its brightness, the edge of a knife is blunted, and dogs tasting them become rabid. Therefore, it is not right to believe that the healthy structure of the fetus and its growth arise from a thing so impure. Second, because (they say) in pregnant women, the heat increases in respect to the living creature existing in generation, and consequently the menses are destroyed and consumed by it.

But I myself think that the menses do not appear at that time because their subtle part passes into the increase of the blood, so that the good blood which concurs for the nutrition of the fetus can be continually supplied. Furthermore, a portion of it, divided from its poisonous and earthy dregs by many strainings, can contribute something to the generation of milk; for in the menstrual blood, there is a portion of good blood mixed with the bad and poisonous blood. The fecal parts, however, are ejected from the body and flow out during the cleansing after childbirth. Yet, physicians confess that the principal nourishment of the fetus is drawn from the liver by means of the umbilical vein. But the Holy Scriptures also teach us this clearly, in which we read: <margin>Wisdom 7:2</margin> *In my mother’s womb I was fashioned into flesh, being compacted in blood in the period of ten months from the seed of man*, where it is not said that the seed was curdled into flesh, but the seed with blood; <margin>Leviticus 12:2</margin> and not menstrual blood, for in respect to that it is written: *If a woman has conceived seed and borne a male child, she shall be unclean seven days. And elsewhere: she shall continue thirty days in the blood of her purifying after birth; during which time she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary.* Also in the time of an unclean flow or menses: namely, when the flow <margin>Leviticus 15:20</margin> is in her flesh for seven days, let her be in her separation, and whoever touches her shall be unclean until evening. But "good blood" (which the wise man <note>Solomon, traditionally the author of the Book of Wisdom.</note> mentions here) is understood where it is said <margin>Genesis 9:4</margin> *that blood is the seat of souls.* From such blood, therefore, mixed with the seed, the substance of the infant is fabricated, according to the opinion of Solomon cited above.

### Chapter VII.

->*On the manner of infecting and corrupting the seed, by which purulent Gonorrhea is produced; likewise, that seed held too long in its vessels sometimes contracts a demonic disposition.*<-

Just as the seed is a most precious thing in its pure and unpolluted nature, insofar as it reaches toward the perfection of a rational creature and proceeds by the natural way of generation, so also by the contrary way, if it be polluted by a preternatural reason and infected by a foreign form and a pollution contrary to its nature, it tends not toward generation, but conversely toward corruption. That is, it is reduced by a meteorological medium not to the "goal toward which" (generation), but to the "point from which"—namely, into that which it was before by a destructive nature. Do we not observe by equal reasoning that clouds gathered by a southern wind, or air condensed by the breathing of the same, are dissipated by the demons or forms of an opposing blast and reduced as if to nothing—namely, into thin air, such as they were at the beginning of their motion? Thus, the southern spirits prepared for the generation of clouds and rain are hindered in their progress by the strongly resisting northern spirits and are driven back to their windy caves in the southern region.

And the reasoning for opposites is the same: for if the northern spirits previously predominating and producing snow and hail are overcome by an opposing wind now predominating, those <term>meteors</term> <note>In this period, "meteors" referred to any atmospheric phenomena, including rain, snow, and hail.</note> which were on the way to generation—namely, in the progression from the "point from which" (simple air) to the middle, and then from the meteorological middle to a perfect mixture—are suddenly dissolved by a southern blast. They are changed from the earthy hardness of hail or the dryness of snow first into thick air, and then by an Eastern wind they are converted into that thing which they were before; that is, they are led backward from the motion of generation to that of corruption. We say, therefore, if a depraving <term>demon</term> <note>Here used in the Neoplatonic sense of a spiritual force or "form" that shapes matter.</note> has dominion over the spermatic mass, it drives away from it its genital demons sent into it from the fountain of life, and it also destroys its works by corrupting them. For as we see clean and healthy air, by the frequency of pernicious demons or spirits, incline from its healthy disposition to a poisonous or contagious nature, and tend not toward life but toward death, so also the seed is harmed and destroyed by a defiled or pestilential habit, and can no longer proceed to the path of generation, but flows down in its substance no differently than...

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Seed.

Just as a cloud frozen by Northern winds flows down and is dispersed by a southern breeze, so the world proper to the seed is the female egg, or the concavity of the womb. Its air fills the seed like a bladder; if it is joined to benign spirits or forms, it will act favorably upon the seed and lead it to the goal of generation. But if preternatural forms swim within it—which have leaped forth either from French ulcers <note>original: "ulceribus gallicis"; a common historical term for syphilis</note>, or from a contagious or poisonous substance—it does not only destroy and corrupt the healthy seed cast into that place. Indeed, that contagious air, at the moment the seed is emitted by the man into the female womb, is drawn into his own seminal vessels in place of the ejected seed (lest a vacuum be admitted in them). It then continually corrupts the matter of the seed; thus, by successive motion, it descends into those vessels from the body, and with its poisonous spirit dissolves the solid seeds, corrupts its healthy parts, and when it invades the entire spirit of the blood with its intoxicated breath, it strives to infect the whole machine of man with the so-called venereal plague <note>original: "lue venerea"; syphilis</note> and to kill by infection.

Sometimes also, if this spermatic substance remains too long in the path of its motion or natural progression beyond the statutes of nature—that is, after its exact preparation, being detained from the place assigned to it by nature for generation, namely the womb—it is frequently accustomed to take on a new nature. It contracts and puts on a foreign spirit which is most opposed to the nature of the parents; indeed, a demon <note>The author uses "daemonium" here to refer to a corrupting spiritual force or "spirit" of disease rather than necessarily a sentient devil.</note> converting its generative nature into ruin. It rejoices to attract to itself a spiritual monster (thirsting to procreate something by a mad appetite), by whose tempestuous disposition the connatural spirits of the parents are oppressed; indeed, they sometimes seem to be suffocated. 

This can be seen in older virgins, and also in widows and other women abstaining from intercourse for a long time, who are afflicted by cachexia <note>A state of ill health and wasting</note> and tremendous suffocations of the womb <note>original: "suffocationibus matricis"; historically referred to as 'hysterical suffocation,' believed to be caused by the womb wandering or being deprived of its natural function</note> as if they had been possessed by a demon. Likewise, men who practice a life of continence are perceived to be vexed by not a few infirmities (in which demons also seem to have their portions), namely Epilepsy, the disease called "Hercos" <note>likely referring to the "Herculean disease," an old name for epilepsy</note>, raging melancholy, or mania, or a solitary madness seducing the infirm from the society of men, and others of this kind, concerning which I have written more abundantly elsewhere.

->C O N C L U S I O N.<-

<margin>Pimander 1. <note>Referring to the first book of the Corpus Hermeticum</note></margin>
From these things which have been said, we have revealed not only the internal agents of the seed, but also its external patients <note>In the philosophical sense: that which is acted upon</note>, which are derived from the purity or subtlety of the elements. We have demonstrated that the internal acts descend from the celestial regions, while the external substance springs from the sublunary ones. All of these things Hermes Trismegistus <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the Hermetic corpus is attributed</note> depicts so clearly in a few words: *The female, having power over the union of air and water, took maturity from fire and spirit from the air, and nature conjoined them to fashion the likeness of man.* 

We, however, contemplating the super-celestial agents a little more deeply both in the elements and in the ether, have attempted to explain them: namely, the virtues and efficacies of angels, both good and malignant. These are the middle instruments between God and man, or most swift ministers always ready to execute the commands of God upon the creatures of both visible worlds—namely, the celestial and the terrestrial. These angels, or formal winds, hide within the spirit of the seed no differently than a most active wind within a cloud, which conducts itself as the soul to the body. And thus we have briefly completed the description of the winds in the western microcosm.

### CHAPTER I.
#### Concerning the relationship of the human heart with the worldly sun, and how the Heart is the sun of the microcosm, just as the sun is the heart of the macrocosm.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'Q' featuring floral and vine motifs within a square frame.</image-desc>

Just as Phoebus <note>A poetic name for Apollo or the Sun</note>, shining with golden hair and holding the scepter of the world, is observed to sit like a king and Emperor in the very midst of heaven, ruling and governing all things by the breath of his life—as one in whom, according to Iamblichus and many others, *all the virtues of the heavenly bodies reside*; for Proclus did not hesitate to assert *that at the sight of the sun, all the powers of all the heavenly beings are gathered into one, which are finally scattered into this lower world through his fiery breathing-holes*—so also we perceive the heart to behave in the lesser world <note>The "Microcosm" or human body</note>. Indeed, Heraclitus seems to explain this comparison clearly to us, intentionally falling into this discourse: *If you take away the sun from the world (he says), what is our poor body if the soul is missing? No pulsing vein is contracted there; no judgment remains to be felt; there is no vital breath in it, nor any respiration.* For this reason, it has seemed to some, not without consideration, to call the Sun the "heart of heaven," because just as in the heart the living fount and spring of blood is found, gently moistening and watering the other members of the human body and pouring out the act of life everywhere both upward and downward, so also in the sun the faculty of nourishing and preserving all things, both higher and lower, seems to be enclosed as if in a sanctuary of life. It is from the sun that life, or innate heat, is breathed into the lower things—and indeed even the higher ones—by means of his light. By a similar logic, the heart disperses the spirit of life from its storehouse <note>original: "myrothecio," literally a spice-box or ointment-jar</note> by means of its rays, which are shot out everywhere in the human body, both upward and downward through the branches of the aorta, according to that saying of Hermes Trismegistus:

<margin>Pimander, 10</margin>
> The spirit, diffused through the veins and arteries and the blood, stirs the animal on every side; and it supports the suspended mass of the body.

We see also that, just as the sun by its motion and vital breath inspires and gives life to all things in the visible world, similarly and in like respect, the heart of man, by its action through the medium of the vital spirit, floods and inspires all parts of the body by means of the arteries. If the sun is the spring of healthful heat and vital spirits, by a similar relationship the Heart is a most overflowing fount of innate and beneficial heat. Furthermore, just as the action of solar heat is pleasing and favorable to the things of the earth, air, and waters, so also the heat of the heart is graciously present to the things of the human body. We see also that just as the celestial sun is accustomed to be hindered or at least sometimes disturbed by the imbalance and labors of the other stars—namely by Eclipses and conjunctions—so also the human heart is disturbed and afflicted by the imbalance and affections of the other internal organs. Indeed, just as the hindrances and labors of the sun are accustomed to bring harm to the earth, so also the disturbances of the heart never cease to bring damage to bodily things; so much so that when the sun labors, the machinery of the world labors, and when the heart labors, the entire fabric of the human body falls ill. Furthermore, the sun is observed never to interrupt its natural motion, and the human heart also shows itself constant in its motion—that is, immune from interruption. It is situated in the middle of the chest <note>original: "Thoracis meditullio"</note> no differently than the sun is in the center of heaven, from which it is most clearly evident that the heart is accustomed to perform this same office in the microcosm that the sun performs in the greater world. Therefore, so that man might most rightly...

# On the Mystical Anatomy of the Heart.

<note>original: "De Mystica Cordis Anatomia"</note>

...most [wisely] by Hermes Trismegistus <note>A legendary Hellenistic figure to whom various mystical and alchemical texts are attributed.</note> *is called the son of the world*, and for this reason is called the microcosm <note>The "little world" or man, reflecting the "macrocosm" or great world.</note>, since all its members were derived from those of the greater world at its creation, in no other way than those of an infant in generation arise from those hidden in the parents' seed. It follows from this that the heart is the son of the worldly sun, which is also confirmed by the fact that it is seen to imitate the sun in all its actions and functions, and especially in its primary action; for as the rays of the Sun relate to the aerial spirit as male to female, so also the vital action whose fountain is the heart is adapted in a similar ratio to the natural spirits in man. The source of these, namely the liver, is divided from the region of the heart by the diaphragm, just as the mass of the air and its mid-region (which is situated in the middle part of the same) is divided from its Solar husband by the Sieve of the Moon <note>A metaphorical reference to the atmospheric boundary or the lunar sphere filtering celestial influences.</note>, through which it liberally rains its solar seeds into the air, in no other way than a male [pours] his seeds into the womb of a woman.

### CHAPTER II.

->That the heart is the Eastern region of the microcosm, and how it relates to the East of the macrocosm.<-

**IN** the first book of this treatise, where we distinguished the microcosm into its quarters in imitation of the macrocosm, and also attributed to each of them its own proper wind or breath, we applied its eastern part to the heart not without consideration. Just as we referred the spermatic vessels and the places adjacent to them to the point opposite to it for the reasons produced by us in this third book, we shall now proceed to declare with clear reasons how the quarter or region of the microcosm assigned to the heart agrees in all things with the disposition of the worldly East.

First, therefore, from those things related in the preceding chapter, we can gather how great a relationship exists between the solar body and that of the animal heart, and how close a friendship and kinship exists between these most principal bodies in both worlds; since this [the heart] is as it were the son of that [the sun], so that the Sun, in a reciprocal manner, is to be held as the father of the heart. For as the Sun in the macrocosm is the fountain and origin of life, so also in the microcosm the gifts of life are observed to spring from the sanctuary of the heart. But indeed, we observe the Sun to have its daily rising in the East, which region is therefore attributed by Astrologers to the life of the native <note>The person for whom a birth chart is cast.</note>; for they call the first house of the Hemisphere the "angle of the east," namely that place in which both the Sun and the remaining planets, rising upon our horizon at the moment of birth, claim for themselves the names of the lords of the generation and life of the native. For the first house, called the Horoscope <note>The Ascendant or the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth.</note> (as the whole crowd of Astrologers testifies), signifies the life and body of the native, and also the beginning of life and birth, whence they also call it "Life" itself. To this house they assign triplicities, and to each of them as many lords, the first of whom they affirm argues for the life and nature of the native (namely, what he will love or what will come to him in the beginning of his life), the second for the strength of the body and the state of life in middle age, and the third for the end of life. From this, therefore, it is evident how great the force of life is in this angle, and accordingly this Pivot <note>term: Cardo (Pivot/Hinge). One of the four critical points in an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Descendant, Midheaven, and Imum Coeli.</note> or quarter is the defense of life, the fan of life, from which its soul—namely the Solar virtue—is breathed into the hemisphere of the world. Whence those well-versed in the mysteries of nature attribute the eastern angle to Michael (who is the Solar Archangel), whose office is to resist the malice of evil demons, and consequently to preside diligently and happily over the life and health of creatures, as we shall declare more widely in the following chapter. From this, therefore, we see that after the intense darkness of the night, and the quasi-death of the hemisphere, or the privation of the lucid form and the life of the preceding day, the Sun—the sanctuary of life—rising again with a new light of life, regenerates and resuscitates the worldly spirit which was as if deformed and overwhelmed by darkness. Whence we also observe the origin of rising life and light to exist in the angle of the east. In a plainly similar way in the procreation of man, we see that once the seed is corrupted, or after the removal of the prior seminal form, a new light of life and form is accustomed to rise again in the dark mass of the fetus, to take away its deformity, and to restore a new human form. Thus, after the privative night in the seed, the Sun of life rising in the angle of the heart (which is the eastern one) or the horoscope of the microcosm, yearns to produce a new life, a new day, a new form and being, and a new man. From this it is clear that the heart is the beginning of man, the fountain of life, and the Sunrise of the microcosmic day, in no other way than the Sun from the east of the macrocosm is seen to bring life, light, and a new regeneration to the world. Just as, conversely, in the region of the world opposite to the east where the sun sets, the hemisphere of the world is seen to be killed by its setting—that is, it is weighed down by darkness and the privation of the diurnal form. So also by equal reason we observe that the vivifying outflow of the heart (most full of rays and spirits of life, and most fit for generation), leaping out from the left chamber of the heart, sets into the spermatic vessels situated opposite to it, where the dung-filled and dark viscera (compared to the western earth) are placed by nature, and is then precipitated into the womb; and then it is likened to the setting of the Sun. Whence in several places of the Holy Scriptures the grave is compared to the abyss and the infernal lodging. For thus we notice that a grain of wheat must be cast into the earth and die in its superficial depth before its spirit can rise again to life. By equal reason we also say that the rising of the celestial sun in the world makes as it were a regeneration of a new day; the rising of the animal sun from the seed in the matrix, and of the vegetable sun in the earth, also make a new day or life. Thus this axiom of the Philosophers is best verified in this: namely, that *the corruption of one is the generation of another, and consequently generation follows corruption*. The reason for these opposite mutations in the world is that action and resistance which is made between form and matter, so that matter, having entire dominion over form...
