# In Defense against the 12th Analysis
## Signature Dd 4

From these things, therefore, it is clearly evident that the string of the **monochord** <note>A single-stringed instrument used to demonstrate mathematical musical intervals</note> in its entirety refers to the **Father**, who, as he is Unity, is also everything that exists, and fills all things with his harmony. But by dividing himself into equal parts according to his justice, he demonstrates the emanation of unity into duality—namely, that which is the image of the **Second Person** <note>The Son/Christ</note>, who fashions the world and its parts by harmonic proportions. And the second portion of unity, proceeding from the center of the string **c.** (or the first portion) just as from the Father and the Son—namely, the space **c. 𝄢.** <note>The symbol for the bass clef/lower register</note> related to the **Holy Spirit**—is that property which joins **c.** in a spherical progress with **C.** in a union of love and harmony. It gives life and virtue to all creatures of the world, according to that saying of the royal Psalmist: *By the Word of the Lord the heavens were made firm, and by the Spirit from his mouth all their power.* It is as if he were saying that by the emanation of the perfect consonance of the **Diapason** <note>The Octave</note>—that is, the shining Word—from the central **C.** (the Father emitting the light of his face) to the worldly **c.**, the heavens were made firm; and by the emanation of the Diapason consonance (that is, **c. 𝄢.** proceeding from both), the world was completed and its creatures given form.

But because the **Sun** in this world is endowed with the fullest divinity (insofar as it is most full of Light, according to St. Augustine and others: *The more light something has in itself, the more it seems to claim God for itself*; and that saying of Plato and Apuleius: *Do not speak of God without Light, seeing as he is the father of light*), it therefore participates most greatly in the harmonic perfection of God. Consequently, its proportion to God is as **C.** to **c.**—namely, a double proportion <note>2:1 ratio</note>, which produces the most perfect consonance, the **Diapason**. Because of its most perfect aspect toward Him, **Wisdom** (which is the highest perfection of all things leaping forth from the fountain of perfection) is said to have *placed her Tabernacle in the Sun*. Here, then, we have **Alpha** the beginning and **Omega** the end, in the middle of which is placed the most beautiful of all creatures <note>The Sun</note>, being more fit and worthy because of the most polished and pure substance of its body to receive the rays of highest perfection from both extremes of the circular perfection, joined and continued to one another by a union of inexplicable love.

We see, therefore, from the diligent mystery of this **Monochord**, how God is the center and how He is the circumference: namely, the center hiding within himself before creation, and the circumference in and after creation through the revelation and expansion of his rays in a circuit. Finally, He is the whole in the whole, or "all that is," insofar as He is a circle. For just as the string (which they compare to the radius of a circle) fills all the intervals of the monochord, so also God, revealing himself circularly in creation or rising peripherally from the center of darkness, is said to fill the worldly spirit or the "waters" with the splendor of the **Word** (which is likewise God), according to that saying of St. Peter: *From water, in water, and through water the heaven and earth were made by the mediation of the Word.* We see also by what proportion of perfection God migrated into the Sun after creation: namely, by the leap of a double proportion. From which it is clear that the Sun must be in the very center between God as the Center and Him as the Circumference. And this place where the Sun walks is called by the Platonists the **sphere of equality**, as if they were saying that in this place the radius is equally divided into a double and equal proportion from both extremes (namely, from God the center and God the circumference), constituting a double Diapason.

But where does **Johannes** <note>Likely Johannes Kepler, the author's primary intellectual rival</note> find an error here among these three principal terms of the general World Harmony? Or where in these proportions is there found so grave a "sin" as he seems to claim in text 26? Or is this demonstration of mine veiled in the most perplexed riddles and mysteries? Does this not seem to agree with the opinions of both the Philosophers and the Holy Scriptures? Does not the judgment and reason of any man of sound mind confirm this? Indeed, if the Reader prepares himself to consider and contemplate this with due respect, he will observe that the matter truly cannot be otherwise.

But Johannes will perhaps ask: how can the remaining intervals of the world be filled if only these three terms are admitted? I answer that where a greater consonance (namely the **Diapason**) is found, there the lesser consonances are necessarily understood to be within it; and where these lesser ones are imprinted on the world monochord, there even the smallest intervals are included, namely the **tone** and **semitones**. Furthermore, we can fill these smaller intervals of the monochord in this way: by starting from the dissolution of the composite and moving backward through the path of generation, proceeding from **Alpha** to **Omega**. We count the orders of the heavens as they are commonly accepted—that is, in the quantitative distance and position of place—although in truth God’s harmonic progression in nature occurs according to degrees of refinement and purification, through which the subtle is reached, and the corruptible becomes incorruptible, according to the Apostle: *What is sown corporeal and corruptible, shall rise spiritual and incorruptible.*

Therefore, the space between **C.** and **D.** relates to that between **Earth** and **Air** (namely, **Water**), corresponding to a **tone**. And again, between **D.** and **E.** <note>Original text says D. and D., likely a typo for D. and E.</note> to that interval between **Water** and **Fire** (namely, **Air**), assigning another **tone**. And between **E.** and **F.** to that between **Air** and the **Moon** (namely, **Fire**), which corresponds to a **Semitone** because of its sharpness and thinness. And intervals of this kind in the sublunary heaven are found among themselves in a **sesquialter** proportion <note>3:2 ratio</note>, from which the imperfect consonance of the **Diatessaron** <note>The Fourth</note> arises, whose nature best suits this region of the world, as it is imperfect and subject to generation, corruption, and change. We proceed now to the intervals of the middle region of the world, or the ethereal heaven, and we say that the space between **F.** and **G.** relates to the sphere of the **Moon** between Fire and that of **Mercury**, and corresponds to a single tone. And that between **G.** and **a.** to the sphere of **Mercury** between that of the Moon and **Venus**, related to another tone. And that between **a.** and **b.** to the sphere of **Venus** placed between Mercury and the **Sun**, compared to a third tone. And **b.** to **c.** to the sphere of the **Sun** between those of Venus and **Mars**, responding to the condition of a **Semitone**.

# Robert Fludd’s Reply

...on account of the subtle, pure, fiery, and hidden power of the solar nature; and thus the material **Fifth** <note>original: *Diapente*</note> is procreated, which is a consonance of lesser perfection; for such is the nature of the heaven, to which the **Fifth Essence** <note>The *Quinta Essentia* or ether, the fifth element beyond earth, water, air, and fire.</note> most rightly seems to correspond because of this consonance. And from these two lesser consonances, the material **Octave** <note>original: *Diapaſon*</note> has arisen. Next, we shall proceed in the same manner from God in the circumference—or the Heaven of Heavens—to complete the spiritual **Octave** in the Sun in this way: by dividing according to the midpoint of the monochord string into parts similar to the previous ones, thus: I say that the interval between C, c, and b holds itself as the first Hierarchy of Angels between the seat of God and the region of the second Hierarchy; and this space, because of its infinite purity and subtlety, corresponds to a **semitone**. And that between b and a holds itself as the interval of the middle Hierarchy, corresponding to a **whole tone**. And that from a to g relates to the interval of the lowest Hierarchy, referred to as a second **tone**. And thus we have the spiritual **Fourth** <note>original: *Diateſſaron*</note>. Then, that from g to f holds itself as the interval of the eighth sphere <note>The sphere of the fixed stars.</note> compared to a **semitone**, and f to e relates to the sphere of Saturn as a **tone**, and e to d to that of Jupiter responding as another **tone**, and finally d to c to that of Mars, which is contiguous to the Sun; and thus we have the spiritual **Fifth** produced even in the middle heaven, from which joined together the greatest and most perfect consonance, the **Octave**, is produced. 

But if we wish to fill these intervals in a mystical rather than a common way, then we must proceed in all things by a path contrary to this; because from the center in the first creation, God, shining forth, indeed first filled the spiritual **Octave**, beginning with the creation of the spheres and the worthier creatures, as is demonstrated in our **Monochord**. And in this way, the division of the mundane monochord into two consonances is completed. And although here Johannes has attempted to attack this division because of the difference of the heavens in dimension, I reply to him here as elsewhere: that one gross weight does not differ in philosophical weight from one that is spread out, and consequently units are not measured by the same lines but by weights. Wherefore I advise the readers to note here, that they should not understand my substances to be of quantitative dimensions, but differing in formal quality. Just as if the same thing in the same substance and degree of quantity—once raw, now more mature, pure, transparent, subtle, and incorruptible by the predominance of a lucid form within it—whereby that same thing can be led back from the nature of the earth through natural purification to the nature of the Spirit surrounding God himself; in the middle degree, the Sun presents itself to either extreme, responding through the **Octave** consonance. 

For example: the empty Earth, darkness and as it were nothing, is changed into water by the appearance of light; and then by the continuous action of divine Light, that water is reduced into air by purification; and afterward, through a third degree, that air rises into elemental fire by the operation of the **Word** <note>The *Logos*.</note>; and that into ether through a fifth degree; and then that purifying light gathers itself in the substance of the Sun, according to that saying of **Hippocrates**, the divine Philosopher and Physician: *That immortal thing, which is called heat, when all things were confused, departed into the highest periphery, which the Ancients called the ether.* And **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>original: *Mercurius Triſmeg.*</note> in his sacred discourse: *There was* (he says) *an infinite shadow in the abyss, water above, and a thin intellectual spirit was within the chaos by divine power; and when all things had been indistinct, the light things afterward flew forth into the high region, the heavy things settled under the moist sand, with things distinguished and balanced, which were carried by a fiery spirit, the heaven shone forth into seven circles.* 

In this way and by this reasoning, the wise have diligently observed the degrees of the **World Harmony**, through which, by means of the **Ladder of Truth**, we ascend from the earth into heaven, even to the solar body, through the material **Octave** consonance; and then afterward from the Sun to the seat of the Creator himself through the degrees of another **Octave**, which is therefore called spiritual. And this is that **Jacob’s Ladder**, through which the Patriarch dreamed in truth and not in fiction that Angels were descending from heaven to earth, and ascending again from earth to heaven. Again, according to the three Enneads of **Plato** (999), we have disposed this mundane Harmony by dividing the monochord into three **Octave** consonances, as is explained clearly enough in the aforesaid example; and to each great consonance, nine stations are attributed with nine voices, which concur with the **Fifth** and **Fourth**, from which the **Octave** is composed, responding accordingly: just as is explained in my *Harmony* in the *History of the Macrocosm and Microcosm*.

# In Defense of the Twelfth Book of the Annals

With respect to the Trinity, the properties of the Godhead working within it are distinguished. Therefore, according to the model of both the greater world <note>the Macrocosm</note> and the lesser world <note>the Microcosm, or Man</note>—which is the image of Wisdom flashing forth before all things into the darkness of the world—God created both the world and Man. (Hence, Hermes Trismegistus called Man the "son of the World," just as he called the world the "son of God.") For just as the world is divided into the Empyrean heaven, the ethereal Spirit, and the elementary region, so too is Man fashioned from a divine mind, a living spirit, and an opaque body. In exactly the same way, Moses divided the Ark or Tabernacle into a portion called the Holy of Holies, where the Cherubim were; a middle region adorned with gold and seven lamps; and a part subject to the changes of the sky and air, destined for the slaughter and death of cattle. So also Solomon’s Temple, following the model of Moses’s Tabernacle, was distinguished into three parts, each excelling the other in dignity.

Therefore, Wisdom (or the Word) is the image of the Father; the World is the image of Wisdom; Man is the image of the world; the Tabernacle of Moses is the image of Man; and finally, the Temple of Solomon is a likeness of the Tabernacle. Through the emanation of Wisdom from the Father, the perfection of the first Harmony is achieved through the resonance of the *Diapason* <note>an octave</note> in this world. This occurs through another *Diapason* in the unity of essence—which, starting from the Father as the source or center, and Wisdom as the Son and the bright river of life or diameter filling the circle, and establishing a tabernacle in the sun—the third Person of the same essence joins the two extremes into one by an inviolable bond.

So also in the great name, the Tetragrammaton <note>the four-letter Hebrew name of God, YHWH</note>, <term>Iod</term> <note>the letter Y</note> passes through <term>He</term> <note>the letter H</note> into <term>Vau</term> <note>the letter W</note>, and again through the second <term>He</term>, the <term>Vau</term> returns to the <term>Iod</term> from which it proceeded. Here, <term>He</term> is the sign of spirit or breathing; it is that loving and eternal "glue" by which and through which the second Person goes out from the first and returns to the first.

So also in the fabric of the world, Wisdom went out from the bosom of the Father—or the dark *Aleph*, or the hidden God, or His unity, or center—and immersed itself into the multiplicity of the world. In the spiritual Sun (that is, in the bright spirit created on the first day), it placed the tabernacle of its perfection through the first *Diapason* of the world. Because of its subtlety and purity, this space was the most capable of containing all things; and thus the interval of this *Diapason* harmony, springing immediately from the center **C** to **c**, is the most capacious of all. In the divine idea or Great Name, this refers to the first <term>He</term>, in which the <term>Iod</term> or Light immerses itself. In the world, it refers to the Empyrean heaven—the fiery, super-celestial, intellectual, and angelic world—divided into nine grades of Angels, compared to unities or "roots" because of their simplicity. These grades represent the first series of the <term>Enneads</term> <note>groups of nine</note>, signifying nine unities; this is the work of the first day of creation. In Man, the Mind with its nine dimensions is compared to this region; in the Tabernacle of Moses, the Holy of Holies; in the Temple of Solomon, its most secret part guarding the Ark of God.

Next, through a completed middle *Diapason*, the second region of the World is formed: the firmament, or the starry sky, or the ether, or the celestial region, modeled after the highest heaven. For just as the <term>Iod</term> (the source of Light) first entered the <term>He</term> (the source of the clearest spirit) for the creation of the Empyrean heaven—that is, the rays of divine light once hidden were then diffused through a purer worldly spirit, and in this way Light was created as the first creature—so also the rays of that same <term>Iod</term> in the Empyrean spirit, immersing themselves more deeply into a worldly and thicker spirit, produced the spirit in the world. This is related to the Son in the Trinity, just as that Angelic spirit is related to the Father (hence that saying of the Prophet King <note>David</note> previously cited: *By the word of the Lord the heavens were made firm*, etc.). This Heaven is denoted in the Tetragrammaton by the letter <term>Vau</term>, which is the middle between the first <term>He</term> (spirit) and the second <term>He</term>, acting like a firmament separating the waters from the waters.

And here, a less perfect harmony, the *Diapente* <note>a perfect fifth</note>, ends in the Sun, where the Word placed His Tabernacle; and the *Diatessaron* <note>a perfect fourth</note>, a still less perfect harmony, ends in the Moon, denoting the Moon's imperfection compared to the Sun. Both the *Diapente* and *Diatessaron* together constitute the *Diapason* of life, or the intermediate octave. This spirit is denser and thicker than the first, and the first informed spirit serves this one as the soul serves the body. It is divided into nine spheres, which stand as "squares" to those of the Angels; in respect to their thinness, the spheres of the ether are as roots to squares. In Man, we compare the vital Spirit to this heaven; in the Tabernacle of Moses, the gilded part where the seven lamps are (the icons of the seven Planets); in the Temple of Solomon, its heart or middle part and its mysteries.

Finally, God, descending still more deeply into multiplicity toward the periphery of things, produced the material and elementary *Diapason* of the world. This was the work of the third day, in which the letter of the Tetragrammaton, <term>Vau</term>, immersed itself into the final spirit <term>He</term>—that is, into the lower waters of the world situated beneath the firmament—just as the letter <term>Iod</term> did into the first <term>He</term> or the upper waters. This heaven is attributed to the Holy Spirit, since it derived its soul from the first and second heavens as if from the Father and the Son; and this spirit is said to "blow where it wills." Properly, the soul of this heaven is the substance of the middle heaven, just as that of the middle is a portion of the superior heaven. Thus, ether is the body and the Empyrean heaven is its soul; air is the body and ether is its soul; and the matrix or final receptacle of all these is the earth.

Therefore, this lowest region is to the superior ones as "cubes" are to "roots." It is signified by the final Ennead of Plato, insofar as it is also divided into nine regions, as explained by us elsewhere in our *Macrocosmic History*, but especially in the *Microcosmic History*. In Man, the body is compared to this; in the Tabernacle, the part subject to external changes and alterations; in the Temple of Solomon, the more vulgar and common part.

Here, however, we think it must especially be observed that on the <term>monochord</term> <note>a single-stringed musical instrument used for measuring intervals</note>, the quantity of any *Diapason* harmony always becomes more contracted and shorter as one descends. From this, we argue that the matter of any region is thicker and denser, and consequently requires less space for its existence in the world. Thus, we see in the nature of water that a handful of earth, when expanded by thinning into water, requires ten times as much space as it did before in its earthy state.

He argues that the density of matter increases as one moves from the divine center to the material periphery, mirrored by the shortening of musical strings.</summary>

# Robert Fludd’s Reply
<note>original: Replicatio Roberti Flud</note>

### Second Section
<note>original: Secund-</note>

As for those lower octaves <term>Diapason<gloss>the interval of an octave</gloss></term> which arise beyond the general ones, they indeed prove that composite bodies—in which this same Harmony sounds—are formed from the aforementioned principles. However, the first octave is assigned to **Man**, specifically between the numbers 300 and 400, as he contains the complete harmony of the world, counting from Unity (or God) descending to the lowest of the Elements, through whom all things in heaven and earth subsist. For here, Man designates God as the Alpha and Omega, or the small and large *Aleph* <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, used here to symbolize the beginning and the end, or the microcosm and macrocosm</note>, and is said to have union with God through God; he is the truest son of the world, just as the World is the offspring of God. The second octave from this is given to the composition of the other **animals**. The third to **vegetables**, and the last to **minerals**, as they are adjacent to the center of the whole. And so, all created things in the world, counting from Unity to the number one thousand, are explained most clearly on our <term>monochord<gloss>a single-stringed instrument used to demonstrate mathematical proportions of music</gloss></term> according to the intention of **Plato**: so that composite bodies are like cubes composed of cubes. For just as in the simple structure of the world there was a relationship of the root (or highest heaven) to the square (the ethereal), and the square to the cube (the elementary heaven): so in composite things, Animals relate to vegetables as a root to a square, and Vegetables to Minerals as a square to a cube. Furthermore, Angelic or super-celestial bodies relate to the stellar ones as a line to a surface, and these to sublunary bodies as a surface to a solid body. We conclude, therefore, that God, existing as One in Himself, is nevertheless everything that is, and encompasses all Harmony by His divine power. He measured the Harmony of His perfection against the highest heaven, according to whose pattern the middle heaven was formed on the second day, and finally the lowest heaven on the third day. Among composite things, animals look toward the first heaven, being of a more fiery condition; their head is **Man**, compared to the Seraphim angels who always stand before the face of God. Vegetables refer to the middle heaven, as they are more airy; and their head, namely **Wheat**, is rightly compared to the celestial Sun. And Minerals are compared to the lowest heaven, as they participate more in gross water; and their head, namely **Gold**, participates in the central Sun.

I could have published a huge Volume on this matter: but it is not my intention to bring boredom to the Reader in this little Treatise, but only to warn him honestly and candidly that my worldly Harmony is not so far removed from mathematical proportions as **Johannes** <note>Johannes Kepler</note>—deceived in this comparison—imagined: nor indeed is Robert so ignorant of Platonic, Pythagorean, and Proclean Harmony as he has attempted to trumpet to the world.

And now, because Johannes seems to some to judge Robert’s knowledge or science of the Harmony arising from the 5 regular solids <note>The Platonic Solids</note> lightly or flippantly—as if he had never, or not well, sown seeds in this harmonic field—I will show the Reader in a few words what I observed in my youth (contrary to Johannes' opinion) and how much profit I elicited from them. Regarding the regular bodies, we have noted five figures corresponding to the parts of the world—namely the heaven and the 4 elements (according to the opinion of the best Mathematicians). We recognized three of these as consisting of triangular surfaces, the fourth of squares, and finally the fifth of plane pentagons. For beyond these figures, no more are found by Mathematicians in Geometry, because no solid angle can equal or exceed four right plane angles: as is found more extensively in the 21st proposition of the 11th book of **Euclid’s** *Elements*.

Therefore, the triangles that meet to form a solid angle must be either 3, 4, or 5. For in an equilateral triangle, any angle contains 60 degrees; from which it follows that three angles of this condition constitute 180 degrees, which is less than 4 right angles <note>360 degrees</note>: and consequently, four angles of this kind produce 240 degrees, and five likewise produce 300 degrees. Beyond this, one cannot proceed with these angles, because six such angles produce 360, which is equivalent to four right angles, which by no means suits the nature of a solid angle.

From the meeting of these angles, three figures are produced, the first of which is the **Tetrahedron**, which is a pyramid with a plane of four triangular bases. And this is likened to the element of **Fire**. Its solid angle consists of three plane angles or surfaces of an equilateral triangle, as appears in the following.

From these things, therefore, it seems established that there are only five figures of regular bodies described by us, and no more. <note>Fludd is explaining why only five "Platonic Solids" can exist based on how their angles fit together in three-dimensional space.</note>

As for the Harmony or proportion of these figures to the parts of the world, the Platonists <note>Followers of Plato who believed the universe was built on mathematical principles.</note> determine it thus: namely, that the **Cube**, being the most stable and firm among all figures, corresponds to the **Earth**, which is fixed and immobile. Furthermore, they applied the **Pyramid** or **Tetrahedron** to the element of **Fire**, since fire is observed to tend upwards in such a shape. But truly, since the **Octahedron** closely approaches the composition and figure of a pyramid, they assigned to it the Element of **Air**, as it is closest to fire. Next, they adapted the **Icosahedron** (because it has many different sides and angles) to **Water**, which, due to the diversity of its waves, is changed into infinite forms like Proteus <note>A Greek sea-god capable of changing his shape.</note>. And finally, they compare and liken the **Dodecahedron** (since it allows for the inscription of all other figures within itself) to the **Heaven**, because heaven contains all things in its natural embrace. Furthermore, this figure is most excellently adapted to heaven in this way: just as the heaven is most conveniently divided into 360 parts or degrees, so also the Dodecahedron is observed to consist of just as many right angles. For this figure consists of twenty solid angles, and three pentagons meet to form them; in every pentagon, three equilateral triangles are found, so that in every solid angle there are nine equilateral triangles, which, multiplied by 20, make 180. In every triangle, three angles are equivalent to two right angles, so that in the Dodecahedron there are potentially contained 360 right angles.

# Reply of Robert Fludd

...[the sun] differs in every way from the other four elements in the substance of its essence, and consequently it has been explained that it is a **Fifth Element** <note>The "Quintessence" or ether, distinct from earth, water, air, and fire</note>. Fourthly, its composition most clearly reveals to the diligent Philosopher the equality of the Solar body’s makeup in light and spirit. And I confess that I received the discovery of the equal pyramids of Light and spirit from this; I established there that place of the middle sphere and of equality (in which the Sun is said to move by the Platonists) where the intersection is made between two pyramids arranged in opposite positions to one another. I affirmed that this intersection relates to the axis of either pyramid as 1 to 2—that is, in a **double proportion**. Just as if I were to divide a single **monochord** <note>A single-stringed musical instrument used to demonstrate mathematical proportions of intervals</note> through the middle, from its beginning to that middle intersection, the proportion to the whole will be as 1 to 2, which sounds the harmony of the **Diapason** <note>An octave</note>. 

From this kind of proportion thus arranged—namely, the whole and its two equal parts—I have organized my Harmony, both spiritual and material. Specifically, from the starting point on the monochord toward its midpoint, where the spiritual Diapason or the perfection of the Higher World sounds in the Sun; for it is in the Sun that God, or supreme perfection, has placed his Tabernacle. Then, from the midpoint to the other extremity, as if descending further down into the "multitude" <note>The material world of many things, as opposed to the divine Unity</note>, where another harmony of the Diapason sounds in the coarser and more material things of the world.

Therefore, as was said before, when we come to the demonstration of the solar body using the example of bread <note>Fludd often used the chemical analysis of wheat/bread as a microcosm for universal processes</note> by observing the 5 sensible substances of the elements, returning through the steps of the **material Diapason** from the endpoint (the multitude) toward the midpoint: I then judged that we must look with the eyes of the intellect into the steps of the **spiritual Diapason**. By this, we may approach the starting point—the Monad, God himself, and the ruler of Light—since undoubtedly sensible and corporeal things are made according to the patterns of insensible and spiritual things. And so, rising upward from the heavy mass, I yearned to explain the mysteries of the Soul and the Angels, and I did not despair of finally reaching the very fountain of uncreated Light by this path.

These things, I say, (Johannes) <note>Addressing Johannes Kepler</note> I have observed in the very center of nature’s womb. And although I may seem to "create" nothing in this, yet by your leave, what a creature is, how it is created, and from what worldly means it is constituted, will be very easy for a Philosopher to conceive through this inquiry of ours.

### In Defense against the 13th Analysis

Behold me here, that Robert <note>Robert Fludd</note> who has until now, as you say, hidden himself in the groves of his Hermes <note>A reference to Hermes Trismegistus and the Hermetic tradition</note>; I am stepping forth, I say, into the mathematical arena. You see him here, ready to defend his sayings and writings against all—whether it be John himself or any of his listeners—who cry out against my "unworthy work" or the smallest part of it, and ready to repel their insults.

First, therefore, you assert that I conclude, against the assertions of the Ancients, that musical consonances are incommensurable <term>Incommensurable: magnitudes that have no common measure, like the side and diagonal of a square</term>. You misunderstand me here, John; I do not thereby overturn the Geometric dogma concerning incommensurable proportions, but I only seem to suggest this: that in a certain Physical or even Mathematical respect, every interval—such as the tone, the Fourth <note>original: "Diatessaron"</note>, the Fifth <note>original: "Diapente"</note>, and the Octave <note>original: "Diapason"</note>—is divisible into its parts, since every measure of motion is through limits, just as those of number are through units and lines through points. Do I here refute any dogma of Geometry? Or if John imagines this is not true, he also denies that any proportion of the monochord <term>Monochord: a single-stringed instrument used to demonstrate mathematical musical ratios</term> is divisible into parts—that is, into tones and semitones—since the Fourth is composed of three intervals (namely, two tones and a semitone), the Fifth of four, and the Octave of the Fourth and Fifth combined. The Ancients indeed acknowledge this division into lengths or intervals, and even without their consensus, the visual and infallible observation of the monochord testifies to the same. Take the incommensurability of consonances in your own way, then; for me, it will suffice to have understood their commensurability in my way, with experience also supporting it.

Furthermore, you wrongly conclude that I said consonances are named by numbers; nevertheless, I do not blush to affirm that they are explained and distinguished from one another by proportional numbers by way of comparison. For example, the Octave stands in a double proportion as 1 to 2; the Fifth in a sesquialterate <note>3:2 ratio</note>, and so on. Similarly, we say there are four voices in a Fourth, five in a Fifth, and consequently eight in an Octave. Therefore, John is not yet strong enough in the mathematical arena, seeing as he thinks he can overcome Robert with empty words; nor indeed have I yet been reduced to such great straits that I must implore the assistance of any Adversary.

Besides, you make a great difference between "commensuration" and "connumeration," considering very little that every measure must be made through motion, and that motion itself is nothing other than a multitude of units, just as every measure is in a line, which is nothing other than a flow of points. Such, therefore, is the difference between commensuration and connumeration as exists between an arithmetic unit and a geometric point, which in effect are the same.

After this, it pleases you to argue with me about the nature of unity, which you say is a work of the mind, simple, and in the abstract. You seem to use words equivocally with us, John; for I understand unity in this or that sense—namely, as one real and concrete substance, by whose proportion such a sound is produced. For example, I take a certain flat piece of wood and distinguish it into nine equal parts with compasses adapted for this work. The first part, therefore, will be the dimension of a tone of the first monochord, since the dimension of this space or interval will correspond to the proportion of a tone; and by this kind of commensuration, the monochord is divided into other units, as was declared in the preceding pages. And such are my units: not in the abstract, but in the concrete, just as among merchants "one pound" or "one crown," etc.

But let us proceed further. I compare a Tone to the line of a Triangle, and I say (as you assert) that just as sides are multiplied in figures, so also tones are heaped together in consonances. Are these the "Cimmerian shadows" <note>A proverb for total darkness</note> of Robert which John seems to intimate? And yet he himself writes that the origin of that and all other consonances comes from the sectioning of the string of a circle made through figures. I respond that I applied tones to the lines of a triangle in a certain comparative respect, not as one who thought they originally arose from those same sides. Therefore, I warn the Reader to look diligently at the analysis of that context, so that he may draw the truth of this controversy from it.

Then afterward you cry out with an open mouth: "O Geometers, inquire accurately if there is anyone from your number who understands Robert’s preceding speech!" It is evident that the smaller intervals are simple. Indeed, has any Geometer dared to maintain with John that parts are not more simple than the whole composed of them? That...

# Reply of Robert Fludd

That a single sound is indeed simpler than the <term>Diatessaron</term> <note>The interval of a perfect fourth</note>—since that consists of two whole tones and a semitone—or the <term>Diapente</term> <note>A perfect fifth</note>, or the <term>Diapason</term> <note>An octave</note>, which is composed of the fourth and the fifth together, is a fact I believe is hidden from no one skilled in either philosophy or geometry.

In the following passage, I see Johann <note>Johannes Kepler</note> glowing with rage; therefore, until he experiences some cooling down, I shall impose silence upon myself. Meanwhile, I perceive him to be as far removed from his expected trophy of victory as I remain unshaken and secure against the fear of his words.

### On the Apology regarding Analysis XIV.

You say that you have not spent your labor in learning the mysteries of Nature from the fables of the Poets. I easily believe you, and your writings testify that this assertion of yours is no fable. But whether your mathematical demonstrations—hidden without truth beneath the fables of the Poets—are more certain or not: *This is the labor, this is the task* <note>A reference to Virgil’s Aeneid: "Hoc opus, hic labor est," referring to the difficulty of returning from the underworld</note> to describe.

### To Analysis XV.

This analysis pertains to your own Harmony; therefore, I will impose silence on myself in this place.

### To Analysis XVI.

Here I perceive Johann to be goaded by some sort of anger, by whose burning vapor I find myself so "cooked and re-cooked" (to use his own words) that—utterly neglecting the earthly kitchen of the Chemists—I believe he has long performed the office of a cook in that combustion and most full indignation of the sphere of Mars. I gladly refer the reader to the subject of my own Analysis regarding this matter.

### To Analysis XVII.

What your "equal or unequal units" of Geometry may be does not interest me, as I am content with my own units. Furthermore, even if I were to dispute further with you concerning formal numbers, it would be a vain business for me, as you are one who either does not know, or will not seem to know, either the formal proportions in nature or the reasoning of essential numbers. If you do not know, then there is no disputing against the ignorant; if you know but will not seem to know, contention with the perverse would be empty. 

But as soon as I begin to treat the essence of the thing—namely, the quantities of the mind (if there be any such dimensions)—you are immediately seized by a certain blast of malevolence and break out into insults against me. You also seem to falsely cite your Proclus <note>A 5th-century Neoplatonist philosopher whom Kepler admired</note>, as if he, joined together with you as his disciple, would cast my "maturations" and "perfections," as you call them, into <term>the great wave of the loud-roaring sea of generation</term> <note>original Greek: "μέγα κῦμα βαρυφλοίσβοιο γενέθλης." This refers to the chaotic world of material change.</note>. Since he lived long ago, I was nowhere to be found; and now that I exist among men, do you know where I might find him, Johann? And yet you are not ashamed to use his mouth, feigning that he judged falsely concerning Robert <note>Fludd refers to himself in the third person</note> who did not even exist in his time. 

But perhaps you dream that the spirit of Proclus is present with you now, who, like a Socratic Daemon <note>A guiding spirit or inner voice</note>, instructs you in the things you desire. But you are deceived, my Johann; your spirit is deceived regarding my maturations and perfections. A <term>Cacodæmon</term> <note>An evil spirit</note> is present with you and deceives you; therefore, beware meanwhile lest he cast your imaginary demonstrations—which feign real geometric circles and parts of the same within the indivisible mind—into <term>the great wave of the loud-roaring sea of generation</term>. 

I acknowledge your violence: for I see you are intensified with wrath because of my true opinion concerning formal unity. Indeed, you make everything said by me out to be enigmatic and parabolic, which in truth are as clear and transparent to a diligent observer as your own Sun. Therefore, I gladly commend what follows in this Analysis of mine to the judgment of a fair judge. For if I were to stir up everything proposed and opposed by Johann, it would perhaps be a weariness both to me and to the reader.

### To Analysis XVIII, XIX, XX.

In these parts of Johann’s Apology pertaining to my Harmony, I am so secure in my own Analytical Discourse, and so fortified by the aforementioned description of my <term>monochord</term> <note>A single-stringed instrument used to demonstrate mathematical musical ratios</note> and its application to the harmony of the world, that I hope it is clearly explained to the just reader that the things Johann seems to bring against it in his Apology are of no moment.

### To Analysis XXI.

Here, Johann, I could speak with you—and with a more certain effort and more apt reasoning than you did with me regarding Analysis 13—by saying that as long as you hid yourself in the groves of your Proclus, you maintained your reputation well enough. Now, after you come forth into the Chemical arena, you are immediately so manifest to all devoted to this profession that they will cry out against this part of your Apology as unworthy. And if I were to unshell the errors which you have brought forth in this brief mention of yours of the three Chemical principles, I would undoubtedly render you more and more stomach-sick against me, and I would stray too far from my goal. Therefore, it does not please me to uncover your fault in this place, for the sake of my own quiet and convenience.

### To Analysis XXII, XXIII, XXIV.

# In Defense of the *Analyses* to Chapter XXV.

...can do no harm. Therefore, let the Reader look upon those *Analyses* of mine, and through them he will perceive the sense and intention of my mind to be not at all discordant from the truth.

### To Chapter XXV.

That I have rightly applied my **Monochord** <note>A single-stringed instrument used here as a diagram for the harmony of the universe.</note> and its intervals (contrary to your opinion) to the degrees of the world or of nature in the world, has, I hope, been explained more than enough to the wise in the preceding sections. There, I also demonstrated that the location of the **semitone** <note>The smallest interval in Fludd's musical scale, representing a point of transition or compression.</note> belongs to that degree of the world where Light most abounds; for Light, on account of its subtle disposition, can be reduced and contracted into the smallest space. This is seen, for instance, in the Element of Fire, the sphere of the Sun, and the starry heaven—called *zoon* <note>original: $\zeta\omega\grave{o}\nu$</note>, that is, a **living animal**, because of its life-giving and lucid virtue—and finally the sphere of the **Seraphim**, which burns with the presence of God, the fountain of light and the presiding fire. 

You command me to name the terms of the **counterpoint**. I say, therefore, that they are **Alpha and Omega**, or the small *Aleph* and the great *Aleph* <note>The first and last letters of the Greek and Hebrew alphabets, symbolizing the beginning and end of all things in God.</note>, whose midpoint is that most perfect creature called the **Sun**. The Sun thunders a double **Diapason** <note>An octave; here a "double octave" spanning the spiritual and material realms.</note> to the unity of its creator, denoting here and there that it is the most perfect of the creatures of heaven. Among the composite things in the animal kingdom, **Man** corresponds to it; in the Vegetable, **Wheat**; in the mineral, **Gold**. 

Next, you ask for the difference of the musical genres in that mundane monochord. I respond, according to the Platonists and especially your **Proclus** <note>A 5th-century Neoplatonist philosopher whom Kepler admired.</note>, that the genre of such a melody is more **Diatonic**, and I have explained the reason for this in the preceding pages. Furthermore, by the power of this song, according to the opinion of the Royal Psalmist <note>King David.</note>, the heavens, stars, waters, rains, snows, thunders, winds, and all creatures are said to praise God the Creator and to resound His honors with the highest voice. Indeed, I say to you that a formula of this kind of song exists in the stars and Planets themselves, but in no other way than it exists in all other creatures, however small; though to us, on account of the smallness of the subject, this harmonic virtue does not shine forth so clearly. 

But you say that you are full of certainty in this matter: namely, that the seat of the semitone is marked by certain boundaries of nature, and that the difference of genres, the song, the terms of counterpoint, etc., are expressed in the very motions of the Planets. From this, you conclude that you have detected more of the divine works in your harmonies than I have in mine—I who (as you imagine) indulge in private conceptions of the world confirmed by no sense-perception. 

Truly, my dear **Johannes** <note>Johannes Kepler.</note>, if you had been changed from a Mathematician into a Prophet, I would perhaps grant you greater faith in this matter and hold myself suspect; I would dream that all my secrets and my virtue, whether great or small, had been revealed and detected by you. But from what has been said, I know that you remain a mere Mathematician, and like **Endymion** himself (the lover of the Moon), you have perhaps seen those things in a dream which in reality are not there. Why should we expect that Harmony from the motions of the seven Planets so far distant from us, when it is revealed without any hesitation to open eyes in a single, tiny subject right here among us? 

But you cry out, as is found on page 46: *“When at last, Robert, will you put an end to your arbitrary Nomenclature?”* I respond that all things are surrounded for you by the thick mists of ignorance; they seem "arbitrary" to you, and therefore, to explain mysteries—however true—to men disturbed by incredulity would be to **throw pearls before swine**. 

But I will now produce you as a witness against yourself. On page 13, you acknowledge **Tycho Brahe** (whom you confess to have succeeded in part of your work) as a faithful guardian of silence in **Hermetic matters** <note>Alchemy and mystical philosophy attributed to Hermes Trismegistus.</note>; but in mathematical matters, you make him open and clear to the common people, suggesting he devised no enigmas and handed down nothing in pictures. You say: *“He did not promise to teach celestial motions without quantities, nor did he disdain to help weaker minds.”* 

But what is the point of this story, Johannes? (Let me have you as my witness now). It is that this **Hermetic Art** is so noble in respect to that common **Mathematics** <note>original: *Mathesis*</note> that the latter should be handed over and published to the profane crowd, while the former should be hidden in the Sanctuary of God and His Nature. This is so that the "bread of the children" (to speak with Christ) might not be thrown to the dogs, nor pearls to swine. Brahe himself, refusing to commend or publish the mystery of nature to the profane, reserved it secretly for himself and the worthy; but he did not hesitate to promulgate the common mathematical art in his own way to the world and to men of every condition, as a thing not so worthy of concealment. 

Yet we call both of these "mathematical arts." But the one belonging to common mathematicians is **external** and, as you yourself confess, must be demonstrated by quantities and quantitative dimensions. The other, belonging to the Hermeticists, is **internal**; it is declared by formal demonstration and by the observation of essences in their progress toward perfection. It is not declared by quantitative dimensions, by which it is impossible for that divine form—moving in and from the heart of creatures—to be measured. For that form is infinite and cannot be grasped by any category, much less explained or terminated by mathematical dimensions. 

Therefore, just as the **Soul** is to be preferred to the body, so indeed is **Occult and Formal Mathematics** to be preferred to that which is manifest and measured by quantities—namely, by the line, surface, or body. And here I wish to warn the Reader that the **Seven Liberal Arts**, as they are commonly accepted, are only shadows and external images, as it were, of those seven which depend upon true Wisdom. Whence it is written: *“Wisdom has built her house upon seven columns.”* And elsewhere, the Holy Spirit of discipline is called the producer of true sciences. 

Therefore, all common sciences are nothing but copies of internal and occult ones, just as the body is cast in the image of the soul, and the spirit is said to lie hidden beneath the "letter that kills." Just as the body is usually measured by quantitative dimensions (surfaces, lines, and points), so also the Soul has its own dimensions, which are more essential and truly substantial. Being purely spiritual and very far removed from the nature of the body, they cannot be outlined or demonstrated by quantity, which deals with bodies or triple dimensions. And although Philosophers attempt to describe God and the Mind itself with "merchants' numbers" or geometric dimensions, they do this in an analogical and symbolic manner. Thus we describe God through the algorithmic figures 1, 2, 3. And others say that Jupiter is encompassed in seven hundred numbers...

# The Reply of Robert Fludd

...to be understood as exactly as possible. Some assign the Monad <note>The number one, representing unity or God</note> to God the Creator, the Dyad <note>The number two</note> to matter, and the Triad <note>The number three</note> to form: and under these external numbers they understand internal numbers, which are the true and formal numbers. These are the various visions of Light and darkness in the progress of nature, which are indeed nothing other than the degrees of nature's various progression toward "more-than-perfection." For the observation and modeling of these, wise men have indeed invented external Arts; and I will say this boldly: there has been no original invention in the world which did not have its beginning from this mirror of Justice, according to that saying: *Wisdom teaches all things.* But I shall proceed to the rest, and now turn the thread of my speech toward you.

You say *that you ought not now to wink in silence, but rather demonstrate your indignation, since you see me provoked by rivalry, and driven headlong by the desire for revenge for an injury (which you say I imagine for myself, because you gave God His due, having performed your duty by distinguishing between what is yours and what is mine)—driven to involve the very works of God in the longer-lasting darkness of ignorance, as much as lies within me, by the sprinkling and deformation of your work.* Here certainly you have fashioned a most beautiful prelude for yourself, and you mix threats with an argument of piety very well at the same time. If these things please you, I indeed congratulate your will and the pleasure you find in it. But in the meantime, I would have you know this: Robert neither cares nor gives a straw whether Johannes winks, or looks upon him with open eyes and a more terrible wrath: for I do not fear Johannes any more than I envy the divinity of his virtue. I do not envy the success of his virtue in mathematics—indeed, it is either not worthy of the mark of my envy, or it is far more eminent than it. I do not see what in your work is so admirable; let it suffice if what you have written is worthy of the praise of some. But as for your giving God His due, I think that was done by you as becomes a Christian man, and I advise you to continue in it. 

But as for your giving God His due in that you performed your duty by "distinguishing between what is yours and what is mine": here you are indeed imagining things, since formal things <note>Spiritual or essential principles</note> are received from God more than corporeal things, if you consider the dignity of our Harmonies and philosophical peace and concord, rather than litigation and quarrels (if you understand the controversy arising from the comparison). Therefore, in no way, as it seems to me, do you appear to give God His due in this work, for God is appeased by a sacrifice more formal than material. But as for the idea that I have become angry or resentful toward you because you did all those things, you are greatly deceived in this matter; I do not envy, I am not angry—on the contrary, I see and become more cheerful. Finally, God knows better than that I should involve the works of God in the longer-lasting darkness of ignorance by the "sprinkling and deformation" of your work, just because I liken the Harmony of Johannes to vain chimeras represented in the air. For as interior or formal things are nearest to God, while external and corporeal things are remote from God, so also (I speak now according to the sentiment of the Holy Scriptures) the body is likened to shadow and darkness—that appearing thing which is not—whence it is corruptible; but the soul and mind are the true image and likeness of God. So also I have said that the external doctrine of Johannes concerning the Harmony of the world stands as the letter to the spirit, and the body to the soul. 

Yet I cannot deny that his Harmony is laudable according to the respect of external and common Mathematics <term>Mathesis: the Greek-derived term for the discipline of learning, specifically mathematics and celestial mechanics</term>, and that his inventions or observations are by no means to be despised; but I say that in relation to formal and original Mathematics, it stands as the shadow of a thing to its reality—it is the shadow (I say) of truth, but not the truth itself. May Johannes forgive me if I speak now with the mouth of truth, and find myself far removed from flattery or recantation. But if you should inquire what this occult truth is, or what its description might be: by Hercules, even if I knew it and were well-versed in it, you yourself, Johannes, seem to warn me—by the example of Tycho Brahe—not to reveal it, since you declared him to be silent and quiet regarding the Hermetic mystery. But I would think this one thing sufficient: that I should attempt to strip it bare to its lucid garment by the most fit demonstrations (though in a somewhat metaphorical way) and indicate its degrees tending toward the goal of "more-than-perfection" in a symbolic manner, but one very close to the truth of nature itself.

Many other things you bring forward here are of no great weight, and to examine them all with precision would perhaps be too long and tedious for the readers; therefore I refer them to the examination of my *Analysis*.

-> ### To Analysis XXVI. <-

I shall leave you here to your triumph and the monuments of your praises. In the meantime, I wish only to admonish you of this: the Brothers of the Rosy Cross <note>The Rosicrucians, a mysterious secret society of the era</note>, whom you say I have praised and whom I acknowledge I still praise, are surely greater (as I believe) than those whom the reproaches of the malevolent can harm. I would wish you to be silent, therefore (as was said in the preceding parts), and I advise you to shut your hard mouth: for the blast of envy is moved against them like the spirit of the wind against rocks that cannot be moved by any violence. Thus little dogs are accustomed to bark from afar, but they do not know how to bite. Oh, how robust in body Johannes would be, how powerful and strong in spirit, if he could compel these Brothers—most eminent in Philosophy and Theosophy—to come forth into the crowd of men by his nod alone! Nay, indeed, they are obedient neither to you (my Johannes) nor to me, your Robert, nor to anyone; subject to God alone, they will undoubtedly not fail to come forth in public and reveal themselves to the world in their own time. Meanwhile, let both Johannes and Robert remain content with their own conceptions, and cease to bring reproaches and insults without cause or reason against men who are (as it seems to me) a thousand times more learned than themselves, lest this intemperance of their tongue finally bring them harm.

### Regarding Annals XXVII.

This part of John’s <note>Johannes Kepler</note> Defense does not seem to differ much from the character of his others; it is, I say, full of quarrels and deals with material of little importance compared to certain other matters, which is why I feel it should be omitted for the sake of brevity. But now at last, most desired Readers, let it be right and honorable for me to extend the thread of this brief discourse to you. Although the insolence of certain envious and malevolent men is not to be endured, I nevertheless ask you, most fair-minded men, to remain in the duty of your holy goodness through the common law of humanity. I implore you to weigh everything—both in my *Analytical Demonstration* and in Johannes Kepler’s *Defense*—on the scales of justice. And just as you will find that Robert <note>Robert Fludd, the author</note> has recanted nothing explained in his *Analysis* thus far, so also I hope you will perceive that he has endured John’s mocking words in many places of his *Defense* with enough lightness and patience. You will see that he has introduced nothing against John’s honor or the laws of his own *Harmony* <note>Refers to Fludd's work *Utriusque Cosmi Historia*, specifically the sections on world harmony</note> in this, his *Reply*. Rather, he has accomplished only that which especially becomes a Philosopher: namely, to support his own position against anyone’s insults or slanders to the best of his ability, and to defend his words—supported by the pillar of demonstration—like a strong soldier of Minerva <note>The Roman goddess of wisdom and strategic warfare</note>. Therefore, I gladly commend myself and my cause to your judgments, fortified by equity.

### Epilogue to the most distinguished Man and most celebrated in Mathematics, Johannes Kepler.

Although, most distinguished Sir, a most fit occasion presented itself for me to be roused to a just indignation by various passages in your *Defense*—indeed, to be quite angry and even to rage in proportion to your own vehemence and fervor—yet look and behold! Just as agile rivers are said to be turned back, unanimous winds to cease blowing, and the violence of lightning to be inhibited by a magical whisper, so also I hope you have found me until now imbued with better restraint and patience. I hope the bilious element <note>In the theory of the four humors, "bile" was associated with anger and fire</note> in my innermost heart, however mobile and rapid in itself, has been rendered mild and fixed enough, appeased by the spirit of your fairness and offered friendship. By this, I might indicate courteously to you and to the learned of the world that I have never pursued your glory in Mathematics or your proclaimed virtue in Philosophy (whatever its quality) with emulation or envy. Instead, I have attempted in the preceding pages to support what is mine as if on Atlantic shoulders <note>A reference to Atlas holding up the heavens</note>. Moreover, how disposed my mind is toward peace and literary friendship, how remote from the tangled contentions of disputants, and how inclined toward the contemplation of God and His Nature, I believe has been explained to you more than enough in the Letter attached to the beginning of this little Treatise.

Therefore, most honored Sir, I pray that you may be happy and prosperous in your mathematical studies, both private and public; but I persuade you to abstain from Robert’s Philosophy. In this way, we shall confirm and courteously untie a firm knot and bond of philosophical friendship between us for the future. Thus we shall break through and release the strong chains of our contention and quarreling. With the right hand of friendship thus extended between us in one mind, let us at last enter into a perpetual treaty and pact, if it pleases you, by which that holy spirit of discipline—the lover of concord and teacher of true knowledge—may lead us by his favorable breath into the way of truth. By his mediation, may we happily reach the longed-for goal of supreme wisdom.

->Farewell, the 9th day of December, in the year 1621.<-

->T H E  E N D.<-

### Regarding Analysis XXVIII.

Although you seem to have been very busy in other matters, nevertheless here you—and your associates who assisted in that work and who later set their hands to the same task—could not appear to have done enough. This is especially true regarding the fact that you began to discuss a certain agreement not only in the preface to the 8th and 9th Centuries <note>The "Magdeburg Centuries" was the first great Protestant history of the Christian Church, organized by centuries.</note>, but also here in the same matter, concerning what you call the "discovery of the Antichrist," about which you have woven together many passages from many authors. How coldly and how poorly this has been presented by you, and how unsuccessfully it fights against you, is easy to judge from the many passages you cite. For if anyone were to weigh that matter—which you show with such great effort and exertion—on the scales of truth, they would see how weak are the pillars upon which it rests, and how feeble is the proof of that which you so greatly commend. 

Let us therefore get to the point. First, then, is what is said concerning the Pope, as if he were that Antichrist whom the Prophets foretold and the Apostles marked out as coming. How foreign this is to the truth, and how little it agrees with the Sacred Scriptures, has been demonstrated at length above in the preceding books. Nor is there any need here for us to repeat what was explained there in detail. For both in the preface of that same Century and in the very context of the history, the same thing has been said quite often. Therefore, let us now draw closer to the things brought forward by you in this place, so that we may see how correctly and how much to the point are the things you allege in support of that same opinion.

### Epilogue of Book III to Matthias Flacius Illyricus & Johannes Wigand) <note>Flacius and Wigand were the primary architects of the Magdeburg Centuries.</note>

->The Construction<- <note>original: "Κατασκευή" (Kataskeuē). A rhetorical term referring to the confirmation or positive proof of an argument.</note>

Just as we acknowledge Christ to be our sole savior and the savior of the whole Church, so also we do not deny that the Church, the bride of that same Christ, is one, and that she spreads herself throughout the whole world, and is distinguished by the same marks of the Word of God and the Sacraments. But just as not everyone who says, "Lord, Lord," shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, so not every society that professes Christ is the true Church of Christ. For many have come in His name, saying, "I am Christ," and have led many astray. There are also many false prophets who come in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves. These people take upon themselves the persona and face of the true Church so that they may more easily deceive the unwary. 

Wherefore we must be vigilant and diligently investigate which is that true Church, which alone preaches the word of God purely and administers the Sacraments rightly. For the true Church is not established in words, but in power and truth. You, however, who have undertaken this contest against us, labor greatly in this: to sell your society as the true Church of Christ. But if we examine your doctrine and your way of living by the rule of truth, you will easily see how far you are from the true Church of Christ. For the true Church does not rejoice in contentions, discords, and schisms, with which your entire society swarms. For we are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another. But where there is dissension and strife, there is not the Spirit of God, but the spirit of error. You, however, disagree not only with us, but even among yourselves to such an extent that scarcely two of you agree on the same opinion. Why, therefore, do you boast of your society as the true Church of Christ?

<summary>The author critiques the Protestant identification of the Pope as the Antichrist and challenges the legitimacy of the Lutheran church by highlighting its internal divisions and schisms. He argues that the true Church must possess unity and the Holy Spirit, which he claims his opponents lack.</summary>
